title: 'Equal work, equal pay
body: 'I guess Lim Guan Eng, the former finance minister and now adviser to the Democratic Action Party (DAP), has a soft spot for employers. His call to exclude migrant workers from the minimum wage and the paltry 2% contribution to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) repeats a position he took in early August 2025. Even then, labour groups criticised it. Since he has chosen to lend his voice to employers, be they micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) or others, it is apt to remind him of three fundamental issues. All people are equal Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution treats everyone as equal and entitles them to equal protection. The courts have noted this. In Ahmad Zahri bin Mirza Abdul Hamid v AIMS Cyberjaya Sdn Bhd, the Federal Court took cognisance of Article 10 of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention 143 of 1975. It said Malaysia should promote and guarantee equality of opportunity and treatment between migrant workers and nationals. Referring to the convention, the court said: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Based on the above reasons we take the view that all workers should be treated with fairness, dignity and equality without distinction whether they are locals or foreigners. This is also consonant with Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution which essentially provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law. his judgment alone should put to rest the flawed argument that Malaysia should adopt discriminatory standards against migrant workers to protect employers. Legislative protection Section 69F of the Employment Act 1955 empowers the director general of labour to inquire into and decide any dispute over discrimination in employment. An employer who fails to comply with the director general’s order faces, on conviction, a fine of up to RM50,000. For a continuing offence, there is a further fine of up to RM1,000 for each day it continues. Where an employer has signed a collective agreement with a trade union, section 17(1)(b) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 makes it binding once the Industrial Court takes cognisance of it. It covers all worker employed in the undertaking, now or later. Industrial Court and other judicial decisions have affirmed that such agreements apply to migrant workers. International standards From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, one fact stands unchallenged – there is no room for discriminatory employment practices against migrant workers. Full stop! No reasonable person would dispute that people doing the same work must receive the same pay. The right to equal pay for equal work should never be compromised. Doing so would destroy the foundation of equality, good conscience and fair treatment of workers, whether migrant or local. Working people need greater protection against the ever-rising cost of living, low and stagnant wages and inadequate retirement savings in the EPF. They do not need more protection for employers. Seeking such protection for employers is like asking workers to wallow in a vicious low-wage ecosystem so that employers can profit from staying in business. To even entertain the thought that businesses should be protected by treating migrant workers as second-class employees is heartless, an affront to human dignity and devoid of any sense of justice. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Oil and gas, Sorento Capital Bhd, Bermaz Auto Bhd, UMedic Group Bhd
body: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Oil and gas, Sorento Capital Bhd, Bermaz Auto Bhd, UMedic Group Bhd This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 Oil and gas OVERWEIGHT HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Brent has returned above US$100 per barrel as risks rise across Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi’s East-West Pipeline, while Middle East supply disruptions have widened the global oil deficit. China crude imports are also recovering, adding further upside risk to prices. We now expect Brent at US$95-US$100 per barrel towards end-2026 and raise our 2026 assumption to US$90 per barrel from US$80 per barrel. While we retain “buy” calls on most names, we remain selective and favour companies with earnings drivers that can sustain beyond near-term Brent volatility. We advocate positioning for our 2027 thesis of a recovery in Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s (PETRONAS) upstream capital expenditure (capex) alongside rising regional energy-security investments. We believe the sector remains supported by a recovery in offshore support vessel-related names such as Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd (KL:DAYANG), Keyfield International Bhd (KL:KEYFIELD) and Perdana Petroleum Bhd (KL:PERDANA), while improving oil and gas services and equipment order flows and longer-term demand for storage, pipelines and broader energy infrastructure should continue to support Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) and Wasco Bhd (KL:WASCO). Dialog remains our top pick. We expect Dialog’s earnings to remain well supported in FY27-FY28 by growth across its three key segments. Upstream will be supported by the new Cendramas production sharing contract and Baram Junior Cluster (both commencing from 2QFY27), which are expected to shift the upstream earnings mix higher to 30% to 40%. Meanwhile, Dialog’s downstream earnings visibility remains well supported by several ongoing engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning projects. PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd’s (KL:PCHEM) (PetChem) share price has risen around 25% after we upgraded it to “buy” in our end-June report. We are seeing early signs of stabilisation in key product prices, while elevated Brent prices could support further improvement in overall average selling prices in 4QFY26. We expect utilisation rates to improve with minimal turnaround activities at Methanol 2 for 60 days and Fertiliser Sabah for 10 days in 3QFY26, while no scheduled plant turnaround is expected in 4QFY26. PetChem remains attractive, with recovery of urea prices in 2HFY27 as seasonal planting demand returns, and potential divestment of its Pengerang Petrochemical Co Sdn Bhd stake, which could remove significant earnings drag and reduce the group’s foreign exchange (forex) exposure. We view Dayang as a key beneficiary of a potential PETRONAS upstream capex recovery in 2027. Dayang delivered a stronger performance in 2024, when PETRONAS’ upstream spending was relatively elevated at around RM21.5 billion across 2023-2024, while upstream capex remained subdued at only RM9 billion in 1HFY26. Sorento Capital Bhd Target price: 77 sen BUY TA SECURITIES (SEPT 14): Sorento Capital Bhd’s (KL:SORENTO) FY26 gross profit margin reached 45.2%, the highest in the company’s history, despite challenging market conditions arising from the US-Iran war. Management attributes the margin expansion to a reduction in original equipment manufacturing cost in China late last year, which contributed to a stronger 47% gross profit margin in 4QFY26. According to management, global brass prices rose by 50% following the onset of the US-Iran war, leading to higher production cost for bathroom and kitchen taps. However, prices of ceramic bathroom products have been undergoing price cutting. As China’s exports of ceramic products to the Middle East has been disrupted by the war, these products have been redirected to Asian markets, creating downward price pressure. As such, management is confident of sustaining its gross profit margin above 40% for FY27. As far as project sales are concerned, the group has seen an uptick in orders for its Sorento-series sanitary ware. It order book has increased to RM150 million from RM120 million, and we expect the company to secure new orders of RM80 million each in FY27 and FY28. Bermaz Auto Bhd Target price: RM1.35 BUY MAYBANK INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Bermaz Auto Bhd’s (KL:BAUTO) recovery trajectory continues to outperform market expectations, and we see further upside should the momentum sustain. Near-term margins should improve with stronger support from XPeng China, while Mazda volumes remain resilient. Key considerations include completely built-up (CBU) supply and evolving earnings mix as completely knocked-down (CKD) ramps up. Mazda CBU volume now contributes about two-thirds of sales, which we expect to sustain over the next few quarters until the all-new CX-5 CKD is launched in mid-2027. We expect 5,000 CBU units by year-end, while forex hedging should support CBU margins in FY27. Overall, BAuto’s outlook is underpinned by new Mazda and XPeng model launches, supporting its FY27 sales target of 16,000 units (+23% y-o-y, ex-Kia sales in FY26). Associate earnings are also improving, with Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd returning to profitability and further supported by potential additional assembly contracts. Mazda Malaysia should benefit from CKD expansion, with export volume for the new CX-5 from 2027 (targeting 7,000 units per annum) providing an additional volume boost, while Kia exposure is now minimal. Near-term earnings visibility remains solid, combined with an attractive dividend yield of more than 9%. UMedic Group Bhd Target price: 43 sen BUY MBSB RESEARCH (SEPT 15): The RM47 billion allocated under Budget 2026 and the 13th Malaysia Plan promise of RM40 billion until 2030 continue to support UMedic Group Bhd (KL:UMC). We believe with the upcoming Budget 2027 — which is expected to continue prioritising citizens’ welfare — UMC is positioned for sustained long-term growth by leveraging key industry tailwinds, including hospital overcrowding, medical tourism and an ageing population projected to reach 21% by 2044. To capitalise on these trends, UMC is expected to further expand into ambulatory care by growing its ambulance fleet, scaling its integrated learning and community health centres, and diversifying into the laboratory market and specialised verticals via its Akiteck and Ateria subsidiaries. Additionally, UMC is reinforcing its manufacturing foundation by acquiring three acres of industrial land, expanding clean room capacity and adopting advanced automation to meet rising domestic and global demand across its product portfolio. By incorporating UMC’s FY26 results into our valuation, we revised FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts upwards by 2%. We like UMC for its stable distribution business, paired with its high-margin proprietary manufacturing operations. UMC’s key drivers remain the government’s fiscal support and long-term demographic tailwinds in terms of care demand and medical tourism. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Brokers Digest: Local Equities - Oil and gas, Sorento Capital Bhd, Bermaz Auto Bhd, UMedic Group Bhd
body:
'

This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026

Oil and gas

OVERWEIGHT

HONG LEONG INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Brent has returned above US$100 per barrel as risks rise across Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi’s East-West Pipeline, while Middle East supply disruptions have widened the global oil deficit. China crude imports are also recovering, adding further upside risk to prices. We now expect Brent at US$95-US$100 per barrel towards end-2026 and raise our 2026 assumption to US$90 per barrel from US$80 per barrel.

While we retain “buy” calls on most names, we remain selective and favour companies with earnings drivers that can sustain beyond near-term Brent volatility.

We advocate positioning for our 2027 thesis of a recovery in Petroliam Nasional Bhd’s (PETRONAS) upstream capital expenditure (capex) alongside rising regional energy-security investments. We believe the sector remains supported by a recovery in offshore support vessel-related names such as Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd (KL:DAYANG), Keyfield International Bhd (KL:KEYFIELD) and Perdana Petroleum Bhd (KL:PERDANA), while improving oil and gas services and equipment order flows and longer-term demand for storage, pipelines and broader energy infrastructure should continue to support Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) and Wasco Bhd (KL:WASCO).

Dialog remains our top pick. We expect Dialog’s earnings to remain well supported in FY27-FY28 by growth across its three key segments. Upstream will be supported by the new Cendramas production sharing contract and Baram Junior Cluster (both commencing from 2QFY27), which are expected to shift the upstream earnings mix higher to 30% to 40%. Meanwhile, Dialog’s downstream earnings visibility remains well supported by several ongoing engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning projects.

PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd’s (KL:PCHEM) (PetChem) share price has risen around 25% after we upgraded it to “buy” in our end-June report. We are seeing early signs of stabilisation in key product prices, while elevated Brent prices could support further improvement in overall average selling prices in 4QFY26. We expect utilisation rates to improve with minimal turnaround activities at Methanol 2 for 60 days and Fertiliser Sabah for 10 days in 3QFY26, while no scheduled plant turnaround is expected in 4QFY26. PetChem remains attractive, with recovery of urea prices in 2HFY27 as seasonal planting demand returns, and potential divestment of its Pengerang Petrochemical Co Sdn Bhd stake, which could remove significant earnings drag and reduce the group’s foreign exchange (forex) exposure.

We view Dayang as a key beneficiary of a potential PETRONAS upstream capex recovery in 2027. Dayang delivered a stronger performance in 2024, when PETRONAS’ upstream spending was relatively elevated at around RM21.5 billion across 2023-2024, while upstream capex remained subdued at only RM9 billion in 1HFY26.

Sorento Capital Bhd

Target price: 77 sen BUY

TA SECURITIES (SEPT 14): Sorento Capital Bhd’s (KL:SORENTO) FY26 gross profit margin reached 45.2%, the highest in the company’s history, despite challenging market conditions arising from the US-Iran war. Management attributes the margin expansion to a reduction in original equipment manufacturing cost in China late last year, which contributed to a stronger 47% gross profit margin in 4QFY26.

According to management, global brass prices rose by 50% following the onset of the US-Iran war, leading to higher production cost for bathroom and kitchen taps. However, prices of ceramic bathroom products have been undergoing price cutting. As China’s exports of ceramic products to the Middle East has been disrupted by the war, these products have been redirected to Asian markets, creating downward price pressure. As such, management is confident of sustaining its gross profit margin above 40% for FY27.

As far as project sales are concerned, the group has seen an uptick in orders for its Sorento-series sanitary ware. It order book has increased to RM150 million from RM120 million, and we expect the company to secure new orders of RM80 million each in FY27 and FY28.

Bermaz Auto Bhd

Target price: RM1.35 BUY

MAYBANK INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Bermaz Auto Bhd’s (KL:BAUTO) recovery trajectory continues to outperform market expectations, and we see further upside should the momentum sustain.

Near-term margins should improve with stronger support from XPeng China, while Mazda volumes remain resilient. Key considerations include completely built-up (CBU) supply and evolving earnings mix as completely knocked-down (CKD) ramps up.

Mazda CBU volume now contributes about two-thirds of sales, which we expect to sustain over the next few quarters until the all-new CX-5 CKD is launched in mid-2027. We expect 5,000 CBU units by year-end, while forex hedging should support CBU margins in FY27.

Overall, BAuto’s outlook is underpinned by new Mazda and XPeng model launches, supporting its FY27 sales target of 16,000 units (+23% y-o-y, ex-Kia sales in FY26). Associate earnings are also improving, with Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd returning to profitability and further supported by potential additional assembly contracts. Mazda Malaysia should benefit from CKD expansion, with export volume for the new CX-5 from 2027 (targeting 7,000 units per annum) providing an additional volume boost, while Kia exposure is now minimal. Near-term earnings visibility remains solid, combined with an attractive dividend yield of more than 9%.

UMedic Group Bhd

Target price: 43 sen BUY

MBSB RESEARCH (SEPT 15): The RM47 billion allocated under Budget 2026 and the 13th Malaysia Plan promise of RM40 billion until 2030 continue to support UMedic Group Bhd (KL:UMC).

We believe with the upcoming Budget 2027 — which is expected to continue prioritising citizens’ welfare — UMC is positioned for sustained long-term growth by leveraging key industry tailwinds, including hospital overcrowding, medical tourism and an ageing population projected to reach 21% by 2044.

To capitalise on these trends, UMC is expected to further expand into ambulatory care by growing its ambulance fleet, scaling its integrated learning and community health centres, and diversifying into the laboratory market and specialised verticals via its Akiteck and Ateria subsidiaries.

Additionally, UMC is reinforcing its manufacturing foundation by acquiring three acres of industrial land, expanding clean room capacity and adopting advanced automation to meet rising domestic and global demand across its product portfolio.

By incorporating UMC’s FY26 results into our valuation, we revised FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts upwards by 2%. We like UMC for its stable distribution business, paired with its high-margin proprietary manufacturing operations. UMC’s key drivers remain the government’s fiscal support and long-term demographic tailwinds in terms of care demand and medical tourism.

As far as project sales are concerned, the group has seen an uptick in orders for its Sorento-series sanitary ware. It order book has increased to RM150 million from RM120 million, and we expect the company to secure new orders of RM80 million each in FY27 and FY28.

Bermaz Auto Bhd

Target price: RM1.35 BUY

MAYBANK INVESTMENT BANK RESEARCH (SEPT 14): Bermaz Auto Bhd’s (KL:BAUTO) recovery trajectory continues to outperform market expectations, and we see further upside should the momentum sustain.

Near-term margins should improve with stronger support from XPeng China, while Mazda volumes remain resilient. Key considerations include completely built-up (CBU) supply and evolving earnings mix as completely knocked-down (CKD) ramps up.

Mazda CBU volume now contributes about two-thirds of sales, which we expect to sustain over the next few quarters until the all-new CX-5 CKD is launched in mid-2027. We expect 5,000 CBU units by year-end, while forex hedging should support CBU margins in FY27.

Overall, BAuto’s outlook is underpinned by new Mazda and XPeng model launches, supporting its FY27 sales target of 16,000 units (+23% y-o-y, ex-Kia sales in FY26). Associate earnings are also improving, with Inokom Corp Sdn Bhd returning to profitability and further supported by potential additional assembly contracts. Mazda Malaysia should benefit from CKD expansion, with export volume for the new CX-5 from 2027 (targeting 7,000 units per annum) providing an additional volume boost, while Kia exposure is now minimal. Near-term earnings visibility remains solid, combined with an attractive dividend yield of more than 9%.

UMedic Group Bhd

Target price: 43 sen BUY

MBSB RESEARCH (SEPT 15): The RM47 billion allocated under Budget 2026 and the 13th Malaysia Plan promise of RM40 billion until 2030 continue to support UMedic Group Bhd (KL:UMC).

We believe with the upcoming Budget 2027 — which is expected to continue prioritising citizens’ welfare — UMC is positioned for sustained long-term growth by leveraging key industry tailwinds, including hospital overcrowding, medical tourism and an ageing population projected to reach 21% by 2044.

To capitalise on these trends, UMC is expected to further expand into ambulatory care by growing its ambulance fleet, scaling its integrated learning and community health centres, and diversifying into the laboratory market and specialised verticals via its Akiteck and Ateria subsidiaries.

Additionally, UMC is reinforcing its manufacturing foundation by acquiring three acres of industrial land, expanding clean room capacity and adopting advanced automation to meet rising domestic and global demand across its product portfolio.

By incorporating UMC’s FY26 results into our valuation, we revised FY27-FY28 earnings forecasts upwards by 2%. We like UMC for its stable distribution business, paired with its high-margin proprietary manufacturing operations. UMC’s key drivers remain the government’s fiscal support and long-term demographic tailwinds in terms of care demand and medical tourism.

title: 'Building on a legacy of Art and Community: Maybank returns for the third edition of CASB 2026 | Maybank
body: 'Since inception, CASB has attracted over 10,000 visitors and generated more than RM460,000 for artisans and cultural practitioners, championing cultural expression and economic empowerment Celebrating the people at the heart of CASB 2026 - Participating artisans proudly receive their Certificates of Appreciation in recognition of their talent, dedication and contribution to Malaysia’s creative and cultural landscape. Joining them are (L-R middle row, standing): Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank & Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation (in a blue, short-sleeve batik shirt); Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in purple kebaya); Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme (in black and floral kebaya); Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) (in pink kurung batik); Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in a black and floral ensemble) & Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt). Maybank Foundation, the social impact arm of Maybank Group, celebrates the return of the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026, reaffirming its continued commitment to preserving Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creating meaningful opportunities for local artisans and cultural practitioners. Now in its third edition, CASB 2026 is being held from 20 August to 20 September 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Kuala Lumpur, bringing together artisans, cultural practitioners, performers and creative communities in a month-long celebration of Malaysia’s diverse cultural identity. The showcase is held in conjunction with the nation’s Hari Kebangsaan and Hari Malaysia celebrations. The official the launch of CASB 2026 - Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer and Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property took centre stage, officiating the month-long celebration of Malaysia’s rich cultural heritage and creative talent at the Cultural Art Showcase and Bazaar (CASB) 2026. They are joined by (from L-R): En. Ahmad Hilmi Hashim, Head of Technical Management and Governance, Group Sustainability Maybank (in brown batik shirt); Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir; member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation; Mr. Surin Segar A/L Gnanasegaram, Head, Group Tax Maybank and Chief Financial Officer of Maybank Foundation; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN); Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik); Datuk R. Karunakaran, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation & Rizqan Helmi Mohd Ariff, Head, Asset Management, Sime Darby Property (in a dark purple batik shirt). Visitors to CASB 2026 can experience cultural performances featuring traditional music, dance, theatre and contemporary interpretations of Malaysia’s diverse cultural heritage, Artisanal workshops led by participating practitioners, Artisan showcases and booths featuring a diverse range of Malaysian craftsmanship, including weaving, beading, batik, wau-making, indigenous art and other traditional crafts and Local F&B offerings, showcasing regional flavours that provide a platform for homegrown culinary talents. The 2026 programme features cultural groups such as Sanggar Seni Malaysia, Nyala Dance Theatre, Persatuan Kompang Cahaya Murni, Iron Gang Puppet Theatre, KRATE Creative Space and Sri Dasmesh Pipe Band. It also features two rotating groups of artisans and artisanal brands throughout the showcase, allowing more creative entrepreneurs to participate while refreshing the visitor experience, exposure and market access across the month. The launch came alive with a vibrant Borneo-fusion performance by Nyala Dance Theatre, inspired by the Ngajat of Sarawak and Sumazau of Sabah. Bringing movement, rhythm and tradition to the stage. The performance set the tone for CASB 2026, a lively celebration of the diverse cultural expressions that makes Malaysia unique. The Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, which marks the halfway point of the showcase was graced by Datin Paduka Marina Mahathir and Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, Members of the Maybank Foundation Board of Trustees; Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer; Dr Yasmin Binti Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property; Puan Putri Shahda Azza Binti Megat Burhainuddin, Deputy Director, Policy and Research Division (Policy), Jabatan Kebudayaan dan Kesenian Negara (JKKN) and Puan Anita Ahmad, CEO, Yayasan MySDG. From celebration to participation - Dr. Yasmin Rasyid, General Manager, Sustainability, Sime Darby Property (in white dress) gets hands-on with traditional weaving, guided by Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin of Tanoti from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, one of the 40 artisans featured at CASB 2026. Against a vibrant backdrop of woven textiles, the moment reflects CASB’s role in bringing heritage closer to the community while creating meaningful platforms for artisans to share their knowledge and craft. Speaking at the Artisan Appreciation Ceremony, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer, said, “CASB reflects what it means to impact society positively by creating opportunities for communities, celebrating our shared heritage and bringing people together through culture and creativity. Initiatives such as CASB demonstrate how cultural programmes can create impact beyond the arts by supporting livelihoods, strengthening community connections and providing greater visibility for the people who keep Malaysia’s traditions alive.” Connecting Artisans, Partners and Community - Engaging with the people at the heart of CASB 2026, Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer (in a blue, long-sleeve batik shirt), Datuk Karunakaran A/L Ramasamy, member of Board of Trustees, Maybank Foundation (in a purple batik shirt), along with Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation (in light blue kebaya batik), engaging with Puan Josefine Midong anak Jubin, a fellow weaver from the Maybank Women Eco-Weavers (MWEW) programme, showcasing her artisanal products from Tanoti. Also pictured is Miss Elvina, Tanoti’s programme coordinator (in black shirt, with glasses). The exchange reflects the spirit of CASB, connecting artisans, partners and audiences to create greater visibility and opportunities for Malaysia’s creative communities. “More importantly, CASB represents something much bigger than a cultural showcase or bazaar. It is aligned with Maybank Group’s ROAR30 aspiration, particularly our commitment to Impacting Society Positively (ISP), which seeks to ensure that Maybank’s growth translates into meaningful and lasting benefits for the communities we serve. Under this pillar alone, the Group has mobilised more than RM30 million towards Social Empowerment initiatives and positively impacted over 466,000 individuals. As part of this journey, Maybank remains firmly on track towards its aspiration of empowering three million lives by 2030. CASB is part of this broader commitment, demonstrating how arts and culture can inspire learning, strengthen community bonds and create opportunities for greater social inclusion, and contribute meaningfully to this shared goal,” added Datuk Shahril. The showcase continues to be supported through Maybank Foundation’s partnership with Kakiseni, while Maybank MAE serves as the digital payment platform for the initiative. CASB 2026 is also made possible through collaboration with Sime Darby Property as the strategic venue partner, which hosts the showcase at KLGCC Mall, its third wholly-owned mall. Building on the momentum of its first two editions, CASB has welcomed more than 10,000 visitors and generated over RM460,000 in cumulative income for featured artisans and cultural practitioners since its inception in 2024. This year, CASB continues to strengthen its role as a platform for cultural expression and economic empowerment, providing artisans with opportunities to reach new audiences, showcase their craft and connect with potential customers. Turning skills into opportunities - En. Azmi bin Taha, representing the seven participants from the Reach Independence & Sustainable Entrepreneurship (R.I.S.E.) programme, received a Certificate of Appreciation from Datuk Shahril Azuar Jimin, Maybank Group Chief Sustainability Officer witnessed by Fadzlin Ariffin, Head of Community Empowerment, Maybank Foundation. The recognition underscores CASB’s commitment to creating inclusive platforms where talent from various skillsets can be showcased, valued and translated into meaningful economic opportunities. As a key programme under the Balai Seni Art Series (BSAS), CASB is part of Maybank Foundation’s longstanding commitment to making arts and culture more accessible to communities, creating platforms for artists and cultural practitioners to thrive. Since the inception of BSAS in 1988, the programme has supported over 9,300 artists and beneficiaries through exhibitions and cultural initiatives. CASB builds on this legacy by bringing art, culture and community directly into spaces where people live, work and gather. The continued growth of CASB reflects Maybank Foundation’s broader commitment to catalysing positive and sustainable change, particularly through its three key pillars of Community Empowerment, Empowering Education and Environmental Diversity. By creating platforms for cultural participation and economic opportunity. The public is welcomed to visit CASB 2026 at KLGCC Mall, Level 1, Main Atrium, Kuala Lumpur till 20 September 2026. Showcases and activities will commence from 10.00am – 10.00pm daily. Visit www.maybankfoundation.com for more information on CASB 2026.

title: 'Maybank Commits RM10 Billion to Technology and Growth Under ROAR30
body: 'Maybank is committing RM10 billion in investment through 2030 as it expands its ROAR30 strategy across technology, regional banking, payments, wealth management and sustainability. The banking group plans to spend RM1.5 billion on technology during FY2026 alone. Its investment programme will cover core system modernisation, artificial intelligence, cloud adoption, resilience improvements and stronger risk and compliance capabilities. Maybank expects those investments to help it increase productivity while providing more personalised services across its regional operations. The programme comes as the group reported RM5.17 billion in net profit for the first half of FY2026. Technology Becomes Central to Maybank ROAR30 Maybank is positioning technology as an important enabler of its next phase of regional growth. The group intends to modernise core banking infrastructure while expanding the use of AI and cloud technologies. It is also investing in systems designed to improve operational resilience and strengthen compliance capabilities. President and Group CEO Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli said technology was already helping Maybank deepen customer engagement, scale its businesses and improve productivity. The ROAR30 strategy will place greater emphasis on businesses where Maybank believes it can establish or extend regional leadership. These include Islamic finance, wealth management, transaction banking, payments, corporate and investment banking, and SMEs. Wealth and Investment Banking Fees Rise Several of Maybank’s targeted growth areas recorded stronger performance during the first half of FY2026. Wealth fee income increased 49.6% year-on-year to RM925.4 million. Corporate and investment banking fee income rose 15.6% to RM1.51 billion. Cross-border payments volume increased 15.8% to RM465.2 billion. Maybank also continued expanding its Islamic financial services business. Islamic corporate and investment banking income increased 3.9% year-on-year to RM896.8 million. Takaful net written contribution rose 10.2% to RM1.72 billion. The figures support Maybank’s strategy of increasing revenue from fee-based and regional businesses alongside traditional lending. Maybank Declares 31 Sen Interim Dividend Shareholders will also receive a higher first interim dividend following Maybank’s resilient first-half performance. The board declared 31 sen per share, compared with 30 sen per share for the first half of FY2025. Five sen per share will be electable under Maybank’s Dividend Reinvestment Plan. The dividend represents an estimated total payout of RM3.75 billion. That amount is equivalent to approximately 72.5% of Maybank’s first-half net profit. The payout highlights the group’s attempt to balance shareholder returns with continued investment in technology, growth and balance-sheet resilience. Maybank maintained a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 14.92% as of June 2026. Its total capital ratio stood at 18.68%. Sustainable Finance Reaches RM31.81 Billion Sustainability remains another major component of Maybank’s longer-term strategy. The group mobilised RM31.81 billion in sustainable finance as of June 2026. It also mobilised RM12.86 billion in social finance and RM30.96 million through social empowerment initiatives during the same period. Maybank said these programmes benefited more than 268,000 people. More than 238,000 people were reached through financial inclusion initiatives, while approximately 30,000 participated in financial literacy programmes. Maybank has refreshed its long-term sustainable finance ambition to RM300 billion by 2030. It is also targeting RM24 billion in annual social finance, with programmes intended to economically empower three million people. Maybank Cuts Operational Carbon Emissions The group reported a 58.9% reduction in carbon emissions against its baseline. That places Maybank close to its 2026 target of a 61% reduction. Its longer-term goals include achieving carbon neutrality by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2050. Maybank also reported continued progress across six priority sectors within its financed emissions portfolio. Physical emissions intensity has declined 23% in power, 13% in palm oil and 10% in commercial real estate since the baseline year. Automotive emissions intensity declined 8%. Steel and aluminium remained below their respective emissions glidepaths. Maybank said those improvements reflected portfolio management, client engagement and increased exposure to lower-emitting assets. ROAR30 Targets Regional Leadership Maybank Chairman Tan Sri Dato’ Sri Ir. Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa said the group’s capital and liquidity positions provide a strong foundation for navigating changing market conditions. He also emphasised the group’s commitment to responsible growth, shareholder value and sustainability. Khairussaleh said Maybank would continue sharpening its focus on businesses where it can lead while strengthening capabilities across the region. The strategy combines several priorities that traditionally compete for capital. Maybank intends to continue paying meaningful shareholder dividends while investing heavily in technology and pursuing regional growth. At the same time, the group is increasing sustainable finance commitments and working towards progressively tighter emissions targets. Its RM10 billion investment programme therefore represents more than a technology upgrade. It forms part of a broader attempt to position Maybank for the next phase of Southeast Asian banking, where digital services, regional scale, fee income and sustainability are becoming increasingly important sources of competitive advantage.

title: 'Asteel lantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Razarudin sebagai pengerusi selepas Clifford Hii ambil alih syarikat
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 7 Okt - Asteel Group Berhad melantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas dan pemegang saham pengawal Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong sebagai timbalan pengerusi eksekutif, berkuat kuasa pada Selasa. Perubahan lembaga pengarah itu menyusuli penutupan tawaran pengambilalihan mandatori pada 5 Oktober yang menyaksikan syarikat pelaburan Clifford, Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd, memegang 53.08% kepentingan dalam pengeluar keluli berkenaan. Clifford memperoleh kawalan pada Ogos menerusi pembelian 270 juta saham Asteel oleh Hii Capital, mewakili kepentingan 52.94%, dengan bayaran tunai RM20.25 juta atau 7.5 sen sesaham. Pembelian itu mencetuskan tawaran mandatori bagi baki saham pada harga yang sama. Jawatan Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai ditukar daripada pengerusi eksekutif kepada pengarah eksekutif merangkap pengerusi emeritus, menurut makluman syarikat kepada Bursa Malaysia. Asteel turut melantik Esther Teh Oun Pheng dan Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng sebagai pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas. Pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas Christopher Hii Lu Ming serta pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee dan Wee Hiang Chyn meletakkan jawatan atas sebab peribadi. Pengalaman dalam keselamatan dan perkhidmatan kewangan Razarudin, 63, mempunyai pengalaman lebih empat dekad dalam keselamatan negara dan penguatkuasaan undang-undang. Ketua Polis Negara ke-14 itu bersara pada Jun 2025 dan turut berkhidmat sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas Advancecon Holdings Berhad. Clifford, 43, mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam sektor pendidikan, hartanah dan teknologi kewangan. Bekas pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas HCK Capital Group Berhad itu mengasaskan Gambit Group Sdn Bhd dan pernah memegang jawatan pengurusan kanan serta menganggotai lembaga pengarah, dengan pengalaman meliputi strategi korporat, pembangunan perniagaan, urus niaga, pelaburan, tadbir urus dan pengurusan projek. Beliau ialah anak kepada bekas wartawan yang beralih menjadi ahli perniagaan, Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, pengasas dan pengerusi eksekutif pemaju hartanah HCK Capital serta pengarah urusan kumpulan dan pemegang saham utama kumpulan pendidikan swasta SEG International. Esther Teh, 47, mengetuai audit dalaman dan pengurusan risiko di Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd serta merupakan pengarah bebas OMS Energy Technologies Inc yang disenaraikan di Nasdaq. Beliau mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam audit, pengurusan risiko, perundingan, pelaksanaan perkhidmatan bersama, operasi dan kawalan kewangan. Jawatan terdahulunya termasuk ketua audit dalaman dan pematuhan kumpulan di Silverlake Axis Ltd, ketua pengurusan risiko dan jaminan bagi bahagian digital kumpulan di Petroliam Nasional Bhd serta pengurus kanan perundingan pengurusan di Accenture. Dr Lor, 62, mempunyai pengalaman lebih 35 tahun dalam perkhidmatan kewangan dan berkhidmat sebagai penasihat kepada Global ESG Leadership Organization serta Kementerian Ekonomi dan Kewangan Kemboja. Beliau pernah menjadi ketua pegawai eksekutif (CEO) dan pengarah eksekutif Canadia Bank PLC di Kemboja, CEO kumpulan EON Bank Bhd, pengarah bebas Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, pengarah rumusan perbankan di Hewlett Packard Enterprise, ketua perbankan pengguna kumpulan di RHB Bank Bhd serta pengarah urusan perbankan pengguna di DBS Bank Ltd. - DagangNews.com

title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
body: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'RHB to charge merchants up to 0.60% on DuitNow QR payments
body: 'RHB Bank is revising the fees it charges merchants for accepting DuitNow QR payments, with the new rates taking effect on 26 October 2026. The bank informed its business customers of the change in a notice dated 3 October. Under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), merchants will be charged 0.35% of the transaction value when a customer pays using a current or savings account, or an e-wallet. Payments funded by a credit card, on the other hand, will come with a higher MDR of 0.60%. To put that into perspective, a merchant receiving a RM100 payment through DuitNow QR from a customer’s bank account or e-wallet will see RM0.35 deducted. If the same amount is paid using a credit card, the deduction goes up to RM0.60. The new rates apply to DuitNow QR payments processed across RHB’s card terminal devices, DuitNow QR Sound Box and Sound Box+, as well as Reflex Mobile and Tent Cards. Consumers will not be affected by the change, as the fee is charged directly to merchants rather than end-users. RHB stated that the revision aligns with the evolving payment landscape and ongoing servicing requirements, ensuring it can continue providing consistent service quality. Merchants seeking further details on the new rates are advised to contact their RHB home branch. Read more of our articles below! The post RHB to charge merchants up to 0.60% on DuitNow QR payments appeared first on Price Shop Malaysia.

title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. “While stronger wealth, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, brokerage and loan-related fees should provide some cushion, these are unlikely to fully offset the trading-income shortfall.” The research firm said the impact on 3Q26 should be viewed more as a foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book. The Treasury has been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. The bank’s return on equity (ROE) target range of 10.8% to 11% appears within reach despite the NOII headwinds, but only towards the lower end as the burden increasingly shifts to core operations, with loan growth of 6% and management having reset cost growth to less than or equal to 1%, providing scope for better operating leverage. “Credit cost is tracking around the lower end of its 13 basis points (bps) to 14bps guidance, with management comfortable at 13bps and hopeful of achieving 12bps should recoveries materialise,” HLIB Research said. Wealth sales have also risen 35% year-on-year as of June 2026, while bancassurance/takaful, brokerage and loan-related fees continue to gain traction. Taken together, these levers should partially cushion the NOII drag, although the path towards the upper end of management’s ROE ambition has become more challenging amid elevated bond yields. Capital management remains an important medium-term catalyst, with management targeting more clarity on its capital/dividend policy by 1Q27. The priority would be to ensure operations and targeted growth trajectory can be adequately funded while sustaining Common Equity Tier 1 around current levels. Should these growth requirements be met without absorbing the existing surplus, the excess capital could potentially be fully returned to shareholders. The existing dividend remains respectable, with projected dividend yield of 6.5% for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027.

title: 'Banking Sectors Funding Conundrum
body: 'The local banking sector remains fundamentally sound, supported by robust business lending, comfortable liquidity and healthy asset quality, but a widening gap between loan and deposit growth is beginning to put pressure on funding costs and could slow the recovery in net interest margins, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest banking sector review, CIMB maintained its Overweight stance, saying system loan growth accelerated to 5.7% year-on-year in August 2026, while deposit growth lagged at 4.2%.  The divergence reflects increasingly strong corporate credit demand as Malaysia’s investment cycle gathers momentum. Business loans expanded 6.8% year-on-year, compared with 5% growth in household lending, while business lending including development financial institutions grew 8%.  CIMB said the pattern suggests credit growth is increasingly being driven by investment, corporate expansion and working-capital requirements rather than household leverage.  Business loan applications rose 5.5% year-on-year in August while approvals jumped 30.9%, contrasting with declines of 5.1% and 10.4%, respectively, for household applications and approvals.  Funding Costs Becoming The Key Constraint  While credit demand remains healthy, CIMB said banks are increasingly contending with more expensive funding.  The ex-foreign currency loan-to-deposit ratio stood at 100.8%, while wider interbank money-market spreads and recent tightening in system liquidity are keeping marginal funding costs elevated.  This could limit the extent to which banks can rebuild net interest margins (NIMs) despite continued loan growth.  The composition of deposit growth also points to pressure beneath the surface. Islamic Tawarruq fixed deposits and wholesale deposits are becoming more important funding sources, but CIMB estimates these can cost 130 to 170 basis points more than conventional fixed deposits.  CASA deposits remained a positive factor, rising 7.9% year-on-year, helped by a 12% increase in business CASA. However, conventional fixed deposits declined 1.4%.  Liquidity, Asset Quality Still Healthy  Despite tighter funding conditions, CIMB said the banking system is not facing an immediate liquidity problem.  The system liquidity coverage ratio remained comfortable at 145.9% in August, although it eased from 148.7% in July. Islamic banks recorded a lower average of about 134%, a trend CIMB said warrants monitoring rather than representing an immediate concern.  Asset quality also remains broadly sound.  The gross impaired loan ratio edged up to 1.44% from 1.43%, while household and business impaired loan ratios remained relatively low at 1.11% and 1.92%, respectively. Loan-loss reserve coverage stood at 125.1%.  CIMB nevertheless observed rising impaired balances in selected segments including passenger vehicles, wholesale trade, retail and services, and transportation and storage.  It does not yet view those increases as evidence of broad deterioration, citing stable employment, contained inflation and ongoing investment as supportive of repayment conditions.  Capital Strength Offers Buffer  CIMB said Malaysian banks remain well positioned to withstand a more volatile global rate environment, backed by a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 14.1%, adequate liquidity, strong reserves and earnings visibility.  The research house also expects stronger capital positions, Basel 3.1-related benefits and balance-sheet optimisation to create greater scope for dividends and other capital returns.  For 2026, 2027 and 2028, CIMB forecasts domestic loan growth of 5.1%, 5.2% and 5.2%, respectively, while sector NIM is expected to remain broadly flat at around 2%. It projects banking sector core net profit growth of 2.9% in 2026, 5.5% in 2027 and 5.3% in 2028.  Its preferred banking stocks are Public Bank, RHB Bank and Hong Leong Bank, citing their capital return potential, dividend prospects and earnings resilience.  Overall, CIMB sees a banking system that remains healthy and profitable, but where the challenge is shifting from credit demand to funding economics: loan growth is strong, asset quality remains manageable and capital is ample, but competition for deposits and greater reliance on higher-cost funding are increasingly constraining margin expansion.

title: 'Bursa dibuka tinggi pada awal dagangan hari ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah da KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia meningkat semula untuk dibuka tinggi pada Jumaat didorong oleh hasil Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang rendah dan sentimen Rizab Persekutuan (Fed) yang berhati-hati memberikan kelegaan kepada pelabur. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.49 mata atau 0.09 peratus kepada 1,631.85 daripada 1,630.36 semasa ditutup pada Khamis. Indeks dibuka tinggi 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 239 berbanding 137 manakala 270 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,127 tidak diniagakan dan 24 yang lain digantung. title: 'AirAsia Indonesia Mulls Share Sales, Liability Restructuring
body: '(Oct 1): PT AirAsia Indonesia is considering restructuring some liabilities and selling shares as the low-cost carrier seeks to repair a balance sheet that has kept its shares suspended since July. The airline is mulling converting trade payables and lease liabilities owed to controlling entities or shareholders into perpetual instruments that would effectively count as equity, according to a Wednesday filing. It is also considering a rights issue or a private placement. The recapitalisation options are unfolding against a much bigger funding squeeze at parent AirAsia Group Bhd (KL:AAGB), which had a record US$4.1 billion (RM16.75 billion) of debt at the end of June and is seeking about US$1 billion in refinancing. Last month, the group’s co-founder and adviser Tan Sri Tony Fernandes said fresh capital would be injected into the Indonesian and Philippine operations, with new shareholders expected to join affiliates. Shares of AirAsia Indonesia have been suspended since early July because its latest financial statements showed negative equity. It has not chosen a path yet and is still assessing funding needs, market conditions and the feasibility of each option with shareholders and outside advisers, it said in the filing. The measures under review are intended to strengthen its capital structure that should also help it comply with exchange requirements, it said. title: 'Petros, Höegh Evi Tie Up to Develop Sarawak’s First LNG Regasification Terminal in Kuching
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) has partnered Norway-based maritime energy infrastructure group Höegh Evi to jointly develop Sarawak’s first liquefied natural gas (LNG) regasification facility in Kuching, with first gas targeted by end-2029. The two parties have signed a joint development agreement to develop, own and operate the Kuching LNG Terminal, which will form part of the Kuching Low-Carbon Hub (KLCH), Petros said in a statement on Thursday. The terminal will use a floating storage and regasification unit, essentially a vessel that receives LNG and converts it back into natural gas before it is supplied onshore. It will also include mooring facilities, subsea and onshore pipelines, as well as receiving facilities on land. Petros said the terminal would provide gas to Kuching and surrounding areas to meet growing energy demand and strengthen Sarawak’s energy security. The gas supply would initially support power generation while helping lay the groundwork for wider industrial development under the KLCH. “The Kuching LNG Terminal is a strategic investment to drive Sarawak’s next phase of economic development,” said Petros group chief executive officer Datuk Janin Girie. He said the project would provide the infrastructure needed to bring natural gas to Kuching while helping attract higher-value investments and new industries. Petros said the terminal could also support services such as small-scale LNG distribution, truck loading, bunkering, storage and reload activities. This would give the facility flexibility to supply gas beyond Kuching to other parts of Sarawak as demand grows. The KLCH was launched in November 2024 under the Sarawak Gas Roadmap. Petros had in May 2025 signed a strategic cooperation agreement with China Jiangsu International Economic and Technical Cooperation Group Ltd to support the hub’s master planning. Petros is Sarawak’s sole gas aggregator, with responsibilities covering gas procurement, distribution, import, regasification and supply. title: 'Bursa opens marginally higher on easing US Treasury yields, Fed tone
body: 'At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.49 points, or 0.09%, to 1,631.85 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 239 to 137, with 270 counters unchanged, 2,127 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover stood at 173.94 million shares worth RM95.98 million. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the latest decline had pushed the index back into oversold territory, which could have encouraged bargain hunting following the sharp correction. “Against the reported foreign-selling backdrop, however, we believe any initial rebound may remain modest. “Nonetheless, the weakness presents opportunities to selectively accumulate fundamentally sound stocks, particularly among established banks, utilities and semiconductor counters,” he noted. Thong said a more sustainable recovery would require stronger participation from heavyweight counters and an improvement in market breadth. Thus, he expects cautious trading today within the 1,625-1,640 range. Among the heavyweights, Maybank was flat at RM9.95, while Public Bank and CIMB fell one sen to RM4.66 and RM7.68, respectively. Tenaga Nasional added four sen to RM12.94 and IHH Healthcare rose one sen to RM7.71. In active trade, Zetrix AI, Jaks Resources and Genetec all remained unchanged at 16.5 sen, 18 sen and 32.5 sen, respectively. V.S Industry gained one sen to 28 sen, but Kinergy Advancement lost half a sen to 39.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries advanced 58 sen to RM41.70, Hengyuan Refining inched up 19 sen to RM3.83, Petronas Chemicals perked up 15 sen to RM4.28, while UWC and MI Technovation both firmed 10 sen to RM7.20 and RM5.36, respectively. MISC led the decliners, falling 14 sen to RM7.54, while LPI Capital, Hong Leong Industries, MNRB and RHB Bank shed four sen each to RM12.80, RM16.10, RM2.78 and RM7.43, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index ticked up 75.93 points to 17,434.91, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 17.18 points to 12,160.71, and the FBM Top 100 Index widened 21.58 points to 11,954.73. The FBM Emas Shariah Index accumulated 34.76 points to 12,047.77, while the FBM ACE Index improved 18.61 points to 5,501.58. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index grew 1.10 points to 178.83, while the Energy Index gained 9.45 points to 844.46. The Financial Services Index fell 26.33 points to 19,034.58, while the Plantation Index ticked up 2.75 points to 9,029.32.

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 25 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI ended 0.2% lower to 1,672.3 points on Thursday, as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters. Telecommunications & Media (-2.0%), Technology (-1.8%) and Consumer Product and Services (-0.4%) led sectoral losses, with Press Metal Aluminium (-1.7%), YTL Power International (-1.9%) and Petronas Gas (-0.6%) among the key laggards. Market breadth, however, was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 677 to 436, and 542 counters unchanged. Asian markets ended mostly lower on Thursday as sentiment turned more cautious amid rising sovereign bond yields, despite positive developments surrounding US-China trade relations and US-Iran ceasefire talks. Japan’s 10- year JGB yield rose to nearly 3.1%, its highest level since 1996, while US Treasury yields also edged higher during Asian trading. The Hang Seng Index fell 0.3% to 24,761.1, the TAIEX declined 0.3% to 48,024.6, and the Shanghai Composite dropped 1.2% to 3,888.4. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.8% to 65,514.0. In China, notable laggards included Kweichow Moutai (-1.14%), Foxconn Industrial Internet (-3.14%), and China Life Insurance (-3.03%). South Korea’s KOSPI was closed for the Chuseok holiday. European stocks closed lower on Thursday as soaring energy prices lifted benchmark rates. The Euro STOXX 50 fell 0.4% to 6,273, and the STOXX Europe 600 fell 0.5% to 637. Fuel and natural gas prices surged amid signs that the naval blockade in the Persian Gulf could be prolonged, in addition to signals from the US presidential administration that diesel exports could be banned. Sovereign yields extended their surge this week, weighing on the corporate sector. Infineon sank 4.2% and Siemens Energy dropped 1.7%, tracking the negative AI trade in North America. US stock indices closed mixed on Thursday amid renewed volatility in bond yields and oil prices. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq CI ended broadly flat, while the Dow Jones fell 162 points. The 10-year US Treasury yield briefly rose above 5.15% before easing to around 5.1%, remaining near its highest level since 2007, while the 30-year yield climbed to its highest level since 2004. Rising oil prices and heightened US-Iran tensions contributed to the increase in borrowing costs. However, sentiment was supported by reports that US and Iranian negotiators were moving closer to an agreement to restore tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Among AI hyperscalers, Alphabet gained 1.3% and Meta rose 4.5% following positive feedback on its AI agent software and latest gadget releases, while Microsoft declined 0.5% and Amazon was broadly flat. US: Global bond selloff rolls on, US 30-year yield at highest since 2004 US long-dated Treasury yields rose to their highest in more than 20 years on Thursday, extending a global selloff that has accelerated on worries that high energy costs, resilient economic growth and increased government spending will keep inflation elevated Bond markets worldwide have been under pressure for months, sending yields to multi-decade highs as the Iran war raised energy prices and as investors fret about government spending. Rising yields mean bond prices are falling. (Reuters) US: Oil Halts Rally on Talks of a Phased Deal Crude oil steadied near $94 per barrel on Friday, pausing its recent rally amid reports that the US and Iran were considering a phased deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift a US blockade on Iranian ports. Efforts to reach a breakthrough were reportedly underway on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Qatari officials mediating the talks. (Reuters) US: To either reform IEA on climate issues or leave group, energy secretary says The US might consider leaving the International Energy Agency (IEA) if there is no alignment on climate issues, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Wednesday. "We are either going to reform the IEA or we will leave the IEA. My strong preference is that we reform it," Wright said at an event in New York hosted by The Wall Street Journal. The Paris-based IEA has provided research and data to industrialised governments for more than half a century to help guide policy around energy security, supply and investment. (Reuters) US: New home sales jump to eight-month high in August Sales of new US single-family homes surged to an eight-month high in August as buyers took advantage of price cuts and other incentives, but rising mortgage rates stemming from the war in the Middle East remain a drag on the housing market. New home sales increased 6.4% to a seasonally adjusted annualised rate of 684,000 units last month, the highest level since December 2025, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Thursday. (Reuters) US: Current account deficit widens sharply in second quarter The US current account deficit widened sharply in the second quarter amid a surge in imports of goods, government data showed on Thursday. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said the current account deficit, which measures the flow of goods, services and investments into and out of the country, increased US$33.4 billion (RM136.1 billion), or 15.7%, to US$246.0 billion last quarter. (Reuters) US: Gold slips as rising oil prices, Treasury yields dent appeal Gold prices eased on Thursday, pressured by rising oil prices and US Treasury yields, while expectations the US Federal Reserve (Fed) could tighten monetary policy further weighed on sentiment. Spot gold fell 0.6% to US$4,261.55 (RM17,409.71) per ounce, by 1206 GMT, having hit its lowest since Sept 17. US gold futures for December delivery eased 0.5% to US$4,296.30. (Reuters) US: Weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows as labour market regains footing The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to a firming labour market. Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended Sept 19, the Labor Department said on Thursday. 'The FBM KLCI ended 0.2% lower to 1,672.3 points on Thursday, as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters. Telecommunications & Media (-2.0%), Technology (-1.8%) and Consumer Product and Services (-0.4%) led sectoral losses, with Press Metal Aluminium (-1.7%), YTL Power International (-1.9%) and Petronas Gas (-0.6%) among the key laggards. Market breadth, however, was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 677 to 436, and 542 counters unchanged. Asian markets ended mostly lower on Thursday as sentiment turned more cautious amid rising sovereign bond yields, despite positive developments surrounding US-China trade relations and US-Iran ceasefire talks. Japan’s 10- year JGB yield rose to nearly 3.1%, its highest level since 1996, while US Treasury yields also edged higher during Asian trading. The Hang Seng Index fell 0.3% to 24,761.1, the TAIEX declined 0.3% to 48,024.6, and the Shanghai Composite dropped 1.2% to 3,888.4. In contrast, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.8% to 65,514.0. European stocks closed lower on Thursday as soaring energy prices lifted benchmark rates. The Euro STOXX 50 fell 0.4% to 6,273, and the STOXX Europe 600 fell 0.5% to 637. body: '（吉隆坡1日讯）债券收益率上升，拖累银行股普遍下跌，而马银行（Malayan Banking Bhd）（KL: MAYBANK ）股价更是近9个月来首次跌破10令吉。  收益率上升通常对银行不利，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，导致更大的账面亏损，这会侵蚀资本，并迫使银行在出售时确认损失。银行还需要提高利率以吸引存款人，从而导致融资成本上升。  艾芬黄氏投资银行今日在报告中指出，这将影响银行的短期非利息收入以及资本比率。  马来西亚资产规模最大的银行马银行连续第三天下跌，收盘下跌0.4%，报9.95令吉。联昌国际集团（CIMB Group Holdings Bhd）（KL: CIMB ）和丰隆银行（Hong Leong Bank Bhd）（KL: HLBANK ）各跌逾1%。  大马交易所金融服务指数下跌至10个月以来的最低水平。  本月初，美联储3年来首次加息，导致马来西亚10年期基准国债收益率一度高达4.18%，之后有所回落。  越来越多经济学家预计，国家银行将在11月举行的年度最后一次货币政策评估会议上调高隔夜政策利率（OPR）。  艾芬黄氏指出，收益率上升通常会导致企业债券收益率上升，这也会与银行及其他企业的融资决策挂钩，进而影响银行的手续费收入。  根据该研究机构的分析，马银行和安联银行（Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd）（KL: ABMB ）拥有最长的债券期限——即债券以现金流形式偿还本金所需的时间，同时也衡量了其对利率变动的敏感性。  与此同时，大众银行（Public Bank Bhd）（KL: PBBANK ）和丰隆银行的期限最短。就资本充足率而言，马银行、兴业银行（RHB Bank Bhd）（KL: RHBBANK ）和联昌国际集团的降幅可能最大，而大众银行和丰隆银行的降幅最小，因为它们的投资组合期限较短。

title: 'Insider Moves: Cuscapi Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, Excel Force MSC Bhd, Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd, MyMBN Bhd, RHB Bank Bhd, Gamuda Bhd
body: 'Insider Moves: Cuscapi Bhd, Zetrix AI Bhd, Excel Force MSC Bhd, Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd, MyMBN Bhd, RHB Bank Bhd, Gamuda Bhd This article first appeared in Capital, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 Notable filings During the week of Sept 7 to 11, notable changes in shareholding at Bursa Malaysia-listed companies included those at IT company Cuscapi Bhd (KL:CUSCAPI), where Datin Seri Lee Lan Moi and Jessie Lim Me Xian ceased to be substantial shareholders. According to Bursa filings, Lee hived off 67.5 million shares or a 7.14% stake in an off-market deal, while Lim sold 58.5 million shares via a separate off-market transaction. Both transactions took place on Sept 3. Separately, Cuscapi’s largest shareholder, Wong Thean Soon, saw his stake cut from 28.07% to 13.43%, as the share price tumbled from nine sen at end-August to close at six sen last Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM56.7 million. Filings showed that the bulk of the shares Wong disposed of had been pledged, and were likely forced sold as the share price fell. There have also been a slew of boardroom changes at Cuscapi. Following the transactions, Tan Boon Seng emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi after acquiring 100.33 million shares or a 10.62% stake on Sept 11. Wong had emerged as a substantial shareholder of Cuscapi in March 2022, with a 7.73% stake. Apart from his shares in Cuscapi, Wong’s shares in his flagship Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) and Excel Force MSC Bhd (KL:EFORCE) were also likely forced sold after their market prices plummeted. During the week in review, Wong’s direct stake in Zetrix AI was slashed by 571.36 million shares to 525.27 million shares, or a 6.67% stake, while his indirect interest held via Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd was substantially reduced after 632.05 million shares were sold, bringing the firm’s stake in Zetrix AI down to 5.56% or 438.17 million shares. Wong now has 12.23% equity interest in Zetrix AI, in stark contrast to the 29.25% he held in early April this year. Meanwhile, his stake in Excel Force was reduced to 14.01% or 85.42 million shares after 104.21 million shares were disposed of. At Formosa Prosonic Industries Bhd (KL:FPI), privately held OS Capital Sdn Bhd emerged as a substantial shareholder of the audio products manufacturer after acquiring 53.45 million shares or 20.01% equity interest on Sept 10. OS Capital is the vehicle of Gan Chun Hui, who also has a direct stake of 0.36% or 955,500 shares in Formosa Prosonic. The shares acquired by Gan could have come from Taiwanese managing director Shih Chao Yuan, who sold 66.78 million shares or a 24.88% stake on Sept 10 and ceased to be a substantial shareholder. Another substantial shareholder of Formosa Prosonic, Singaporean Wu Swee Ngor, sold 44.18 million shares or a 16.46% stake in the company. Formosa Prosonic’s share price closed at RM1.08 last Thursday, giving the company a market value of RM288.5 million. Meanwhile, privately held Gentle Rainbow Sdn Bhd — the private vehicle of Fong Hew Chung and Hew Hong Thee — ceased to be a substantial shareholder of edible bird’s nest processor MyMBN Bhd (KL:MBN) after disposing of 28.8 million shares or a 7.46% stake in the company during the week in review. While Fong ceased to be a substantial shareholder, Hew still has 129.6 million shares, or 33.58% equity interest, in MyMBN. Hew is the mother of Lavernt Chen Vun Wo, executive director and CEO of MyMBN. In early September, MyMBN chairman Liw Chong Liong sold 43.2 million shares or an 11.19% stake in the company, halving his shareholding. It is not clear who acquired those shares. From eight sen at end-June, MyMBN’s share price had doubled to 17 sen in the first week of September, before tapering off and finishing at 14.5 sen last Thursday, valuing the company at RM56 million. Notable movements Bursa filings during the week in review showed the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) accumulating shares in RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK). The provident fund acquired another 31.46 million shares to bring its equity interest to 35.47% or 1.55 billion shares. At end-June, it held 1.51 billion shares or a 34.54% stake in RHB. RHB’s share price closed at a multi-year high of RM8.88 on Aug 10, having gained 11% since early April. However, it had since eased 12.05% from its high to close at RM7.81 last Thursday, giving the banking group a market capitalisation of RM34.09 billion. Bourse filings also showed that EPF continued to accumulate Gamuda Bhd’s (KL:GAMUDA) shares and emerged as a net buyer during the week in review, having mopped up 20.92 million shares to bring its equity interest to 21.93% or 1.32 billion shares. In early July, the provident fund held a 20.83% stake or 1.24 billion shares in the construction giant. Gamuda’s share price closed at RM4.74 last Thursday, having gained about 17% since early July. This gave the group a market capitalisation of RM28.64 billion. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. OS Capital is the vehicle of Gan Chun Hui, who also has a direct stake of 0.36% or 955,500 shares in Formosa Prosonic. The shares acquired by Gan could have come from Taiwanese managing director Shih Chao Yuan, who sold 66.78 million shares or a 24.88% stake on Sept 10 and ceased to be a substantial shareholder. Another substantial shareholder of Formosa Prosonic, Singaporean Wu Swee Ngor, sold 44.18 million shares or a 16.46% stake in the company. Formosa Prosonic’s share price closed at RM1.08 last Thursday, giving the company a market value of RM288.5 million. Meanwhile, privately held Gentle Rainbow Sdn Bhd — the private vehicle of Fong Hew Chung and Hew Hong Thee — ceased to be a substantial shareholder of edible bird’s nest processor MyMBN Bhd (KL:MBN) after disposing of 28.8 million shares or a 7.46% stake in the company during the week in review. While Fong ceased to be a substantial shareholder, Hew still has 129.6 million shares, or 33.58% equity interest, in MyMBN. Hew is the mother of Lavernt Chen Vun Wo, executive director and CEO of MyMBN. In early September, MyMBN chairman Liw Chong Liong sold 43.2 million shares or an 11.19% stake in the company, halving his shareholding. It is not clear who acquired those shares. From eight sen at end-June, MyMBN’s share price had doubled to 17 sen in the first week of September, before tapering off and finishing at 14.5 sen last Thursday, valuing the company at RM56 million. Notable movements Bursa filings during the week in review showed the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) accumulating shares in RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK). The provident fund acquired another 31.46 million shares to bring its equity interest to 35.47% or 1.55 billion shares. At end-June, it held 1.51 billion shares or a 34.54% stake in RHB. RHB’s share price closed at a multi-year high of RM8.88 on Aug 10, having gained 11% since early April. However, it had since eased 12.05% from its high to close at RM7.81 last Thursday, giving the banking group a market capitalisation of RM34.09 billion. Bourse filings also showed that EPF continued to accumulate Gamuda Bhd’s (KL:GAMUDA) shares and emerged as a net buyer during the week in review, having mopped up 20.92 million shares to bring its equity interest to 21.93% or 1.32 billion shares. In early July, the provident fund held a 20.83% stake or 1.24 billion shares in the construction giant. Gamuda’s share price closed at RM4.74 last Thursday, having gained about 17% since early July. title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.

Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.

Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.

He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.

Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.

In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.

According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.

On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.

The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.

The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.

The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application.

The appellate court then ordered RHB to produce its Minimum Due Diligence guidelines governing foreign exchange transactions to the company within 45 days.

Maritime Network further alleged that the bank’s vague allegations placed it in a position of uncertainty, depriving it of any opportunity to defend itself.

The company asserted that this conduct amounted to an abuse of power that prejudiced its rights.

It also claimed that the bank’s conduct demonstrated an intention to oppress rather than protect its legitimate banking interests.
