title: 'RHB Makeover Flexi Loan for Home Renovation
body: '21st September 2026 - 3 min read You can now include renovation costs in your home loan with the Makeover Flexi Loan, from RHB Bank and The Makeover Guys. It covers up to 90% of the property’s value, plus up to 30% more for renovation and related costs, for a total of up to 120%. With a standard home loan, you can usually borrow up to 90% of the property’s value, and the renovation is paid for separately with savings, a personal loan, or a renovation loan. The extra 30% can go towards your renovation, legal and documentation fees, and Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA). MRTA is insurance that pays off the rest of your home loan if you pass away or become totally and permanently disabled. If you take an Islamic home loan, the same cover is called Mortgage Reducing Term Takaful (MRTT). It’s also a full flexi loan. You can put extra cash, like a bonus, into the loan, which lowers what you still owe and the interest you pay on it. If you need that money back later, you can take it out again, which is called a redraw. As an example, on a RM500,000 home, you could borrow up to RM450,000 to buy the property, and you’d pay the remaining RM50,000 yourself as your down payment. You could then borrow up to RM150,000 more for your renovation, MRTA, and legal fees. The final loan amount you get depends on RHB Bank’s check of your income and any loans you already have. Since the renovation is part of your home loan, you apply once and make one monthly repayment. Home loan interest rates are generally lower than personal loan rates. Your renovation cost is also spread over your home loan’s repayment period of up to 35 years or until you turn 70, whichever comes first, while most personal loans run for up to 10 years. The savings you’d have set aside for renovation can go towards furniture or your emergency fund instead. RHB Bank pays out the renovation money bit by bit, each time your contractor finishes a stage of the work. The renovation is done through The Makeover Guys, which handles the design, project management, and construction. Your renovation budget is set when you apply for the loan, so get a quote first to see how much of the extra 30% you’ll need. You can also compare home loan rates before sending an enquiry through The Makeover Guys’ website. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia
body: 'Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur. The post F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia appeared first on Oh! Media.

title: 'Banks weather Middle East shock with asset quality intact
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's banking sector asset quality remains broadly resilient despite the economic impact of the conflict in the Middle East, according to RHB Research. The firm said any repayment strain remained confined to pockets of the economy rather than becoming systemic. Citing Bank Negara Malaysia's recent assessment and engagement session, the firm said the main transmission channels from the conflict were through the real economy and global financial markets rather than direct bank exposures. Higher input and logistics costs, coupled with softer demand, were putting pressure on business margins, particularly among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the wholesale and retail trade, construction and manufacturing sectors. However, domestic demand and electrical and electronics exports continued to support overall economic conditions, while business and system impairment ratios remained steady at 2.8 per cent and 1.4 per cent, respectively. RHB Research said Stage 2 loans had also eased, while household borrowers remained resilient. Meanwhile, the banking sector could withstand higher bond yields, although a 100-basis-point rise could reduce the sector's common equity Tier-1 (CET-1) ratio by about 46 basis points after mitigation measures. The firm said the impact would be manageable but banks would have thinner capital cushions compared with the 2021-2022 bond sell-off. It estimated that a 100-basis-point parallel shift in bond yields could reduce sector CET-1 capital by about RM8 billion at the group level. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) were among the most sensitive to higher yields at group level, with estimated CET-1 reductions of 88, 62 and 57 basis points respectively. At the bank-entity level, Maybank was the most sensitive, with an estimated 104-basis-point reduction, followed by Bank Islam at 88 basis points and Alliance Bank at 70 basis points. RHB Research said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank Bhd and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital releases under Basel III reforms, cushioning much of the mark-to-market impact. For banks using the internal ratings-based approach, corporate restructuring and dividend reinvestment plans (DRPs) could provide some capital relief. RHB Research said the sector's buffers were thinner than during the 2021-2022 bond sell-off, when the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yield rose to 4.07 per cent at end-2022 from 2.69 per cent at end-2020. The firm estimated that banks incurred about RM16 billion in fair-value losses on securities classified as fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) over the two years. Despite this, the sector's CET-1 ratio remained broadly within 14 to 15 per cent, supported by strong net profit growth, sizeable FVOCI reserve buffers and DRPs. Banks also shifted some new security purchases into held-to-maturity portfolios to reduce exposure to mark-to-market losses. On funding conditions, Bank Negara was said to have played down concerns that rising KLIBOR reflected thinning liquidity in the instrument, although average funding costs had increased. RHB Research said regulatory liquidity ratios remained healthy, with the central bank comfortable with banks operating at lower levels rather than paying excessively to secure funding. title: '丰隆银行3分行明年关闭，客户业务转移至附近分行！ | 老板好
body: '丰隆银行3分行明年关闭，客户业务转移至附近分行！ 丰隆银行（Hong Leong Bank）将关闭3家位于吉隆坡的分行，最后营业日定于2027年2月19日（星期五），受影响分行的客户及业务将转移至附近分行。 根据丰隆银行官网资料，3家即将关闭的分行分别位于Segambut、Brickfields及Pandan Indah。 3家分行将搬去哪？ 其中，Segambut分行关闭后，相关业务将转移至Menjalara分行；Brickfields分行的业务则转往Bangsar分行。 至于Pandan Indah分行，相关业务将转移至Ampang Taman Putra分行。 这意味着，受影响客户日后仍可继续通过丰隆银行其他分行办理相关业务，不过需要前往新的指定分行。 2月19日最后营业 上述3家分行的最后营业日为2027年2月19日（星期五）。 客户若平时习惯到这些分行办理银行业务，可留意相关安排，并在分行关闭后前往指定的替代分行。 银行也建议客户根据自身需要，提前熟悉新的服务地点，以免分行关闭后影响日常银行业务。 全国仍有逾200家分行 尽管这3家分行将关闭，丰隆银行在全国仍维持规模庞大的实体服务网络。 目前，丰隆银行在全国拥有超过200家分行及1025个自助服务机（ATM），客户仍可通过其他分行及自助服务渠道办理相关银行业务。 随着银行业持续推动数码化，越来越多客户通过网上银行及手机应用办理转账、缴费及其他日常银行业务，银行也持续根据客户使用情况调整实体分行网络。 因此，这次关闭3家分行主要涉及相关地点的服务网络调整，客户的银行账户及业务并不会因为分行关闭而终止。

title: 'Daily Newswatch - 2 Oct 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI closed in the red, tumbling 1.3% to 1,630 points on Thursday amid broad-based profit-taking and continued foreign selling despite gains across several key regional markets. Sentiment remained fragile amid persistent external uncertainties and a lack of domestic catalysts, with investors keeping a close watch on global bond yields, oil prices and overseas market developments for direction. Construction, Utilities and Plantation led sectoral losses, with all dropping 1.9%. This is dragged by Kuala Lumpur Kepong (-3.5%), Hong Leong Bank (-1.3%) and Press Metal Aluminium (-3.9%). Market breadth remained weak, with 749 losers against 342 gainers, while 496 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Thursday, led by strong gains in technology and semiconductor stocks following Micron Technology’s upbeat outlook, while softer-than-expected US inflation data eased expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike. Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged 3.3% to 68,957, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.9% to a record 48,354, and South Korea’s KOSPI rose 2.0% to 6,971. Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged 3.3% to 68,957, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.9% to a record 48,354, and South Korea’s KOSPI rose 2.0% to 6,971. In South Korea, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix climbed 2.61% and 3.10%, respectively, alongside gains in SK Square (+1.32%), Hanwha Aerospace (+2.78%), LG Energy Solution (+0.98%) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (+2.95%). South Korea’s September exports also surged 83.5% YoY to a record US$120.9 billion, driven by a 263% jump in semiconductor exports to a record US$60.3 billion. Hong Kong and China markets were closed for the National Day holiday. European stocks opened the fourth quarter sharply lower on Thursday, weighed by rising global government bond yields and concerns that major central banks could keep interest rates higher for longer. The STOXX 50 fell 1.5% and the STOXX 600 dropped 1.3% to their lowest levels in around three and a half months, with financials leading the declines as banks fell more than 3.5%, while automobiles and parts and basic resources dropped between 1.5% and 2%. US stocks closed mostly higher on Thursday, recovering from earlier losses as the selloff in Treasuries eased. The S&P 500 gained 0.2% while the Nasdaq CI and the Dow ended broadly flat. The 10-year Treasury yield retreated from its highest level since 2002 as the unwinding of crowded positions helped ease pressure on equities. Treasuries also found support after Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said more time may be needed to assess whether further rate hikes are warranted, lending some support to credit-sensitive stocks. Chipmakers also advanced, with Nvidia gaining 1.1%, AMD 0.6% and Micron 3.0% after the company issued an upbeat current-quarter outlook following strong fiscal fourth-quarter results. US: Manufacturing Activity Remains Robust, Prices Soar The ISM Manufacturing PMI edged down to 54.5 in September 2026 from 54.6 in August, compared to forecasts of 55. Still, the reading continued to point to robust growth in the manufacturing sector, with new orders (55.3 vs 53.7) and employment (52.7 vs 51.2) rising at a faster pace while production slowed slightly (56.7 vs 58.3. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Gains on Middle East Risks Crude oil traded around $93 per barrel on Friday after gaining for two consecutive sessions, as the US weighed sending another aircraft carrier to the Middle East, raising the prospect of an escalation in the war with Iran and further disruptions to regional energy supplies. The Pentagon is also considering the deployment of 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, giving President Donald Trump additional options if he decides to intensify attacks on Iran. (Trading Economics) US: Treasury Sell-Off Eases 5.3% on Thursday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note topped 5.3% on Thursday, its highest level since early 2002, before retreating slightly to 5.27%. The bond market has remained under pressure amid expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Fed, as persistent inflationary pressures from higher oil prices and the lack of a resolution to the Middle East conflict continue to weigh on sentiment. Concerns over the US fiscal and debt outlook, along with resilient economic data, have added to the pressure. (Trading Economics) US: Benchmark yield hits highest since 2002 as bonds sell off The US benchmark yield climbed to the highest since 2002 as rising oil prices drove a renewed sell-off in global bonds. The yield on the 10- year Treasury note rose as much as six basis points to 5.34% on Thursday, rising past the 2007 peak. Earlier this week, the rate on 30-year US bonds also hit a 24-year high. (Bloomberg) US: House Price Growth Slows More Than Expected US private payrolls growth accelerated in September, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday. Private employment rose by 90,000 jobs this month after a downwardly revised 36,000 in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment increased by 70,000 after a previously reported 38,000 advance in August. (Nationwide Building Society, United Kingdom) US: Gold Rises on Soft US PCE Inflation Data Gold climbed toward $4,200 an ounce on Thursday, recovering losses from the previous session as softer-than-expected US PCE inflation data reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. The US PCE price index rose 0.3% in August, below the 0.4% forecast, while core PCE increased 0.2%, also coming in below expectations for a 0.3% gain. Markets now see roughly a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October, down from 51% before the PCE release. (Trading Economics) JP: 10-Year Yield Rises on Hawkish BOJ Outlook Japan’s 10-year government bond yield climbed above 3.1% on Thursday, returning to 30-year highs as strong economic data and hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan reinforced expectations for a faster pace of policy tightening. Central bank data showed manufacturing sentiment improved in the third quarter to its highest level in more than eight years, while overall business conditions reached their most favorable levels in decades. (Trading Economics) SK: Inflation Rate Slows in September South Korea’s annual inflation rate slowed to 2.9% in September 2026 from 3.1% in August, in line with market expectations but remained above the central bank’s 2% target. The slowdown was largely driven by softer price growth for food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.0% vs 1.3% in August), and alcohol and tobacco (0.1% vs 0.2. (Trading Economics) TW: Plans US$13 bil in extra energy spending given high global prices Taiwan's government said on Thursday that it plans to spend around T$415 billion (US$13.0 billion) this year to help its main power producer Taipower and oil refiner CPC absorb costs from sharply rising global energy prices due to the Middle East war. Taiwan has not passed on most of the rising costs to consumers, unlike in other parts of the world, and it heavily subsidises energy bills, helping to keep inflation down. (Reuters) SG: Home prices accelerate despite slowdown in sales Singapore private home prices rose at the fastest pace since 2024 even as sales slowed, in a sign that the property boom in the city-state has yet to abate. An index of private residential property increased by 1.4% in the third quarter, accelerating from 0.5% in the second, according to preliminary estimates released by the Urban Redevelopment Authority Thursday. (Bloomberg) MY: MEF welcomes minimum wage reprieve for MSMEs, backs sustainable wage growth The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed the government's decision to grant micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) a reprieve from further increases in the current RM1,700 minimum wage, for the time being. MEF senior advisor for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the decision provides much-needed breathing space for MSMEs, which continue to face rising operating costs and an increasingly competitive business environment. (Bernama) MY: Manufacturing ends 3Q broadly stable as orders soften, hiring rises, inflation eases - PMI data Malaysia’s manufacturing sector ended the third quarter broadly stable, with softer new orders and output offset by rising employment and easing inflation. The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Malaysia manufacturing purchasing managers index (PMI) fell below the neutral 50 mark for the first time in four months in September. (The Edge) MY: Budget 2027: Govt to review cost pressures faced by small enterprises, says Anwar The government will study the cost pressures in procurement and operations faced by small enterprises following the global supply crisis when formulating Budget 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said the matter was among those raised during the Budget 2027 engagement session with representatives of associations and Bumiputera contractor companies held at Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, on Wednesday. (The Edge) MY: Singapore to explore third-country investment in Johor's special economic zone Malaysia and Singapore are exploring ways to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), further strengthening the zone as a regional investment and export hub. Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said the cooperation would extend beyond Johor and Singapore to include efforts to attract investors from other countries and facilitate exports to other markets. (The Edge) CKI: Taps independent partners to expand sales network Home appliance maker Cuckoo International (MAL) Bhd has launched an associate sales partner (ASP) structure and signed four independent businesses to expand its sales network. The initiative complements its existing workforce of more than 8,000 sales and service personnel by allowing external partners to sell and support Cuckoo products. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Former CEO Erkki Tapio Ranta returns to helm Hengyuan Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has brought back former chief executive officer (CEO) Erkki Tapio Ranta to lead the company, with immediate effect. Ranta, 62, previously served as Hengyuan’s CEO from March 2020 to July 2021. He now returns to succeed Yin LuJiang, 55, who is stepping down from all duties and responsibilities as CEO after nearly three years at the helm, according to a statement on Thursday. (The Edge) EMPG: Clothing company EMPG has Berjaya Securities to underwrite ACE Market IPO Clothing designer and manufacturer EMPG Group Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd for its planned ACE Market listing. Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd is to underwrite the shares offered to the Malaysian public and eligible persons through pink form allocation, said the company in a statement on Thursday. (The Edge) KKB: secures RM517 mil contract for water infrastructure upgrade in Sarawak KKB Engineering Bhd said on Thursday it has secured a government contract for water infrastructure upgrade in Sarawak worth RM517 million. This marks the group’s second major win within a week. In a bourse filing, the engineering group said the three-year contract was awarded through the Regional Corridor Development Authority (Recoda), the state agency managing the development plan for the Sarawak Corridor of Renewable Energy (Score). (The Edge) ECOSYS: IPO oversubscribed by 206.7 times ahead of Oct 14 ACE Market debut The public portion of EcoSys (Malaysia) Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 206.70 times ahead of its Oct 14 debut on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia. The industrial solutions provider said in a statement Thursday that it received 31,734 applications for 5.93 billion shares, against the 28.57 million new shares made available for public subscription. (The Edge) TIENWAH: Tien Wah Press unit to buy Indonesian factory from BAT for RM34m, secures three supply deals Tien Wah Press Holdings Bhd said its unit plans to buy a factory in Malang, Indonesia, which it currently leases, for 150 billion rupiah (RM34.07 million) from British American Tobacco (BAT) Group’s PT Bentoel Prima. The five parcels of land, measuring 5.78 acres, are currently used by Tien Wah’s 51%-owned unit, PT Bintang Pesona Jagat (BPJ), for its tobacco packaging printing operations. (The Edge) ZETRIX: TS Wong pares down Zetrix AI stake to 10.6% Zetrix AI Bhd managing director Wong Thean Soon on Thursday sold more of his shares in the company, bringing his combined direct and indirect stakes to 10.602%, down from last week's 10.97%. Wong, better known as TS Wong, disposed of 22.73 million shares held by his investment vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd at 16.2 sen per share in a transaction dated Sept 30, according to filings on Thursday. (The Edge) MAYBANK: Falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks Malayan Banking Bhd fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields.Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. (The Edge) MNHLDG: Founders make windfall from selling 20 sen warrant-converted shares at RM3.91 The three co-founders and executive directors of Main Market-listed MN Holdings Bhd have made a combined net gain of nearly RM45 million after converting company warrants into shares at just 20 sen apiece and offloading a chunk of those shares to institutional investors at RM3.91 per share. (The Edge) SDRED: Selangor Dredging plans Penang development, reports RM156m unbilled sales Selangor Dredging Bhd is planning a residential development near Bukit Mertajam, Penang, comprising 122 three-storey superlink villas and a clubhouse, according to a press statement issued on Sept 30. The property developer also reported RM155.78 million in unbilled sales from its ongoing residential projects. (The Edge) GBBOND: To boost adhesive production capacity by 35% with new Penang factory Newly listed GB Bond Holdings Bhd plans to increase its annual industrial adhesive production capacity by about 35% to 31,971.3 tonnes as it sets up a new factory near its headquarters in Bukit Panchor, Penang. The industrial adhesive maker has allocated RM5.5 million from its initial public offering (IPO) proceeds to rent the approximately 40,000 sq ft factory and purchase new production machinery. (The Edge) GBBOND: Closes below IPO price on debut, second ACE counter to do so in a week GB Bond Holdings Bhd was barely higher in its ACE Market debut on Thursday before the industrial adhesive maker slipped below the listing price. The stock opened at 25.5 sen, just half a sen above its initial public offering (IPO) price of 25 sen per share. (The Edge) IOIPROP: Gets Bursa Securities approval for RM7.58b REIT listing IOI Properties Group Bhd said Bursa Malaysia Securities has approved the listing of its proposed RM7.58 billion IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) on the Main Market. In a filing on Thursday, the property developer said Bursa Malaysia Securities had, via a letter dated Sept 30, approved the admission of IOIPG REIT to the Official List of Bursa Securities, and the listing and quotation of its 5.5 billion units under the REITs sector. (The Edge) YINSON: Privatisation talks ongoing, no firm decision yet, says CEO Yinson Holdings Bhd said discussions over its potential privatisation remain ongoing, with no firm decision on whether a deal will proceed, according to group chief executive officer Lim Chern Yuan. “We’re still in discussion, which we have announced,” he told The Edge on Thursday. “Whether we will sign or not, we don’t know as well. Because we are still in talks.” (The Edge) YINSON: Unit to run two electric ferries on Langkawi-Kuala Perlis route A Yinson Holdings Bhd unit and Langkawi Port Sdn Bhd (LPSB) signed a memorandum of understanding to operate an electric ferry service between the resort island and Kuala Perlis on the peninsula's northwest coast. Two 100-passenger capacity vessels will begin sea trials in January ahead of full deployment in May, in time for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima), a biennial trade show of maritime and aerial military assets. (The Edge) PETROS: Hoegh Evi partner to develop Kuching LNG terminal Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) has entered into a joint development agreement (JDA) with Höegh Evi, a global leader in maritime energy infrastructure, to develop the Kuching Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) terminal as part of the Kuching Low-Carbon Hub (KLCH). In a statement today, Petros said the proposed terminal will establish Sarawak’s first LNG regasification facility, delivering natural gas directly to Kuching and surrounding areas to support growing energy demand and strengthen the state’s energy security. (The Star) AAGB: MOF backs AirAsia fundraising drive led by Alton, sources say Global aviation advisory firm Alton Aviation Consultancy has launched a campaign to help low-cost carrier AirAsia Group Bhd raise as much as US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. The fundraising effort is backed by Malaysia’s Ministry of Finance (MOF), which is helping Alton attract lenders and investors as banks and other financiers become more selective in funding airlines amid tougher market conditions and surging jet fuel prices, the sources told The Edge. (The Edge) HEKTAR: Unit bags RM60 million Sarawak roadworks subcontract Hextar Capital Bhd subsidiary Legacy Core Sdn Bhd has secured a RM60 million subcontract from Doland (M) Sdn Bhd to upgrade a road in Sibu, Sarawak. According to a bourse filing on Thursday, the subcontract covers road works, drainage and services relocation on Jalan Oya in Sibu. Work is to start on Oct 2 and will end on Feb 11, 2029. (The Edge) GLOTEC: Redesignates Chen Heng Mun as deputy group CEO; founder's son appointed as ED Globaltec Formation Bhd has announced the redesignation of executive director Chen Heng Mun, 56, as deputy group chief executive officer, with immediate effect. In a bourse filing, Globaltec said Chen would retain his positions as executive director in the boardroom, as well as group finance director. Chen joined Globaltec’s board on March 28, 2012 and also sits on the board of its 70%-owned Australian clean energy unit NuEnergy Gas Ltd. 'The FBM KLCI closed in the red, tumbling 1.3% to 1,630 points on Thursday amid broad-based profit-taking and continued foreign selling despite gains across several key regional markets. Sentiment remained fragile amid persistent external uncertainties and a lack of domestic catalysts, with investors keeping a close watch on global bond yields, oil prices and overseas market developments for direction. Construction, Utilities and Plantation led sectoral losses, with all dropping 1.9%. This is dragged by Kuala Lumpur Kepong (-3.5%), Hong Leong Bank (-1.3%) and Press Metal Aluminium (-3.9%). Market breadth remained weak, with 749 losers against 342 gainers, while 496 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Thursday, led by strong gains in technology and semiconductor stocks following Micron Technology’s upbeat outlook, while softer-than-expected US inflation data eased expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike. Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged 3.3% to 68,957, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.9% to a record 48,354, and South Korea’s KOSPI rose 2.0% to 6,971. Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged 3.3% to 68,957, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.9% to a record 48,354, and South Korea’s KOSPI rose 2.0% to 6,971. In South Korea, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix climbed 2.61% and 3.10%, respectively, alongside gains in SK Square (+1.32%), Hanwha Aerospace (+2.78%), LG Energy Solution (+0.98%) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (+2.95%). South Korea’s September exports also surged 83.5% YoY to a record US$120.9 billion, driven by a 263% jump in semiconductor exports to a record US$60.3 billion. Hong Kong and China markets were closed for the National Day holiday. European stocks opened the fourth quarter sharply lower on Thursday, weighed by rising global government bond yields and concerns that major central banks could keep interest rates higher for longer. The STOXX 50 fell 1.5% and the STOXX 600 dropped 1.3% to their lowest levels in around three and a half months, with financials leading the declines as banks fell more than 3.5%, while automobiles and parts and basic resources dropped between 1.5% and 2%. US stocks closed mostly higher on Thursday, recovering from earlier losses as the selloff in Treasuries eased. The S&P 500 gained 0.2% while the Nasdaq CI and the Dow ended broadly flat. The 10-year Treasury yield retreated from its highest level since 2002 as the unwinding of crowded positions helped ease pressure on equities. Treasuries also found support after Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said more time may be needed to assess whether further rate hikes are warranted, lending some support to credit-sensitive stocks. Chipmakers also advanced, with Nvidia gaining 1.1%, AMD 0.6% and Micron 3.0% after the company issued an upbeat current-quarter outlook following strong fiscal fourth-quarter results. US: Manufacturing Activity Remains Robust, Prices Soar The ISM Manufacturing PMI edged down to 54.5 in September 2026 from 54.6 in August, compared to forecasts of 55. Still, the reading continued to point to robust growth in the manufacturing sector, with new orders (55.3 vs 53.7) and employment (52.7 vs 51.2) rising at a faster pace while production slowed slightly (56.7 vs 58.3. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Gains on Middle East Risks Crude oil traded around $93 per barrel on Friday after gaining for two consecutive sessions, as the US weighed sending another aircraft carrier to the Middle East, raising the prospect of an escalation in the war with Iran and further disruptions to regional energy supplies. The Pentagon is also considering the deployment of 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, giving President Donald Trump additional options if he decides to intensify attacks on Iran. (Trading Economics) US: Treasury Sell-Off Eases 5.3% on Thursday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note topped 5.3% on Thursday, its highest level since early 2002, before retreating slightly to 5.27%. The bond market has remained under pressure amid expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Fed, as persistent inflationary pressures from higher oil prices and the lack of a resolution to the Middle East conflict continue to weigh on sentiment. Concerns over the US fiscal and debt outlook, along with resilient economic data, have added to the pressure. (Trading Economics) US: Benchmark yield hits highest since 2002 as bonds sell off The US benchmark yield climbed to the highest since 2002 as rising oil prices drove a renewed sell-off in global bonds. The yield on the 10- year Treasury note rose as much as six basis points to 5.34% on Thursday, rising past the 2007 peak. Earlier this week, the rate on 30-year US bonds also hit a 24-year high. (Bloomberg) US: House Price Growth Slows More Than Expected US private payrolls growth accelerated in September, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday. Private employment rose by 90,000 jobs this month after a downwardly revised 36,000 in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment increased by 70,000 after a previously reported 38,000 advance in August. (Nationwide Building Society, United Kingdom) US: Gold Rises on Soft US PCE Inflation Data Gold climbed toward $4,200 an ounce on Thursday, recovering losses from the previous session as softer-than-expected US PCE inflation data reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. The US PCE price index rose 0.3% in August, below the 0.4% forecast, while core PCE increased 0.2%, also coming in below expectations for a 0.3% gain. Markets now see roughly a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October, down from 51% before the PCE release. (Trading Economics) JP: 10-Year Yield Rises on Hawkish BOJ Outlook Japan’s 10-year government bond yield climbed above 3.1% on Thursday, returning to 30-year highs as strong economic data and hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan reinforced expectations for a faster pace of policy tightening. Central bank data showed manufacturing sentiment improved in the third quarter to its highest level in more than eight years, while overall business conditions reached their most favorable levels in decades. (Trading Economics) SK: Inflation Rate Slows in September South Korea’s annual inflation rate slowed to 2.9% in September 2026 from 3.1% in August, in line with market expectations but remained above the central bank’s 2% target. The slowdown was largely driven by softer price growth for food and non-alcoholic beverages (1.0% vs 1.3% in August), and alcohol and tobacco (0.1% vs 0.2. (Trading Economics) TW: Plans US$13 bil in extra energy spending given high global prices Taiwan's government said on Thursday that it plans to spend around T$415 billion (US$13.0 billion) this year to help its main power producer Taipower and oil refiner CPC absorb costs from sharply rising global energy prices due to the Middle East war. Taiwan has not passed on most of the rising costs to consumers, unlike in other parts of the world, and it heavily subsidises energy bills, helping to keep inflation down. (Reuters) SG: Home prices accelerate despite slowdown in sales Singapore private home prices rose at the fastest pace since 2024 even as sales slowed, in a sign that the property boom in the city-state has yet to abate. An index of private residential property increased by 1.4% in the third quarter, accelerating from 0.5% in the second, according to preliminary estimates released by the Urban Redevelopment Authority Thursday. (Bloomberg) MY: MEF welcomes minimum wage reprieve for MSMEs, backs sustainable wage growth The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed the government's decision to grant micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) a reprieve from further increases in the current RM1,700 minimum wage, for the time being. MEF senior advisor for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the decision provides much-needed breathing space for MSMEs, which continue to face rising operating costs and an increasingly competitive business environment. (Bernama) MY: Manufacturing ends 3Q broadly stable as orders soften, hiring rises, inflation eases - PMI data Malaysia’s manufacturing sector ended the third quarter broadly stable, with softer new orders and output offset by rising employment and easing inflation. The seasonally adjusted S&P Global Malaysia manufacturing purchasing managers index (PMI) fell below the neutral 50 mark for the first time in four months in September. (The Edge) MY: Budget 2027: Govt to review cost pressures faced by small enterprises, says Anwar The government will study the cost pressures in procurement and operations faced by small enterprises following the global supply crisis when formulating Budget 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said the matter was among those raised during the Budget 2027 engagement session with representatives of associations and Bumiputera contractor companies held at Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, on Wednesday. (The Edge) MY: Singapore to explore third-country investment in Johor's special economic zone Malaysia and Singapore are exploring ways to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), further strengthening the zone as a regional investment and export hub. Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said the cooperation would extend beyond Johor and Singapore to include efforts to attract investors from other countries and facilitate exports to other markets. (The Edge) CKI: Taps independent partners to expand sales network Home appliance maker Cuckoo International (MAL) Bhd has launched an associate sales partner (ASP) structure and signed four independent businesses to expand its sales network. The initiative complements its existing workforce of more than 8,000 sales and service personnel by allowing external partners to sell and support Cuckoo products. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Former CEO Erkki Tapio Ranta returns to helm Hengyuan Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has brought back former chief executive officer (CEO) Erkki Tapio Ranta to lead the company, with immediate effect. Ranta, 62, previously served as Hengyuan’s CEO from March 2020 to July 2021. He now returns to succeed Yin LuJiang, 55, who is stepping down from all duties and responsibilities as CEO after nearly three years at the helm, according to a statement on Thursday. (The Edge) EMPG: Clothing company EMPG has Berjaya Securities to underwrite ACE Market IPO Clothing designer and manufacturer EMPG Group Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd for its planned ACE Market listing. Berjaya Securities Sdn Bhd is to underwrite the shares offered to the Malaysian public and eligible persons through pink form allocation, said the company in a statement on Thursday. (The Edge) KKB: secures RM517 mil contract for water infrastructure upgrade in Sarawak KKB Engineering Bhd said on Thursday it has secured a government contract for water infrastructure upgrade in Sarawak worth RM517 million. This marks the group’s second major win within a week. In a bourse filing, the engineering group said the three-year contract was awarded through the Regional Corridor Development Authority (Recoda), the state agency managing the development plan for the Sarawak Corridor of Renewable Energy (Score). (The Edge) ECOSYS: IPO oversubscribed by 206.7 times ahead of Oct 14 ACE Market debut The public portion of EcoSys (Malaysia) Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 206.70 times ahead of its Oct 14 debut on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia. The industrial solutions provider said in a statement Thursday that it received 31,734 applications for 5.93 billion shares, against the 28.57 million new shares made available for public subscription. (The Edge) TIENWAH: Tien Wah Press unit to buy Indonesian factory from BAT for RM34m, secures three supply deals Tien Wah Press Holdings Bhd said its unit plans to buy a factory in Malang, Indonesia, which it currently leases, for 150 billion rupiah (RM34.07 million) from British American Tobacco (BAT) Group’s PT Bentoel Prima. The five parcels of land, measuring 5.78 acres, are currently used by Tien Wah’s 51%-owned unit, PT Bintang Pesona Jagat (BPJ), for its tobacco packaging printing operations. (The Edge) ZETRIX: TS Wong pares down Zetrix AI stake to 10.6% Zetrix AI Bhd managing director Wong Thean Soon on Thursday sold more of his shares in the company, bringing his combined direct and indirect stakes to 10.602%, down from last week's 10.97%. Wong, better known as TS Wong, disposed of 22.73 million shares held by his investment vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd at 16.2 sen per share in a transaction dated Sept 30, according to filings on Thursday. (The Edge) MAYBANK: Falls below RM10 for first time in nine months, rising bond yields hurt banking stocks Malayan Banking Bhd fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields.Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. (The Edge) MNHLDG: Founders make windfall from selling 20 sen warrant-converted shares at RM3.91 The three co-founders and executive directors of Main Market-listed MN Holdings Bhd have made a combined net gain of nearly RM45 million after converting company warrants into shares at just 20 sen apiece and offloading a chunk of those shares to institutional investors at RM3.91 per share. (The Edge) SDRED: Selangor Dredging plans Penang development, reports RM156m unbilled sales Selangor Dredging Bhd is planning a residential development near Bukit Mertajam, Penang, comprising 122 three-storey superlink villas and a clubhouse, according to a press statement issued on Sept 30. The property developer also reported RM155.78 million in unbilled sales from its ongoing residential projects. (The Edge) GBBOND: To boost adhesive production capacity by 35% with new Penang factory Newly listed GB Bond Holdings Bhd plans to increase its annual industrial adhesive production capacity by about 35% to 31,971.3 tonnes as it sets up a new factory near its headquarters in Bukit Panchor, Penang. The industrial adhesive maker has allocated RM5.5 million from its initial public offering (IPO) proceeds to rent the approximately 40,000 sq ft factory and purchase new production machinery. (The Edge) GBBOND: Closes below IPO price on debut, second ACE counter to do so in a week GB Bond Holdings Bhd was barely higher in its ACE Market debut on Thursday before the industrial adhesive maker slipped below the listing price. The stock opened at 25.5 sen, just half a sen above its initial public offering (IPO) price of 25 sen per share. (The Edge) IOIPROP: Gets Bursa Securities approval for RM7.58b REIT listing IOI Properties Group Bhd said Bursa Malaysia Securities has approved the listing of its proposed RM7.58 billion IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) on the Main Market. In a filing on Thursday, the property developer said Bursa Malaysia Securities had, via a letter dated Sept 30, approved the admission of IOIPG REIT to the Official List of Bursa Securities, and the listing and quotation of its 5.5 billion units under the REITs sector. (The Edge) YINSON: Privatisation talks ongoing, no firm decision yet, says CEO Yinson Holdings Bhd said discussions over its potential privatisation remain ongoing, with no firm decision on whether a deal will proceed, according to group chief executive officer Lim Chern Yuan. “We’re still in discussion, which we have announced,” he told The Edge on Thursday. “Whether we will sign or not, we don’t know as well. Because we are still in talks.” (The Edge) YINSON: Unit to run two electric ferries on Langkawi-Kuala Perlis route A Yinson Holdings Bhd unit and Langkawi Port Sdn Bhd (LPSB) signed a memorandum of understanding to operate an electric ferry service between the resort island and Kuala Perlis on the peninsula's northwest coast. Two 100-passenger capacity vessels will begin sea trials in January ahead of full deployment in May, in time for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima), a biennial trade show of maritime and aerial military assets. (The Edge) PETROS: Hoegh Evi partner to develop Kuching LNG terminal Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) has entered into a joint development agreement (JDA) with Höegh Evi, a global leader in maritime energy infrastructure, to develop the Kuching Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) terminal as part of the Kuching Low-Carbon Hub (KLCH). In a statement today, Petros said the proposed terminal will establish Sarawak’s first LNG regasification facility, delivering natural gas directly to Kuching and surrounding areas to support growing energy demand and strengthen the state’s energy security. (The Star) AAGB: MOF backs AirAsia fundraising drive led by Alton, sources say Global aviation advisory firm Alton Aviation Consultancy has launched a campaign to help low-cost carrier AirAsia Group Bhd raise as much as US$1 billion (RM4.1 billion), according to people familiar with the matter. The fundraising effort is backed by Malaysia’s Ministry of Finance (MOF), which is helping Alton attract lenders and investors as banks and other financiers become more selective in funding airlines amid tougher market conditions and surging jet fuel prices, the sources told The Edge. (The Edge) HEKTAR: Unit bags RM60 million Sarawak roadworks subcontract Hextar Capital Bhd subsidiary Legacy Core Sdn Bhd has secured a RM60 million subcontract from Doland (M) Sdn Bhd to upgrade a road in Sibu, Sarawak. According to a bourse filing on Thursday, the subcontract covers road works, drainage and services relocation on Jalan Oya in Sibu. Work is to start on Oct 2 and will end on Feb 11, 2029. (The Edge) GLOTEC: Redesignates Chen Heng Mun as deputy group CEO; founder's son appointed as ED Globaltec Formation Bhd has announced the redesignation of executive director Chen Heng Mun, 56, as deputy group chief executive officer, with immediate effect. In a bourse filing, Globaltec said Chen would retain his positions as executive director in the boardroom, as well as group finance director. Chen joined Globaltec’s board on March 28, 2012 and also sits on the board of its 70%-owned Australian clean energy unit NuEnergy Gas Ltd. title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026
body: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026 Red Hat has named Hong Leong Bank as the Malaysian winner of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, recognising the bank’s use of open source technologies to modernise its infrastructure and improve digital services. This year’s awards, themed “Unlock what’s next,” recognise 32 organisations across 13 Asia Pacific markets for using Red Hat solutions to address complex business challenges and drive innovation. The awards cover five areas: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization and AI. Hong Leong Bank Modernises Its Infrastructure Hong Leong Bank was recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its efforts to improve the scalability and performance of a critical online business application. The bank moved the application from a traditional monolithic architecture to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. It also adopted Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernise its existing database infrastructure and bring virtual machines and containers together on a common platform. The move has helped reduce software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. The new architecture also allows applications to scale dynamically during periods of high traffic. According to Hong Leong Bank, the modernised infrastructure provides a more flexible foundation for introducing new digital banking capabilities while maintaining the reliability expected by customers. Red Hat said the 2026 winners demonstrate how open source technologies can help organisations simplify complex IT environments, modernise operations and create greater flexibility as technologies such as AI, hybrid cloud and automation continue to evolve. William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, said the collaboration with Red Hat has provided the bank with a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced more quickly. The recognition highlights Hong Leong Bank’s ongoing efforts to modernise its technology infrastructure while supporting the continued development of its digital banking services.

title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank for Unlocking New Possibilities with Open Source at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia
body: 'Red Hat, Inc., the world’s leading provider of open source solutions, today announced the winners of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia. This year, Red Hat recognises Hong Leong Bank for their leadership through open source, demonstrating how open source technologies help organisations navigate complexity, modernise operations, and deliver sustainable growth. As organisations across Asia Pacific embrace AI, hybrid cloud, automation, and cloud-native technologies, managing complexity has become just as important as driving innovation. With AI strategies increasingly spanning different models, accelerators, and cloud environments, enterprises are looking to open source because openness brings choice, and choice brings greater flexibility. That flexibility enables them to adopt the technologies best suited to their business needs while building the agility needed to respond to change. Reflecting this year’s theme, “Unlock what’s next,” the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 celebrate organisations that are leading the way with open source. This year’s awards recognise 32 winners across the region whose innovative use of Red Hat solutions is helping solve complex business challenges and deliver meaningful outcomes for customers, employees, and communities. The winners were recognised for demonstrating how open source can help organisations turn complexity into opportunity. By modernising technology foundations, streamlining operations, and accelerating innovation, each organisation has delivered measurable outcomes that strengthen business resilience and create lasting value. Their achievements reflect Red Hat’s continued collaboration with enterprises across 13 APAC countries to solve real-world challenges through open source. The awards comprise five categories: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization, and AI. Category: Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development Winner: Hong Leong Bank Hong Leong Bank, one of Malaysia’s leading digital-forward banks, has been recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its infrastructure enhancement efforts. As part of the bank’s continuous innovation efforts, the bank sought to improve scalability of a critical online business application by addressing legacy architecture and manual processes. To overcome these performance bottlenecks, Hong Leong Bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. The bank also deployed Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to create a structured path for modernising its existing database infrastructure, effectively unifying virtual machines and containers onto a single, common platform. The architectural shift has transformed the bank’s operational efficiency, cutting software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. By enabling applications to scale dynamically during traffic spikes, Hong Leong Bank has built an agile foundation to accelerate the continuous delivery of innovative digital banking services. Supporting Quotes Daniel Aw, Vice President & General Manager, APAC, Red Hat APAC “Enterprise technology is becoming more complex than ever, but success is no longer about how many new technologies an organisation adopts. What matters more is how effectively these solutions work together to address real business challenges and deliver tangible value. This year’s winners demonstrate that the organisations best positioned for long-term success are those building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Their achievements are a testament to what organisations can accomplish when technology decisions are guided by business needs rather than trends, and it is this approach that we are proud to celebrate through the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards.” William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer, Hong Leong Bank “Enhancing a bank’s technology environment does not happen overnight, and updating infrastructure requires us to understand what is the right-fit for our operations. title: 'Santorini Is Calling, And HLB Connect Has Your Ticket
body: '22nd September 2026 - 4 min read Hong Leong Bank is giving HLB Connect users the chance to collect Connect Points through everyday banking activities. The grand prize is a RM20,000 travel voucher for two to Santorini, Greece. The HLB Connect Tap to Escape Promotion 2026 runs from 21 September to 20 November 2026. There are also travel vouchers for Chengdu, a Machines gift card and RM100 cash prizes up for grabs. If you’re an existing HLB Connect user, you can earn points by logging in and completing eligible transactions during the promotion period. You can earn points from things you probably already do, including: You can also earn points from FPX payments, cross-border QR payments, foreign currency conversions and linking an HLB account to an HLB Singapore account via LINKS. Each transaction comes with its own daily and promotion-period limits, so you can’t simply go on a DuitNow spree and expect unlimited points. New HLB Connect users can also earn 500 points by opening an eligible CASA/CASA-i account online and logging into HLB Connect at least once during the promotion period. You can also earn 200 points for each friend or family member who successfully opens an eligible account through the HLB Connect app. The Connect Points aren’t prizes themselves. They’re used to earn entries into the promotion’s prize draws. You’ll need: And your points aren’t deducted when you earn an entry. For example, someone with 11,370 Connect Points would get one entry into the Grand Prize draw, two entries into the Second Prize draw and three entries into the Third Prize draw. You can check your points through the Points Tracker on HLB Connect. Don’t have the app yet? You can download it from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store, then log in and check your points. The grand prize is a RM20,000 travel voucher for two to Santorini, Greece. Two winners will also receive RM10,000 travel vouchers for a trip for two to Chengdu, China. Four winners will get RM5,000 Machines Gift Cards, while another 500 eligible customers will receive RM100 cash prizes based on their accumulated Connect Points after the main prize draws. The promotion is open to new and existing individual customers who use HLB Connect and have an eligible HLB or HLB Islamic current or savings account, HLB Meezani Account-i and/or HLB credit card. However, some previous HLB Connect promotion winners can still participate, but won’t be eligible to win prizes this time around. HLB’s permanent, contract and temporary staff are also excluded from winning. There’s also a one-prize-per-person rule, so you can only win one prize throughout the promotion period. The travel vouchers can be used for flights, hotels, airport transfers and other travel services provided by Holiday Tours & Travel. However, they’re subject to availability, can only be redeemed once, and any costs exceeding the voucher value will have to be paid by the winner. The vouchers are also non-refundable, non-transferable and can’t be exchanged for cash. Winners are responsible for their own travel documents, permits and visas where applicable. For the Machines gift card, it can only be used for physical product purchases at Machines stores in Malaysia, and each gift card can only be used in a single transaction. Any unused balance will be forfeited. The promotion ends on 20 November 2026, with winners due to be notified by 1 February 2027. So, if you’re already using HLB Connect to pay bills, transfer money or make QR payments, you might as well see how many Connect Points you can rack up. title: 'Hong Leong Bank Launches HLB opus Ceramic Card
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has launched HLB opus, an invitation-only payment card aimed at its most affluent clients. The new card is Southeast Asia’s first credit card made from exclusive ceramic material. It is also Malaysia’s first payment experience built around the Visa Infinite Privilege tier. HLB is positioning opus as more than another premium card. Instead, the bank wants it to act as a gateway to exclusive travel, dining, wellness and concierge services for selected clients. HLB opus Uses Ceramic Instead of Metal Premium credit cards have increasingly relied on metal construction to create a sense of exclusivity. HLB has taken a different approach. HLB opus uses Giesecke+Devrient’s Convego Ceramic technology. The card is produced using high heat and pressure before being finished through diamond refinement. HLB says the result is a scratch-resistant card with a smooth surface and reflective finish. The ceramic construction is also intended to give the card a distinctive physical and acoustic character. For HLB, that physical design reflects the broader positioning of opus as a statement product rather than simply another payment tool. Andrew Jong, Managing Director of Personal Financial Services at HLB, said the bank created opus to recognise the achievements and personal journeys of its clients. He described the card as a tribute to success built through ambition, resilience and long-term effort. Visa Infinite Privilege Brings Global Benefits The new card is anchored around Visa Infinite Privilege. That gives clients access to a collection of premium international services. Benefits include unlimited access to Plaza Premium Lounges worldwide. Clients can also receive selected immigration fast-track services and access to Visa private clubs. Status-matching benefits are available with several luxury and travel programmes. These include Harrods Gold, ALL Accor+ Explorer Gold and Banyan Voyager. The range of benefits reflects HLB’s focus on internationally mobile clients. Jason Phua, Head of Clients at Visa Malaysia, said affluent customers increasingly value personalised experiences over traditional expressions of luxury. He said the partnership combines Visa’s premium privileges with HLB’s understanding of its high-value clients. HLB opus Targets Frequent Travellers Travel rewards form another major part of the HLB opus proposition. The bank has expanded its existing relationship with Malaysia Airlines’ Enrich loyalty programme. HLB says opus provides the highest Enrich Points earning potential in the region. Clients receive 60,000 Enrich Points after paying the annual fee. They can then increase their points earnings through overseas spending. HLB opus clients can also earn one Elite Point for every RM10,000 spent overseas. Those rewards can support status progression and redemptions across Malaysia Airlines and the wider oneworld airline network. Phillip See, Chief Executive Officer of Loyalty & Travel Services at Malaysia Aviation Group, said premium travellers increasingly expect benefits throughout their entire journey. He added that the partnership is designed to provide more flexibility, rewards and travel privileges. HLB Builds a Broader Privilege Ecosystem The card is also tied to HLB’s wider banking relationships. The bank describes this approach as its “One Bank” client success model. Under that structure, Business & Corporate Banking supports business creation and enterprise growth. Private Banking then focuses on protecting and structuring wealth. Personal Financial Services adds lifestyle and rewards benefits through products such as HLB opus. The strategy is designed to keep clients within the HLB ecosystem across different stages of their business and personal financial journeys. That makes opus more than a standalone credit card launch. It also serves as a visible extension of the bank’s affluent and high-net-worth customer strategy. Physical Cards Still Matter in a Digital Banking Era The introduction of a ceramic payment card comes at a time when digital wallets and virtual payment methods continue to grow. However, premium banks still see value in physical cards as status objects. Farouk Musthafa, Managing Director at Giesecke+Devrient Singapore, said physical cards remain an important tangible expression of distinction. He said HLB approached opus as a privilege-first product rather than a conventional card programme. That positioning helps explain the decision to use ceramic instead of more common plastic or metal materials. The card itself becomes part of the luxury experience. HLB Deepens Focus on Wealth and Affluent Banking The launch also supports Hong Leong Bank’s wider transformation strategy. Business banking and wealth management remain important growth areas for the bank. HLB has been strengthening its offerings across corporate banking, private banking and affluent financial services. Its Private Bank already works with global wealth partners including Lombard Odier. HLB opus adds another layer to that strategy by connecting financial relationships with premium lifestyle benefits. For selected clients, the bank wants business banking, wealth management and personal privileges to operate as one connected experience. HLB opus is therefore positioned as both a payment card and a symbol of that broader relationship. With ceramic construction, Visa Infinite Privilege benefits and enhanced Enrich rewards, HLB is clearly aiming at the highest end of Malaysia’s premium banking market.

title: 'HLB Offers RM300 Voucher With iPhone 18 Pro Purchases
body: '15th September 2026 - 2 min read Buying an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max with a Hong Leong Bank (HLB) Credit Card can get you RM300 in accessories vouchers at selected retailers. HLB also offers 0% Extended Payment Plan (EPP) options, depending on where you buy. The campaign runs from 12 September to 31 October 2026, or until the vouchers run out. Spend at least RM5,499 in a single receipt on an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max at Switch, Urban Republic or Machines. The purchase must be made through HLB’s EPP. Switch and Urban Republic accept 24-, 36- and 48-month plans, while Machines accepts 24- and 36-month plans. The voucher can only be redeemed in-store and is limited to one per cardholder. There are 115 vouchers available at Switch and Urban Republic, and 80 at Machines, all on a first-come, first-served basis. The campaign also covers other Apple products. Spend at least RM5,000 in a single receipt on products such as an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch and you’ll get a RM200 accessories voucher at Switch, Urban Republic, Machines or Senheng. The EPP periods vary by retailer. Senheng accepts 24-, 36-, 48- and 60-month EPP purchases, while Machines accepts 24- and 36-month plans. There’s also a separate RM300 accessories voucher for an iPhone Duo purchase, with 50 vouchers available at Switch and Urban Republic and 20 at Machines. If you buy from Apple The Exchange TRX or the Apple Store Online, HLB offers 0% EPP for 6, 12 or 24 months. You can also trade in an existing device through Apple’s trade-in partners. Trade-in quotes are estimates, with the final value depending on the device’s condition, year and model. Any balance left after the trade-in credit can be paid with an eligible HLB Credit Card in full or through 0% EPP. The accessories vouchers aren’t stated as being available for purchases made directly from Apple. If you’re buying from one of the participating retailers specifically for the voucher, check availability before paying. title: 'Venture Capital: Cypress Asia launches RM50 mil debut venture fund with New Hoong Fatt as anchor investor
body: 'Venture Capital: Cypress Asia launches RM50 mil debut venture fund with New Hoong Fatt as anchor investor This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 Two veterans of Malaysia’s start-up and investment ecosystem — entrepreneur and investor Sivapalan Vivekarajah and former Pitch Platforms Sdn Bhd (pitchIN) chief operating officer Xelia Tong — are launching a RM50 million debut venture fund. Main Market-listed automotive replacement-parts manufacturer New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd (NHF) (KL:NHFATT) has committed up to RM20 million as its anchor limited partner. The investment will be made through its wholly owned subsidiary Jhi Soon Manufacturing Industries Sdn Bhd, which will subscribe for up to 20 million Class A redeemable preference shares in Cypress Drive Ventures at RM1 each, NHF said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia. Cypress Drive Ventures is the first fund managed by Cypress Asia Sdn Bhd, which was founded by Sivapalan and Tong. It will target technology-driven local businesses at the pre-Series A and Series A stages that are profitable or have a clear path to profitability. Cypress Asia is seeking the remaining RM30 million from family offices and other investors. Investments will range from RM1 million to RM3 million per company. Cypress Asia expects to make five to seven investments initially and build a concentrated portfolio of 10 to 12 companies if the fund reaches its RM50 million target. Depending on the deal, it may lead the round, co-invest with another fund or join an existing group of investors. The fund has a seven-year term, with the option of two successive one-year extensions. Cypress Asia expects to make its first investment in the first quarter of 2027. It plans to hold its first investment committee meeting in November and already has a pipeline of potential deals that will undergo due diligence. The pipeline will draw on the co-founders’ existing networks, including companies from accelerator ScaleUp Malaysia’s portfolio and Sivapalan’s Soonicorn Collective for later-stage technology businesses as well as businesses within the network Tong built at pitchIN, a digital fundraising and investment platform. Sivapalan and Tong worked together at ScaleUp Malaysia, as a senior partner and a managing partner respectively. They invested in 38 companies under the initiative. Sivapalan also launched the Soonicorn Collective’s Titan, a 12-month coaching and execution programme for founders seeking to scale their business towards RM100 million in revenue, in which 18 businesses took part. “We have a network of companies that we can invest in. Because we’ve been in the ecosystem for so long, people trust us,” says Sivapalan, co-managing partner of Cypress Asia. The firm will also source investments through equity crowdfunding platforms and other venture capital firms. The fund is sector-agnostic but will invest only in technology-driven businesses, says Tong, CEO and managing partner of Cypress Asia. Potential areas include electrical and electronics, automotive, digital health and agriculture. “There are certain areas that we don’t touch — highly regulated businesses, those very dependent on state government contracts, businesses that are purely software, such as human resources software, or very e-commerce-driven. Other than that, we’re quite open,” she says. Cypress Asia will look for companies that can grow profitably and reach a listing or acquisition without having to raise money repeatedly. Tong says an investee should ideally need no more than one or two additional funding rounds after Cypress Asia’s investment. “Our investment thesis is to look for companies that already have a profitable business. It doesn’t have to be a lot; it can be a small profit, or at least they should be profitable this year. But they must be able to prove to us that they can be profitable,” says Sivapalan. “We want to take them to RM8 million to RM10 million in profit over a five-year period and then list them on Bursa Malaysia or another exchange. The good thing about getting them to profitability is that they also become interesting for a merger and acquisition, so it serves a dual purpose.” Endorsement from a public listed company NHF became Cypress Drive Ventures’ anchor investor after about 2½ years of discussions with Tong, as the automotive-parts group explored ways to gain exposure to innovation and diversify its sources of income. Tong first came to know the family behind the company through business and start-up networks when she was at Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd. She had previously encouraged a family member involved in running the group to set up a corporate venture capital arm but the proposal was too early for it at the time. The proposal was subsequently presented to NHF’s board of directors two or three times, with the board raising extensive questions as the company was new to venture investing. Tong says the process gave both sides time to understand what they were entering into and helped build trust. Initially, NHF committed RM10 million. When Cypress Asia decided to apply for Jelawang Capital’s Emerging Fund Managers’ Programme at the end of 2024, NHF raised it to RM12 million, which was the amount of private capital Cypress Asia needed to meet the programme’s 20% threshold for a fund of at least RM60 million. In the end, Cypress Asia was not selected for the programme but Tong says NHF proceeded with the investment as its decision was based on the managers’ experience rather than the prospect of matching capital.
