body: 'This article first appeared in Wealth, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026  Transitioning from the entertainment industry to the food and beverage (F&B) sector is not easy, but when comedian Ajak Shiro heard his child express a desire to start a fried chicken business, he thought of making the idea a reality.  Ajak, whose real name is Mohd Hanaffi Razak, looked for a business partner. This ended up being Aliey Othman, an F&B industry veteran with 20 years of experience and involvement in many notable brands.  Starting with fried chicken as the foundation, their conversation gradually evolved into a discussion on nasi padang, a Minangkabau meal of steamed rice and a variety of side dishes.  “In Malaysia, nasi padang hasn’t become mainstream yet. Moreover, it is considered expensive, so we thought of coming up with a large-scale nasi padang brand, but with low prices,” says Ajak.  He went on to start Babah Ventures Sdn Bhd (BBV) and opened its first stall, named Bumbu Babah, at a food court in Giant Batu Caves in November 2024. There are now more than 50 outlets across Peninsular Malaysia and the company is on track to reaching 60 outlets this year.  Delivering affordable and accessible food is important to Ajak. So, a plate of nasi padang can be priced as low as RM9.90. The uncompromised value the company offers in terms of price point and flavour has become Bumbu Babah’s unique selling point, he says.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price,” says Ajak.  To accelerate its next stage of growth, BBV will launch an equity crowdfunding (ECF) campaign on pitchIN to attract institutional investors with its numbers, create a fundraising exercise with customer engagement and possibly look at fast-tracking to an initial public offering (IPO) by 2028 at the earliest. On the ECF platform itself, the company aims to raise between RM5 million and RM20 million, with shares issued at RM10 each.  BBV plans to allocate 40% of the funds from the ECF campaign to acquiring its top-performing licensed outlets. Two activities, the setting up of corporate-owned outlets in malls and supporting the rollout of the new concept, will be allocated 25% each, while the final 10% will go to enhancing technology and its working capital.  “At this time, we understand the current economic situation. If we look at the customers now, they value the experience of eating in restaurants more, they like good food, but they’re quite sensitive to price.” - Ajak (Photo by BBV)  Behind the quick expansion  The business has been able to expand quickly because its licensees have shown interest in opening more outlets.  “We call it a licensed-and-managed concept because we are very mindful that we don’t want licensees or franchisees to run the outlets their own way and steer away from the standard operating procedures (SOPs). So, we came up with a structure where they provide the funding and become a passive investor in the outlet,” says BBV corporate finance manager Chan Eu-Jinn.  This is how the system works: the licensee fully owns the outlet, but BBV continues to run it as if it belonged to the company. BBV also charges a management fee based on a percentage of the licensed outlet’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) on a monthly basis. “If the outlet is not profitable, we do not charge the management fee, so we have to ensure that it is run properly,” he notes.  There are currently seven corporate-owned Bumbu Babah outlets. The remaining outlets are owned by licensees.  BBV aims to continue expanding, but with a strategy centred more on mall outlets.  “Our MyTown, Melawati Mall and IOI City Mall outlets are doing well, but we are still not in a lot of the major malls in the market yet. With the funds raised, we can then invest in this,” says Chan.  BBV acknowledges that F&B brands have a tendency to overexpand, and Chan says the company has addressed this by setting a target number of outlets for Bumbu Babah restaurants so as to retain operational quality. “When we hit our target number [we may look more into] maintenance, but we will not be growing for the sake of opening and then cannibalising ourselves.”  Bumbu Babah was also able to grow quickly with the introduction of a centralised kitchen to ensure the quality of the food across its licensed outlets remains consistent.  Chan says the curry, sambal, proteins and sides are prepared in advance and sent straight to the outlets. This contributes to the efficiency of its operations, as the staff are able to run the basic equipment at the outlets by following the SOPs.  Ajak plans to develop more offerings beyond Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang menu. Reflecting this resolve is BBV’s recent collaboration with local music group KRU to open a fine-casual-dining restaurant called KRU Cafe.  “We will also have stalls where we will have food menus that include Chinese and Indian food. This is one of the projects that we will implement in time to come, and I think this is one of the reasons why Bumbu Babah will continue to grow in the F&B industry for many more years,” he says.  On solid operational and financial ground  Based on its audited financial statements, BBV is in a strong financial position. The company has four income streams: retail sales at corporate-owned outlets, central kitchen supplies, monthly management fees and turnkey outlet set-ups involving the building and selling of completed outlets to licensees.  For its financial year 2025 (FY2025) ended on Dec 31, the parent company made RM10.4 million in revenue, while the consolidated group revenue came up to RM25.9 million. As for net profit, the parent company recorded RM2.5 million, while the group registered RM3.2 million.  This gives the group a net profit margin of 12.5%, which Tradeview Capital research analyst Tan Jia Hui says sits at the higher end of the F&B industry norm of 5% to 12%. “The normalised margin is more likely to settle at around 10% in the upcoming years, given the margin mix [of all four income streams],” she adds.  The margin is also anchored by a low marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue due to the marketing pull of Ajak.  The group’s FY2025 earnings quality can be considered clean with only RM24,000 coming from one other source of income, which is the interest from its fixed deposits.  Tan notes that liquidity was BBV’s clearest improvement in FY2025, with the current ratio moving from 0.21 times to 1.71 times and the quick ratio from 0.20 times to 1.70 times. Working capital swung from -RM560,000 to RM1.52 million, while its return on assets rose sharply from 6.6% to 74%.  The company has also fully repaid shareholder advances in FY2025, leaving the group free of debt or borrowings.  “In FY2024, the business leaned on RM600,000 of shareholder and director advances and stretched trade payables to fund itself, so its total liabilities-to-equity ratio stood at 13.9 times. In FY2025, those advances were repaid, so there are no borrowings and no non-current liabilities. The group holds net cash of RM1.47 million, taking the liabilities-to-equity ratio down to 0.97 times,” he says.  Gordon Low, founder and managing partner of management consulting firm PiValue Strategy, agrees with Tan. He notes that the company’s financial improvements are backed by positive cash flow rather than being just profit on paper.  “This is a company entering its next fundraising round from a position of real financial substance, which is a reasonable and encouraging starting point for the growth questions that follow,” he says.  On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy.  The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says.  Zooming in on the numbers  Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low.  However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth.  BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027.  Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year.  “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says.  “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.”  Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met.  However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL: KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO.  “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low.  Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover.  This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders.  Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income.  “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan.  Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group.  Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up.  This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements.  “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan.  Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk.  Key-figure risk  Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status.  “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says.  Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time.  Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results.  Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue.  Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic.  “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan.  BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment.

On the operational aspects, Low sees that BBV is signalling a strong early product market fit, although the goals set alongside its projected pace of growth may pose a challenge if not met with a grounded strategy.  The affordability and everyday-meal positioning allow Bumbu Babah’s nasi padang to be embedded in local eating habits and food that consumers can enjoy regularly. “This naturally supports higher purchase frequency and repeat sales than non-local or occasion-based cuisines,” he says.  Zooming in on the numbers  Supported by its milestones, such as the record for selling the highest number of nasi padang servings sold in a day (23,674 plates), the business’ traction is generated by genuine consumer acceptance rather than hype alone, says Low.  However, to maintain a returning customer base amid the competitive F&B space, the company must be able to align its marketing and promotional activities with its forecast growth.  BBV’s projections show its system-wide revenue jumping to RM102 million in FY2026 from RM50 million in FY2025, with a forecast of 80 outlets. It also expects the figure to rise to RM232.4 million in FY2027.  Low says this implies a growth of roughly 104% in FY2026, then a further 128% jump in FY2027. He notes that reaching the FY2027 target would require the group to double its footprint again in a single year.  “Using the FY2026 target of 80 outlets as a base, a rough per-outlet run rate of around RM1.3 million suggests BBV would need somewhere in the region of 150 to 180 outlets to support the 2027 projected figure at a similar productivity level,” he says.  “This indicates nearly doubling the outlet count again within a single year, an even faster pace than the 50 to 80 outlets planned for 2026. It is a mildly aggressive projection, and the credibility of the entire plan rests heavily on the growth strategy behind it.”  Looking at its valuation for the ECF campaign, BBV currently has a reasonable trailing price-to-sales ratio of 3.09 times, based on a valuation of RM80 million against the FY2025 group revenue, which will drop to 1.11 times if its FY2026 forecast of RM72 million is met.  However, the trailing price-earnings ratio (PER) of 24.7 times, based on its FY2025 net profit, reflects a premium valuation as it comes in higher than peer Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd’s (KL: KOPI) trailing PER of 20 times at IPO.  “This could ease as outlet count and sales scale, giving operating leverage and central production efficiencies room to lift net margins and bring the multiple down over time,” says Low.  Tan cautions investors that BBV is materially smaller than the entire system. The audited FY2025 group revenue of RM25.9 million is roughly half the cited system-wide revenue of RM50 million because licensed outlets only contribute to the group through management fees and supply payments, rather than their full retail turnover.  This means a huge chunk of the RM50 million earned by its network of 52 stores belongs to the individual licensed store owners rather than the company issuing the shares. The group revenue of RM25.9 million reflects the actual audited revenue recorded on the parent company’s books, which is the pool of money that generates profit for shareholders.  Also seen in the financial statements is the parent company’s operating profit for FY2025, which appears to be cushioned from non-operational income.  “The parent company’s profit after tax of RM2.5 million is flattered by RM1.5 million of intra-group dividends and a RM280,000 disposal gain. Strip out both and the standalone operating profit is closer to RM900,000,” says Tan.  Put simply, intra-group dividends are distributions of profit paid by a subsidiary company to its parent company or another related entity in the same corporate group.  Chan offers an explanation for the disposal gain, saying that BBV began reorganising its activities into two new subsidiaries established in the second quarter of FY2025. The subsidiaries are BBV Restaurants Sdn Bhd (BBVR), which handles store management, and BBV Trading Sdn Bhd, which is in charge of supply, trading and store set-up.  This internal restructuring led to a transfer of assets and businesses related to the Melawati Mall and TF Value outlets from BBV to BBVR, and created a one-time gain on disposal on BBV’s standalone financial statements.  “These dividends are eliminated upon consolidation because they represent intercompany transactions between entities of the same group. Accordingly, these dividend payments have no impact on BBVs consolidated revenue, profit or profit margins. The same principle applies to the one-off gain arising from the disposal of assets,” says Chan.  Another accounting flag lies in the brand’s intangible assets that fell from RM590,000 in FY2024 to RM530,000 in FY2025. The figure, which equates to 12% of its total assets, had its amortisation period shortened from 60 years to 10 years and reclassified, posing a potential impairment risk.  Key-figure risk  Tan also cautions that BBV’s reliance on Ajak as a key figure of the company could potentially be a risk as the marketing spend of roughly 1.3% of its revenue can fluctuate depending on public sentiment on a celebrity’s status.  “A reputational event or attention shift affecting the founder would remove that structural cost advantage and force a step-up in marketing spend, compressing margins, and the concentration is compounded by reliance on a single brand and cuisine, as the newer concepts remain unproven,” he says.  Furthermore, the F&B space has a low barrier to entry and is fashion-sensitive, which can influence the performance of same-store sales over time.  Seasonality is another factor, with business during the Ramadan and Hari Raya Aidil Fitri festive periods running about 50% and 30% respectively below typical months. Tan indicates that the quarterly figures vary too much to be simply multiplied and predict the full year’s results.  Nevertheless, Chan says momentum is picking up, especially after the RON95 petrol subsidy cap was restored to 300 litres a month from 200 litres, improving sentiment and driving a spike in revenue.  Additionally, Bumbu Babah recently began listing on Grab exclusively and saw an increase of almost 20% at most of the outlets on the food delivery side without cannibalising dine-in traffic.  “Last year, we were focusing a lot on dine-in. We didn’t want to have an additional delivery business affect our operations. So we’re confident that even with all these challenges, we’re on track to hitting our target this year,” says Chan.  BBV’s ECF campaign is currently at the pre-live stage. Investors can visit pitchIN’s website to find out more information and make an investment.

title: 'Final Sukan Asia Aichi-Nagoya: India pun takut jumpa kita -- Misi Malaysia tamatkan penantian 68 tahun petang ini
body: 'Kontinjen negara kini berpeluang merebut antara pingat emas Sukan Asia paling bernilai dalam sejarah apabila skuad hoki padang lelaki Malaysia hanya selangkah lagi daripada mencipta sejarah di Aichi-Nagoya 2026. The Speedy Tigers akan turun di pentas final dengan satu misi besar — menamatkan penantian emas Sukan Asia yang tidak pernah dimenangi Malaysia sejak penyertaan pertama pada 1958, sekali gus memperoleh tiket ke Sukan Olimpik Los Angeles (LA) 2028. Sepanjang 18 penampilan di temasya itu termasuk edisi Aichi-Nagoya, pencapaian terbaik skuad hoki lelaki negara setakat ini adalah dua pingat perak dan enam gangsa. Kali terakhir Malaysia merasai pentas final Sukan Asia adalah pada 2018 di Indonesia, namun ketika itu skuad negara terpaksa akur dengan kekalahan pada aksi kemuncak. Wartawan Astro Arena, Karl Nunis, sempat mendapatkan reaksi Olimpian dan bekas kapten hoki negara, Datuk Mirnawan Nawawi, menjelang pertembungan akhir pasukan kebangsaan bertemu musuh tradisi, India, petang ini. “India jumpa kita diorang pon takut” Ucapan eksklusif dari bekas kapten hoki negara, Datuk Mirnawan Nawawi yang juga merupakan pembawa Jalur Gemilang di Olimpik 2000, Sydney, Australia. Let’s go for GOLD Speedy Tigers @ASTROARENA pic.twitter.com/mdV6UZMrSh — karlnunis (@_karlnunis) October 3, 2026 “Tahniah layak ke perlawanan akhir. “Anda semua telah buat yang terbaik setakat ini. “Anda akan bertemu India. Tiada satu pasukan yang sempurna. “Mereka juga mempunyai kelemahan tersendiri. Mereka juga takut bertemu dengan kita. “Jangan tertekan. Berikan yang terbaik,” katanya. title: 'Scientex to Acquire 503 Acres in Johor for RM580 Mil
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said in an exchange filing. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. The close proximity between Scientex’s existing projects and the proposed development will generate “better operational efficiencies through greater economies of scale”, the company said. An agreement has been signed between its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd and Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd. Scientex mainly manufactures flexible plastic packaging and develops affordable homes in Malaysia. The company has more than 11,000 acres of land spanning seven states across Peninsular Malaysia in its holdings, according to its website. The company has a goal of building 50,000 affordable homes throughout the nation by 2028 and has delivered 47,000 homes to date. The latest acquisition will be funded through a combination of internal funds and bank borrowings. As of July 31, 2026, Scientex held RM357.8 million in cash against total borrowings of RM2.05 billion. The deal is expected to be closed in the second half of 2027. “The lands are expected to provide a steady and sustainable property development model as Scientex continues to focus on affordably priced landed properties where demand continues to remain firm and resilient,” the company added. Shares of Scientex rose one sen or 0.3% to RM3.61 at Tuesday’s noon break, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM5.6 billion. title: 'Samaiden Reveals RM238 Mil Contract Value for LSS5+ Solar Project
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Renewable energy solutions provider Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. The group disclosed the contract value in a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, four days after announcing the contracts without revealing their value due to confidentiality restrictions. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). YTL Construction, which is the project's main contractor, appointed Samaiden to undertake engineering, construction and commissioning works, as well as the procurement and supply of solar components for the 99.99MW alternating-current solar photovoltaic plant. The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. Samaiden said the scope of works includes the supply and delivery of materials, design, engineering, construction, testing and completion of the solar photovoltaic facility, with work to commence upon the issuance of a notice to proceed. The group had earlier posted record annual earnings and revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), its strongest performance since listing in 2020. Net profit for FY2026 surged 93.3% to RM39.07 million from RM20.21 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 3.1% to RM364.5 million from RM353.47 million. The group's order book stood at RM435.8 million as at end-June. Samaiden shares fell seven sen or 2.19% to close at RM3.12 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM1.75 billion. Year to date, however, the counter is up 124.5%. title: 'World Bank Urges Malaysia to Adjust SME Tax Structure in Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysia could simplify the income tax structure for smaller businesses by consolidating its current multiple rate structure into a consolidated single corporate tax rate, the World Bank said. The government could also consider phasing out the preferential treatment once firms grow beyond the threshold of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), Apurva Sanghi, lead economist for Malaysia at the World Bank, said during a briefing on Tuesday. “Changing the incentive structure that otherwise incentivises firms from graduating from SME status can help,” he said, suggesting that the government make the tax system more supportive for investment. In Malaysia, an SME in manufacturing is defined as having sales turnover not exceeding RM50 million or no more than 200 full-time employees. For services and other sectors, it's sales turnover must be not exceeding RM20 million or no more than 75 employees. The World Bank has provided its input to the Ministry of Finance on the drafting of the budget, like many other organisations. The multilateral institution would like to see tax measures in the upcoming Budget 2027 to address Malaysia’s low tax revenue as a share of the size of its economy, Apurva said. While 2027 is an election year, there are still ways to increase tax revenue without increasing tax rates, he noted. Apurva suggested lowering the current high thresholds at which higher marginal personal income tax applies, or placing clearer limits on personal income tax relief and deductions, particularly at the upper end of the income distribution. “Without going into details, I think it's a pretty reasonably well-known fact” that the T20, or the top 20% of the income earners, “capture the bulk of benefits of reliefs that are given by the government,” he added. The multilateral institution would like to see tax measures in the upcoming Budget 2027 to address Malaysia’s low tax revenue as a share of the size of its economy, Apurva said. While 2027 is an election year, there are still ways to increase tax revenue without increasing tax rates, he noted. Apurva suggested lowering the current high thresholds at which higher marginal personal income tax applies, or placing clearer limits on personal income tax relief and deductions, particularly at the upper end of the income distribution. “Without going into details, I think it's a pretty reasonably well-known fact” that the T20, or the top 20% of the income earners, “capture the bulk of benefits of reliefs that are given by the government,” he added. title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi sejajar sentimen positif serantau
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi hari ini, sejajar dengan peningkatan dalam kebanyakan pasaran utama Asia susulan kenaikan saham teknologi di Wall Street dalam tempoh semalaman, walaupun hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang tinggi terus mengehadkan minat terhadap risiko. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.60 mata kepada 1,633.35 berbanding 1,631.75 semasa ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks petunjuk pasaran itu yang dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38, bergerak antara 1,632.77 dan 1,641.20 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 667 berbanding 456 manakala 551 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,108 tidak diniagakan dan 13 yang lain digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan susut kepada 4.18 bilion unit bernilai RM2.95 bilion berbanding 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS dalam tempoh 10 tahun mencecah 5.349 peratus, paras tertinggi sejak 2002 manakala hasil bon 30 tahun meningkat seketika kepada 5.703 peratus. Semasa ditutup pada Isnin, S&P 500 meningkat 0.66 peratus kepada 7,773.95 mata manakala Indeks Komposit Nasdaq naik 1.05 peratus kepada 27,477.31 mata. "Dari sudut positif, harga minyak mentah Brent menyusut di bawah AS$100 setong apabila eksport Asia Barat yang kekal kukuh serta pelepasan stok simpanan kecemasan oleh negara-negara Kumpulan Tujuh (G7) membantu mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap bekalan," katanya kepada Bernama. Menurutnya di dalam negara, minat belian dapat dilihat dalam saham telekomunikasi dan berkaitan komoditi manakala aktiviti dagangan turut meluas kepada beberapa kaunter teknologi bermodal kecil, tenaga dan perladangan. "Kami yakin bahawa saham mewah terpilih boleh terus menarik aktiviti pembelian saham ketika harga rendah susulan pembetulan yang ketara minggu lalu. Bagaimanapun, ketiadaan pembelian susulan sepanjang tiga sesi dagangan lepas menunjukkan pelabur terus berwaspada, dengan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan hasil bon yang tinggi dijangka mengehadkan kadar pemulihan," katanya. Sementara itu, Thong berkata, penurunan harga minyak mentah dan harapan mengenai Belanjawan 2027 dijangka memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada sentimen. "Belanjawan akan dibentangkan pada Jumaat, dengan sektor strategik termasuk semikonduktor, kecerdasan buatan, pendigitalan, peralihan tenaga, farmaseutikal, logistik dan aeroangkasa antara bidang yang diberi tumpuan oleh kerajaan," katanya. Bagi tempoh yang masih berbaki minggu ini, beliau menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran itu kekal dalam fasa konsolidasi dengan kecenderungan untuk pulih secara sederhana apabila situasi terlebih jual memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada pasaran daripada penurunan selanjutnya. "Bagaimanapun, pemulihan yang lebih kukuh mungkin memerlukan pemangkin baharu, dengan Belanjawan 2027, aliran dana asing, hasil bon dan perkembangan geopolitik kekal sebagai faktor utama untuk diberikan perhatian. "Kami mengekalkan julat dagangan FBM KLCI pada 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata bagi minggu ini," katanya. Antara saham wajaran tinggi, IHH Healthcare meningkat 15 sen kepada RM7.91 manakala Maybank dan CIMB masing-masing susut tiga sen kepada RM9.97 dan RM7.70. Public Bank turun empat sen kepada RM4.67 manakala Tenaga Nasional susut 10 sen kepada RM12.90. Bagi saham aktif, Zetrix AI dan Supermax masing-masing meningkat 2.5 sen kepada sembilan sen dan 46 sen, Top Glove menokok sembilan sen kepada 87.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 33 sen manakala SLGC yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE susut tiga sen kepada 25 sen. Antara kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.56 kepada RM44.96, Nestle naik RM1.26 kepada RM91.26, Pentamaster melonjak 64 sen kepada RM6.08, Mi Technovation menokok 59 sen kepada RM6.00 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong naik 46 sen kepada RM21.32. Kaunter paling rugi diterajui Dutch Lady Milk Industries yang susut 30 sen kepada RM29.70, Allianz turun 18 sen kepada RM20.62, TIME dotCom susut 16 sen kepada RM5.45 manakala Mega First Corporation dan Ayer Holdings masing-masing rendah 15 sen kepada RM2.85 dan RM7.55. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 melonjak 190.62 mata kepada 17,734.11, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 42.52 mata kepada 12,232.87, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 42.40 mata kepada 12,015.78, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 89.97 mata kepada 12,158.98 manakala Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 52.31 mata kepada 5,658.92. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian meningkat 1.44 mata kepada 180.41 namun Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan susut 72.14 mata kepada 19,068.0. Indeks Tenaga pula meningkat 10.78 mata kepada 840.72 manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 111.14 mata kepada 9,042.17. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama susut kepada 2.59 bilion unit bernilai RM2.50 bilion daripada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion pada Isnin. Jumlah dagangan waran turun kepada 932.44 juta unit bernilai RM171.80 juta daripada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta semalam. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 653.91 juta unit bernilai RM276.54 juta daripada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta sebelum ini. Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 204.53 juta saham yang didagangkan di Pasaran Utama, produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (298.70 juta), pembinaan (102.12 juta), teknologi (1.32 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (58.39 juta), hartanah (113.14 juta), perladangan (17.37 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (12.12 juta), dana tertutup (45,000), tenaga (69.91 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (294.68 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (25.52 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (38.51 juta), utiliti (36.68 juta), dan amanah perniagaan (59,700). - BERNAMA

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to temper risk appetite. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.60 points to 1,633.35 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The benchmark index, which opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, moved between 1,632.77 and 1,641.20 throughout the trading session. On the broader market, gainers surpassed decliners 667 to 456, while 551 counters were unchanged, 1,108 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover decreased to 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion, compared with 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion yesterday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349 per cent, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly reached 5.703 per cent. At the close on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 0.66 per cent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31. "On a positive note, Brent crude oil eased below US$100 per barrel as resilient West Asia exports and the Group of Seven's (G7) emergency stockpile release helped alleviate supply concerns," he told Bernama. Domestically, he said buying interest was seen in telecommunications and commodity-related stocks, while trading activity also broadened to selected small-cap technology, energy and plantation counters. "We believe selected blue chips could continue to attract bargain hunting following last week's sharp correction. "However, the lack of follow-through buying over the past three sessions suggests investors remain cautious, with persistent foreign selling and elevated bond yields likely to limit the pace of recovery," he said. Meanwhile, Thong said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 should provide some support to sentiment. "The 2027 Budget will be tabled on Friday, with strategic sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, energy transition, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and aerospace among the areas highlighted by the government," he said. For the rest of the week, he expects the benchmark index to remain in consolidation mode, with a mild recovery bias as oversold conditions provide some downside support. "Nevertheless, a stronger recovery may require fresh catalysts, with Budget 2027, foreign fund flows, bond yields and geopolitical developments remaining key factors to watch. "We maintain our FBM KLCI trading range of 1,620-1,650 for the week," he added. Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90. In active trade, Zetrix AI Bhd and Supermax Corp Bhd improved 2.5 sen to nine sen and 46 sen, respectively, Top Glove Corp Bhd put on nine sen to 87.5 sen, V.S Industry Bhd inched up one sen to 33 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC Bhd slid three sen to 25 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd increased RM1.56 to RM44.96, Nestle (M) Bhd rose RM1.26 to RM91.26, Pentamaster Corp Bhd leapt 64 sen to RM6.08, Mi Technovation Bhd jumped 59 sen to RM6.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd improved 46 sen to RM21.32. Top losers were led by Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd, which declined 30 sen to RM29.70, Allianz Malaysia Bhd fell 18 sen to RM20.62, TIME dotCom Bhd trimmed 16 sen to RM5.45, while Mega First Corp Bhd and Ayer Holdings Bhd shaved off 15 sen each to RM2.85 and RM7.55, respectively.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi berikutan momentum positif Wall Street
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka tinggi pada Selasa, seiring dengan momentum positif Wall Street semalaman, memandangkan harga minyak yang terkawal susulan pemulihan eksport minyak mentah dari Asia Barat, mengimbangi trend penjualan berterusan dalam pasaran bon Perbendaharaan AS. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 7.14 mata atau 0.44 peratus kepada 1,638.89 berbanding paras 1,631.75 ketika ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks utama itu dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38. Sentimen pasaran secara keseluruhan positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 272 berbanding 202, sebanyak 364 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,944 tidak diniagakan dan 13 digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan berjumlah 440.19 juta saham bernilai RM164.76 juta. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd memaklumkan bahawa prestasi positif Wall Street semalaman menyaksikan Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 dan Nasdaq Composite masing-masing meningkat sebanyak 0.2 peratus, 0.7 peratus dan 1.1 peratus, manakala harga minyak mentah Brent dan hasil Perbendaharaan 10 tahun masing-masing mencecah US$100.3 setong dan 5.3 peratus. "Di peringkat tempatan, kami menjangkakan pelabur akan terus bersikap selektif menjelang pengumuman Belanjawan 2027, dengan tumpuan diberikan kepada sektor-sektor yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. "Syarikat-syarikat dalam sektor mekanikal dan elektrikal mungkin terus menyaksikan minat belian, disokong oleh penekanan kerajaan terhadap infrastruktur kecerdasan buatan (AI) serta projek tulang belakang Grid Nasional 500-kilovolt Tenaga Nasional Bhd, yang memberi kelebihan kepada syarikat seperti MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd dan Powerwell Holdings Bhd," menurut firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Selain itu, Malacca Securities menyatakan bahawa usaha mengurangkan air tanpa hasil (NRW) juga mungkin kekal menjadi tumpuan, berpotensi memberi manfaat kepada syarikat seperti ISF Group Bhd dan Ranhill Utilities Bhd. "Akhir sekali, 99 Speed Mart Retail mungkin menyaksikan minat belian baharu susulan jangkaan peruntukan bantuan pengguna lebih tinggi di bawah Sumbangan Asas Rahmah dan Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah," menurut kenyataan itu. Sementara itu, Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng berkata Wall Street ditutup lebih kukuh, dengan Nasdaq mencatatkan paras tertinggi baharu apabila pedagang memilih untuk tidak mempedulikan cabaran pasaran semasa dan sebaliknya menumpukan perhatian kepada saham berkaitan AI bagi mengimbangi kesan kenaikan hasil bon. "Untuk hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks akan bergerak dalam julat 1,630-1,640 memandangkan pasaran saham tempatan mungkin bersedia untuk aktiviti pembelian saham pada harga rendah," katanya kepada Bernama. title: 'Banned from Sarawak – but why?
body: 'Kua Kia Soong In August 2007, I arrived at Kuching airport to officiate at a graduation ceremony for teachers trained by New Era College, where I was then principal. I was not carrying drugs. I was not wanted by the police. I was not entering Sarawak to organise an insurrection. I was there to attend an educational ceremony. Yet I was stopped at immigration and told that I was not allowed to enter Sarawak. After I persistently asked why, I was apparently told that I was on a blacklist because of my “anti-logging activities”. I was then put on a flight back to Kuala Lumpur. The contemporary report of the incident records that I had been an active campaigner against the Bakun Dam and had participated in a fact-finding mission concerning Indigenous people displaced from the Bakun area. Think about that for a moment. A Malaysian citizen, travelling from one part of Malaysia to another, was effectively told: you are not welcome in this part of your own country because you opposed the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous communities. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Nearly 20 years later, the question remains: Sarawak may have the constitutional power to do this. But does it have the moral right? The legal argument is not the whole argument Let me be clear. I am not disputing that Sarawak possesses special immigration powers. These powers are rooted in the constitutional arrangements surrounding the formation of Malaysia. Article 161E protects certain constitutional safeguards for Sabah and Sarawak, while Part VII of the Immigration Act 1959/63 provides the statutory framework for immigration control. The Sarawak government itself describes immigration autonomy as an entrenched constitutional right. But there is a much more important question: what is that power for? The justification traditionally associated with Sarawak’s immigration safeguards was the protection of the state’s special interests – including its economy, employment, security, cultural identity and the interests of its people. The constitutional autonomy was not created as a blank cheque for excluding inconvenient Malaysians. There is a world of difference between immigration autonomy and political exclusion. If the purpose of the special powers is to protect Sarawak and Sarawakians, what exactly was Sarawak being protected from when I was turned away? A former Malaysian MP and college principal coming to officiate at a teachers’ graduation? Or an environmental campaigner who had criticised the Bakun Dam and logging? If the latter was the real reason, then the issue is no longer simply immigration administration. It becomes an issue of freedom of expression, political dissent and the abuse of administrative power. What exactly was my crime? My supposed offence was to oppose the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous people. During the 1990s, I was active in opposing the Bakun Dam project. I participated in a fact-finding mission to investigate the conditions of Indigenous people displaced to Sungai Asap. So apparently, in the strange political dictionary of the time, defending forests and Indigenous communities could make a Malaysian an undesirable person in Malaysia. What next? The irony is almost unbearable. Sarawak has every reason to be proud of its unique constitutional position. But autonomy should mean more democracy, not less. It should mean that Sarawakians have greater control over their land, resources, culture and political affairs. It should not mean that the state acquires a constitutional moat around itself so that environmentalists, human rights defenders, academics or political critics can be kept outside. Otherwise, autonomy becomes a very peculiar proposition: the more autonomous the government becomes, the less accountable it becomes to citizens exercising their democratic rights. That cannot be the meaning of Malaysia’s federal bargain. Apparently, the issue has not disappeared. Just last week, Sahabat Alam Malaysia president Meenakshi Raman was denied entry into Sarawak. A Sarawak deputy minister said the state is not required to give advance notice to people barred from entering and that the relevant immigration laws give the state authority to stop people from entering. Civil society groups have called for the reasons and basis for the restriction to be disclosed. Thus, nearly two decades after my own experience, environmental defenders are still encountering the same question: Who gets to decide who is sufficiently ‘Sarawakian’ in spirit to be allowed into Sarawak? But what about international human rights? Here, the distinction between legal authority and international legitimacy becomes crucial. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states in Article 13(2) that everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights goes further in Article 12(4): “No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.” There is, however, an important qualification: Malaysia has not ratified the covenant. Therefore, I would not argue that my exclusion in 2007 was automatically a violation of a treaty obligation binding Malaysia under the covenant. But that does not make the international human rights question disappear. The Universal Declaration remains one of the foundational statements of the international human rights system. And Malaysia has repeatedly presented itself internationally as a country committed to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. The question is therefore not merely was Sarawak legally entitled to do it? It is: was it consistent with the human rights values Malaysia claims to uphold? And that is a much harder question for the authorities to answer. Sarawak’s forests are not a Sarawak-only issue. There is another irony here. Logging, Indigenous rights, biodiversity and environmental destruction are not purely ‘state matters’ in any meaningful moral sense. The rainforest does not stop at the Kuching immigration counter. Neither does climate change. Nor does the destruction of biodiversity. Nor does the displacement of Indigenous peoples. A Malaysian citizen concerned about what happens to Sarawak’s forests is not a foreign agitator. He is a Malaysian citizen concerned about Malaysia. And if Sarawak’s forests are part of Malaysia’s natural heritage, why should Malaysians be treated as outsiders for expressing concern about them? Indeed, the more internationally connected environmental politics becomes, the more absurd such restrictions appear. Malaysia wants to attract international investment. It wants to promote Sarawak as an ecological and cultural destination. It wants to speak proudly about sustainable development and Indigenous communities. Yet an environmental campaigner can apparently arrive at an airport and be told: Turn around. Your concern for our forests is unwelcome here. What kind of message does that send to the world? A constitutional right should come with a constitutional conscience. That is a question of political morality. And it is a question that Sarawak – and Malaysia – still has to answer. Nearly 20 years after I was turned away at Kuching airport, I am still waiting for a convincing answer. – Suaram Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP and former director of the human rights group Suaram. title: 'UK Job Slump Longer Than During Financial Crisis, PMI Says
body: '(Oct 5): Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. The figures will be a concern for Andy Burnham’s government ahead of the budget later this month with the intensifying energy shock and artificial intelligence (AI) threatening to dampen demand for workers. Employers have been shedding staff since the Labour government raised payroll taxes and the minimum wage shortly after returning to power in 2024. There were some signs of the slump bottoming out, however, as job cuts in the services sector were the smallest in almost a year. Furthermore, Britain’s official unemployment rate remains much lower than during the period after the global financial crisis. Britain’s labour market has been soft despite the wider economy smashing expectations during a resilient first half of the year. S&P’s survey suggested that the private sector is largely holding up against the energy shock for now, with demand boosted by stronger consumer spending and technology services amid a rush to harness AI. The composite PMI eased to 52 in September from 52.5 the previous month, remaining above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. It was slightly better than the 51.7 reading in the flash estimate. Still, the outlook has darkened since a resurgence in energy prices last month that has prompted traders to ramp up bets on the Bank of England raising interest rates several times to stop inflationary pressures spreading across the economy. “Subdued demand conditions and rising inflationary pressures contributed to weaker business activity expectations for the year ahead,” said Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence. “Greater-than-expected business requirements seem to have helped to stem the jobs downturn in recent months.” The survey pointed to price pressures growing. Firms’ cost burdens and the prices they charge customers both rose at the quickest pace since June. title: 'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report
body: 'TOKYO (Oct 5): A framework for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cooperate with Asian countries on oil stockpiling is set to be launched, with Japan supporting the initiative through financial assistance and stockpiling expertise, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. Saudi, UAE to cooperate in building crude stockpile in Asia, Nikkei reports The Japan-led Asia Zero-Emission Community (Azec), a grouping of 11 countries including Southeast Asian nations, will hold a ministerial meeting in the Philippines on Thursday, where senior Saudi and UAE officials are expected to announce their intention to cooperate on oil stockpiling, the Nikkei said. The framework is expected to be included in a joint statement from the meeting, providing a basis for member countries to discuss expanding oil reserves with Middle Eastern producers, it said Specific details and the scale of cooperation will be worked out through bilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and the UAE possibly expanding exports to participating countries or providing priority supplies in an emergency, Nikkei said Japan already leases domestic private storage tanks to state-owned oil companies in countries such as Saudi Arabia under a joint stockpiling scheme, which Japanese companies can access in an emergency Japan is expected to share the framework at a ministerial dialogue of the International Energy Forum in Saudi Arabia on Oct 11, the report said. A Japanese industry ministry official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there will be dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the UAE and oil-consuming countries in Asia on the sidelines of the Azec ministerial meeting, although no concrete projects will be discussed. 'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report

'TOKYO (Oct 5): A framework for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cooperate with Asian countries on oil stockpiling is set to be launched, with Japan supporting the initiative through financial assistance and stockpiling expertise, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. Saudi, UAE to cooperate in building crude stockpile in Asia, Nikkei reports The Japan-led Asia Zero-Emission Community (Azec), a grouping of 11 countries including Southeast Asian nations, will hold a ministerial meeting in the Philippines on Thursday, where senior Saudi and UAE officials are expected to announce their intention to cooperate on oil stockpiling, the Nikkei said. The framework is expected to be included in a joint statement from the meeting, providing a basis for member countries to discuss expanding oil reserves with Middle Eastern producers, it said Specific details and the scale of cooperation will be worked out through bilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and the UAE possibly expanding exports to participating countries or providing priority supplies in an emergency, Nikkei said Japan already leases domestic private storage tanks to state-owned oil companies in countries such as Saudi Arabia under a joint stockpiling scheme, which Japanese companies can access in an emergency Japan is expected to share the framework at a ministerial dialogue of the International Energy Forum in Saudi Arabia on Oct 11, the report said. A Japanese industry ministry official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there will be dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the UAE and oil-consuming countries in Asia on the sidelines of the Azec ministerial meeting, although no concrete projects will be discussed. title: 'Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Bursa Malaysia dijangka memasuki fasa pemulihan sederhana minggu ini selepas mengalami tekanan jualan ketara minggu lalu, dengan indeks FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dijangka bergerak dalam julat 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata. Pensyarah Kanan i-CATS University College, Kuching, Profesor Madya Dr. Abu Sofian Yaacob berkata, indeks penanda aras itu berpotensi ditutup sekitar 1,640 hingga 1,650 mata sekiranya sentimen pasaran global bertambah baik. Katanya, paras 1,620 mata merupakan tahap sokongan penting, manakala 1,650 mata pula menjadi paras rintangan utama. “Sekiranya paras 1,650 mata berjaya ditembusi secara kukuh, terdapat ruang untuk FBM KLCI menguji paras 1,660 mata. “Bagaimanapun, kenaikan dijangka tidak berlaku secara agresif kerana pelabur masih berdepan beberapa ketidaktentuan luaran. “Antaranya termasuk hasil bon Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang masih tinggi, turun naik harga minyak mentah serta ketegangan geopolitik yang boleh meningkatkan semula risiko inflasi,” katanya kepada Utusan Malaysia. Menurut Abu Sofian, data pekerjaan AS yang lebih lemah memberikan sedikit kelegaan kepada pasaran kerana mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap kemungkinan pengetatan dasar monetari yang lebih agresif oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed). “Pada masa sama, perkembangan Wall Street dan hala tuju kadar faedah AS akan terus menjadi antara pemacu utama sentimen Bursa Malaysia minggu ini. “Di peringkat domestik, tumpuan juga akan diberikan kepada prestasi sektor perbankan, teknologi, utiliti dan tenaga, selain aliran dana asing,” katanya. Beliau berkata, secara keseluruhannya, pergerakan pasaran minggu ini lebih mencerminkan pemulihan teknikal dan pengumpulan saham secara selektif, berbanding permulaan satu rali kukuh. “Pelabur masih dijangka mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati sehingga terdapat isyarat lebih jelas mengenai hala tuju kadar faedah global, harga minyak dan perkembangan geopolitik,” katanya. Sementara itu, CIMB Securities berkata, FBM KLCI susut 4.33 peratus bulan ke bulan atau 74.71 mata kepada 1,651 mata pada September 2026, sekali gus mencatatkan prestasi bulanan terburuk setakat tahun ini. “Penurunan itu menjadikan prestasi FBM KLCI bagi tempoh sembilan bulan pertama 2026 susut 1.72 peratus. “Tekanan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan peningkatan mendadak hasil bon global mengatasi prestasi ekonomi domestik Malaysia yang kekal berdaya tahan. “Pelabur asing merekodkan jualan bersih dianggarkan RM1.69 bilion pada September 2026, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke paras terendah sepanjang masa iaitu 17.8 peratus pada akhir September 2026 berbanding 18.1 peratus pada akhir Ogos 2026,” katanya. –UTUSAN The post Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

title: 'Pintu itu terbuka pada tahun 2018. Ia boleh terbuka semula
body: 'Pada malam 9 Mei 2018, saya berada di rumah, terpaku di hadapan televisyen. Saya menonton dengan penuh keterujaan yang memuncak tatkala keputusan pilihan raya umum diumumkan sedikit demi sedikit. Menjelang akhir malam itu, pemerintahan selama lebih enam dekad oleh Barisan Nasional dan gabungan pendahulunya, Alliance atau Parti Perikatan, telah berakhir. Buat pertama kalinya, Malaysia menukar kerajaan persekutuannya menerusi peti undi. Rakyat telah memilih kerajaan Pakatan Harapan yang menjanjikan reformasi yang sekian lama dinanti-nantikan. Bagi ramai antara kita yang telah bertahun-tahun memperjuangkan reformasi, ia terasa seolah-olah sebuah keajaiban politik. Kita telah menyaksikan tatanan politik yang sama bertahan mengharungi pilihan raya demi pilihan raya serta protes demi protes. Kini, apa yang dahulunya dianggap mustahil, benar-benar telah berlaku. Sebuah pintu terbuka Perubahan itu membawa harapan. Timbul satu perasaan bahawa akhirnya sebuah pintu telah pun terbuka. Isu-isu yang sekian lama dibangkitkan oleh masyarakat sivil – kebebasan bersuara, akauntabiliti, kedaulatan undang-undang dan kebebasan institusi – tiba-tiba terasa seolah-olah boleh digapai. Namun, jangkaan sering kali dipengaruhi oleh keterujaan pada saat segalanya berlaku. Apabila euforia kian pudar, jelaslah bahawa pertukaran kerajaan dengan sendirinya tidak akan membawa reformasi. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Undang-undang, institusi dan amalan politik yang telah terbina selama berdekad-dekad tidak akan berubah dalam sekelip mata. Reformasi memerlukan masa, kehendak politik dan tekanan berterusan daripada orang ramai. Bulan-bulan awal kerajaan baharu itu kelihatan menjanjikan. Namun, kemajuan terbantut, dan peristiwa ‘Langkah Sheraton’ pada tahun 2020 menyebabkan kerajaan PH tumbang. Apa yang menyusul kemudian ialah satu tempoh ketidakstabilan politik yang melelahkan. Sebahagian besar harapan pada tahun 2018 akhirnya bertukar menjadi kekecewaan. Pilihan raya umum berikutnya pada bulan November 2022 membuka satu lagi peluang. Namun, tiada gabungan parti yang berjaya memperoleh majoriti. Anwar Ibrahim, yang sekian lama dianggap sebagai wajah gerakan reformasi, dilantik sebagai perdana menteri. ‘Kerajaan perpaduan’ pimpinannya turut merangkumi BN – gabungan yang telah ditentang oleh golongan reformis selama berdekad-dekad. Kembalinya PH ke tampuk kuasa disambut dengan rasa lega selepas bertahun-tahun dilanda ketidaktentuan. Walau bagaimanapun, orang ramai kekal berhati-hati, dan perasaan itu berasas. Boleh difahami jika reformasi mengambil masa. Namun, banyak reformasi yang sekian lama dituntut oleh masyarakat sivil telah ditangguhkan, dilemahkan atau diketepikan. Undang-undang yang bersifat menindas, seperti Akta Hasutan dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia, masih terus digunakan. Kadangkala ia digunakan oleh pihak-pihak yang suatu ketika dahulu pernah berkempen menentang undang-undang tersebut. Penahanan pemimpin Mandiri Layanan yang diterima baru-baru ini oleh kumpulan yang diterajui golongan muda, Mandiri, menunjukkan betapa jauh lagi perjalanan yang perlu ditempuhi. Menurut Mandiri, awal bulan ini [September], akaun bank mereka dibekukan dan larangan perjalanan dikenakan tanpa sebarang penjelasan kepada umum. Kemudian, pada 18 September, pihak polis menyerbu pejabat yang dikongsi oleh Mandiri dengan Hayat, sebuah kumpulan yang menentang hukuman mati. Seterusnya, pada 22 September, polis menahan pengarah eksekutif Mandiri, Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi, dan pengarah kewangannya, Dobby Chew, di bawah undang-undang pencegahan pengubahan wang haram. Mereka telah hadir secara sukarela di hadapan pegawai penyiasat untuk memberikan keterangan. Kedua-duanya kemudian dibebaskan, namun siasatan masih diteruskan. Walau apa pun kesudahannya, cara tindakan keras ini dilakukan menghantar mesej yang menggerunkan kepada sesiapa sahaja yang bersuara. Undang-undang yang bertujuan memerangi pengubahan wang haram tidak seharusnya digunakan untuk menakut-nakutkan masyarakat sivil. Perkara ini tidak boleh diterima di bawah kerajaan yang pernah berjanji untuk membuka ruang demokrasi. Pihak berkuasa mesti mendedahkan asas siasatan tersebut serta menarik balik pembekuan akaun dan larangan perjalanan yang dikenakan tanpa penjelasan. Mereka juga mesti menghentikan penggunaan kuasa pencegahan pengubahan wang haram terhadap kumpulan masyarakat sivil. Nampaknya, pertukaran pihak yang memerintah tidak menjamin perubahan dalam cara kuasa digunakan. Itulah sebabnya detik sekarang ini penting. Tekanan terhadap masyarakat sivil bukanlah satu isu terpencil. Ia merupakan sebahagian daripada kerja reformasi demokrasi yang belum selesai. Malah, kemajuan yang perlahan menjadikan peranan masyarakat sivil semakin penting, bukan sebaliknya. Apabila kerajaan bertukar tetapi struktur asas kekal, perlu ada pihak yang bersedia untuk mempersoalkan, meneliti dan menuntut akauntabiliti. Hal ini telah difahami oleh Aliran sejak ditubuhkan pada tahun 1977. Ia terus membangkitkan persoalan mengenai demokrasi, hak asasi manusia dan keadilan sosial di bawah setiap kerajaan yang pernah memerintah Malaysia. Setelah terlibat dengan Aliran selama hampir dua dekad, saya sendiri telah menyaksikan beberapa perubahan tersebut. Saya juga melihat betapa mudahnya untuk berasa tawar hati apabila, selepas bertahun-tahun berjuang, kemajuan tidak sentiasa dicapai sepantas yang kita harapkan. Harapan dalam perjuangan yang panjang Namun, kita juga harus mengingati tahun 2018. Selama bertahun-tahun, perubahan kelihatan mustahil. Kemudian, secara tidak disangka-sangka, ia berlaku. Perkara ini seharusnya membuatkan kita berhati-hati untuk tidak menganggap keadaan hari ini sebagai sesuatu yang kekal. Kita tidak tahu bila perubahan akan berlaku lagi, atau dalam bentuk apa ia akan muncul. Namun, masa depan tidak terikat kepada masa kini. Itulah erti harapan dalam sebuah perjuangan yang panjang. Ia bukanlah satu kepastian bahawa segala-galanya akan menjadi seperti yang kita inginkan. Ia adalah kesedaran bahawa keadaan boleh berubah, dan bahawa apa yang kita lakukan sementara itu penting. Václav Havel menghabiskan masa bertahun-tahun sebagai seorang disiden sebelum menjadi presiden Cekoslovakia yang bebas. Beliau mengungkapkannya begini: harapan “bukanlah keyakinan bahawa sesuatu perkara akan berakhir dengan baik, tetapi kepastian bahawa sesuatu perkara itu bermakna, tidak kira bagaimana kesudahannya nanti.” Perjuangan demi Malaysia yang lebih demokratik sejak awal lagi tidak mungkin dimenangi hanya melalui satu pilihan raya atau satu kerajaan. Pengajaran tahun 2018 bukanlah bahawa perubahan itu mudah. Pengajarannya ialah bahawa perubahan itu boleh berlaku. Dan apabila kemajuan kelihatan perlahan, itu sudah cukup menjadi alasan untuk kita terus melangkah. Chris Chong Editor bersama, surat berita Aliran 28 September 2026 Diterjemahkan oleh Zikri Rahman The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

Beliau mengungkapkannya begini: harapan “bukanlah keyakinan bahawa sesuatu perkara akan berakhir dengan baik, tetapi kepastian bahawa sesuatu perkara itu bermakna, tidak kira bagaimana kesudahannya nanti.” Perjuangan demi Malaysia yang lebih demokratik sejak awal lagi tidak mungkin dimenangi hanya melalui satu pilihan raya atau satu kerajaan. Pengajaran tahun 2018 bukanlah bahawa perubahan itu mudah. Pengajarannya ialah bahawa perubahan itu boleh berlaku. Dan apabila kemajuan kelihatan perlahan, itu sudah cukup menjadi alasan untuk kita terus melangkah. title: 'Court allows temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport
body: 'The Sessions Court has granted the temporary release of former PM’s political secretary Shamsul Iskandar’s passport for travel to Germany and London. KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, the former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intended to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the MADANI principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aimed to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he planned to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During today’s proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy Public Prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Judge Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective today, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249, respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei’s company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Tracking Wall Street Gains
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Monday morning, tracking overnight gains on Wall Street as softer US payroll growth eased investor concerns regarding an immediate interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) climbed 5.01 points, or 0.31 per cent, to 1,635.88 compared to last Friday’s closing figure of 1,630.87. The benchmark index initially opened 2.55 points higher at 1,633.42. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 224 to 158, while 337 counters remained unchanged, 2,054 untraded, and 24 suspended. Total market turnover stood at 206.30 million shares valued at RM98.78 million. Key market indices and sector performances during early trade included: - Heavyweight Movement: Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to reach RM10.06, RM4.70, RM7.69, and RM13.00, respectively. Conversely, IHH Healthcare shed six sen to RM7.74. - Top Active Stocks: VS Industry advanced three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTec gained four sen to 74.5 sen, GB Bond edged up half-a-sen to 23.5 sen, SFP Tech added one sen to 28.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange traded flat at 51.5 sen. - Top Gainers: Samaiden surged 19 sen to RM3.03, UWC gained 16 sen to RM7.73, Critical Holdings rose 15 sen to RM2.61, Mi Technovation moved up nine sen to RM5.30, and Solarvest advanced eight sen to RM4.25. - Top Decliners: Nestle led losses, dropping 32 sen to RM89.20, followed by Vitrox (down 14 sen to RM10.32), Kobay Technology (down 12 sen to RM2.18), Kelington (down five sen to RM8.58), and YTL Power International (down four sen to RM5.64). - Index & Sector Breakdown: The Financial Services Index gained 97.59 points to 19,138.10, the Energy Index added 2.57 points to 835.60, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.59 of a point to 179.11, and the Plantation Index moved up 2.23 points to 9,058.78. The FBM Mid 70 Index climbed 28.14 points to 17,510.07, the FBM Emas Index rose 33.81 points to 12,204.38, and the FBM ACE Index improved 31.41 points to 5,560.87. –NMT
