'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail berkata pembiayaan berkenaan menyediakan platform mampan untuk syarikat beroperasi secara bebas sambil meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti. “Penyempurnaan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini merupakan pencapaian penting bagi DNB dan mencerminkan keyakinan kukuh terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang kami dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia,” katanya. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bertindak sebagai pengatur utama yang diberi mandat, pengurus buku dan pengatur penyelaras bagi pembiayaan itu. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd pula merupakan pengatur utama bersama yang diberi mandat, manakala AmInvestment Bank bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan DNB. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities
body: 'Indonesia land reform raises uncertainty for Malaysian planters with exposure there — CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 25): Malaysian plantation companies with sizeable operations in Indonesia face greater regulatory uncertainty following the country’s new agrarian reform law, with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG), Genting Plantations Bhd (KL:GENP) and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KL:KLK) among those with the largest exposure, according to CIMB Securities. The potential impact, however, remains unclear as key details — including maximum landholding limits for companies and affiliated entities, and how a provision requiring at least 20% of certain land to be made available for agrarian reform and redistribution — have yet to be finalised through implementing regulations. As such, CIMB has not made any adjustments to its earnings forecasts or the land banks of plantation companies under its coverage, saying it sees higher regulatory uncertainty rather than an immediate loss of land or earnings. “We do not expect an across-the-board 20% cut in existing land,” the research house said in a note on Friday. Indonesia’s parliament approved the Agrarian Reform Law on Tuesday, creating a broader framework to address land ownership concentration, redistribution and longstanding agrarian conflicts. The law also provides for a dedicated body under the president to oversee implementation, supervision and conflict resolution. However, the Indonesian government still needs to draw up implementing rules that will, among other matters, determine minimum and maximum landholding limits. Agrarian Affairs and Spatial Planning Minister Nusron Wahid said such details would be provided through subsequent regulations. The development was reported earlier this week, including by Bloomberg, which highlighted broader risks to Indonesia’s plantation and property sectors. CIMB’s latest assessment focuses on the potential implications for Malaysian-listed plantation companies. Among CIMB’s Malaysian plantation coverage, SD Guthrie, Genting Plantations and KLK have the largest absolute plantation exposure to Indonesia. IOI Corp Bhd (KL:IOICORP) has a smaller relative exposure, while Johor Plantations Group Bhd (KL:JPG), Ta Ann Holdings Bhd (KL:TAANN) and Hap Seng Plantations Holdings Bhd (KL:HSPLANT) have plantation operations entirely in Malaysia. CIMB said the impact will depend on the final land limits, whether the 20% rule applies to existing plantations and how it will be implemented. Bloomberg consensus as at Friday showed analysts remaining broadly positive on SD Guthrie and Genting Plantations, while views on KLK were more mixed. For SD Guthrie, 17 analysts had "buy" calls and three had "hold" calls, with a 12-month target price of RM7.68. Genting Plantations had 10 "buy" calls and two "hold" calls, with a target price of RM6.81. KLK had nine "buy" calls, 10 "hold" calls, and one "sell", with a target price of RM24.57. Separately, India’s decision to lower import duties on major edible oils could provide some support for crude palm oil (CPO) demand, although CIMB expects the benefit to Malaysian planters to be modest. India cut the basic customs duty on crude palm oil and crude soybean oil to 5% from 10%, while eliminating the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil, effective Thursday. The Indian government said the move was aimed at reducing import costs and easing domestic edible oil prices. CIMB said the lower CPO duty should reduce landed costs and support Indian palm oil imports, although the larger tariff reduction for sunflower oil could make it more competitive against palm oil and limit the increase in demand. India accounted for about 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025. CIMB said the main benefit for Malaysian planters would likely come through firmer CPO prices rather than a significant direct increase in export volumes. CIMB maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 per tonne for 2027. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. Contact us for any changes. Related Stocks Comments

title: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says
body: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says KUALA LUMPUR — Tenaga Nasional Bhd could absorb an additional RM120 million to RM150 million in costs between September and December 2026 following the expansion of government exemptions covering electricity-related charges for residential consumers, according to CIMB Securities. The brokerage said nearly one million additional households are expected to benefit after the monthly electricity consumption threshold for the exemptions was raised to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) from 600 kWh. The change brings the total number of residential consumers covered to more than eight million. The exemptions involve the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and sales and service tax, reducing the immediate impact of electricity costs on a wider group of households. However, CIMB Securities said the arrangement means TNB is expected to absorb additional costs during the September-to-December protection period. The eventual financial impact will depend on the level of AFA charges during that period, which in turn is influenced by fuel costs. Unexpected cost for utility CIMB Securities described the development as a negative surprise because it had previously expected TNB to recover any government-sanctioned AFA subsidies through the Kumpulan Wang Industri Elektrik fund. The latest arrangement instead places an estimated RM120 million to RM150 million of additional costs on the national utility during the final four months of 2026. The research house noted that TNB had previously made a voluntary RM150 million corporate contribution towards the government’s tiered electricity rebate initiative between April and September 2020. That programme was introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. CIMB Securities said it regarded the 2020 contribution differently because it was made in response to what it described as a severe and unprecedented crisis. The latest cost absorption therefore raises a broader question for investors over whether TNB could be required to shoulder similar costs beyond 2026. 2026 profit forecast trimmed Despite the additional burden, CIMB Securities maintained its “buy” recommendation on TNB and kept its discounted cash flow-based target price unchanged at RM15.90. The brokerage reduced its core net profit forecast for TNB’s full 2026 financial year by two per cent to account for the additional costs. Its core net profit forecasts for the 2027 and 2028 financial years were left largely unchanged. CIMB Securities said the immediate effect on TNB’s core earnings remained relatively small and was insufficient to change its valuation. Its longer-term concern centres instead on what could happen if fuel prices remain elevated and the expanded AFA exemptions continue beyond the end of 2026. Regulatory predictability in focus The research house warned that requiring TNB to absorb further subsidies could affect investor perceptions of the predictability of the utility’s regulated returns. TNB operates under Malaysia’s Incentive Based Regulation framework, which is intended to provide a structured mechanism governing electricity tariffs, costs and regulated returns. For investors, the issue therefore extends beyond the RM120 million to RM150 million estimated impact this year. CIMB Securities said continued cost absorption beyond 2026 could raise concerns about how consistently costs and returns would be treated under the regulatory framework. For households, meanwhile, the higher 800 kWh threshold extends protection from the specified electricity charges to almost one million more residential users. The balance between shielding consumers from higher electricity costs and maintaining the financial predictability of the regulated utility could consequently remain an important issue if fuel costs stay elevated into 2027.

title: 'Stronger MyCC Powers Put Competition Compliance Higher On Governance Agenda, CIMB Report
body: 'Competition compliance is set to become a more important corporate governance and ESG consideration for Malaysian companies as the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) gains stronger enforcement powers, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest Malaysia strategy report, CIMB said the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026, passed by the Dewan Rakyat on July 6, significantly broadens MyCC’s enforcement toolkit. As of the report dated Sept 15, CIMB noted that the amendments had yet to be gazetted. Parliament records confirm the Bill was passed on July 6.  The research house said the changes strengthen MyCC’s powers through new settlement mechanisms, whistleblower protection and rewards, and expanded authority to compel companies to provide information during market reviews.  Companies admitting liability after receiving a proposed decision may, according to CIMB’s account of the amendments, negotiate settlements with penalties potentially reduced by up to 40%.  CIMB said MyCC’s enforcement priorities remain focused on cartels, abuse of dominance, government procurement, food supply chains and digital markets, with the commission increasingly evolving from a traditional enforcement body into a broader economic regulator.  Cartels remain the main enforcement priority, particularly in food supply chains and public procurement. MyCC has also increased scrutiny of sectors affecting household living costs and industries where bid-rigging risks are higher.  The report highlighted the chicken feed cartel case as an example of more sophisticated enforcement. MyCC imposed RM415.5 million in total penalties across five companies, its largest competition penalty to date, after finding coordinated price increases between January 2020 and June 2022. The Competition Appeal Tribunal upheld the RM415.5 million decision in February 2026.  Digital markets are also emerging as a major regulatory frontier. MyCC’s review covers mobile operating and payment systems, e-commerce marketplaces, digital advertising, online travel agencies and data privacy, reflecting growing scrutiny of platforms that act as “gatekeepers” between businesses and consumers. MyCC’s official digital economy review identifies the same five areas and 34 competition, market and regulatory issues.  CIMB said competition compliance should increasingly be treated alongside anti-corruption policies, whistleblower mechanisms, board oversight and corporate ethics under the governance pillar of ESG.  It expects Malaysian companies, particularly those operating in concentrated industries, government procurement or sectors with extensive interaction among competitors, to increase investment in board oversight, employee training and formal competition compliance programmes.  While stronger enforcement could increase compliance costs and regulatory scrutiny in the near term, CIMB believes the longer-term impact should be positive for Malaysia’s capital markets by improving market integrity, corporate governance and investor confidence.  The research house does not expect competition enforcement to materially alter sector investment cases in the near term, but said governance standards are likely to become a more important differentiator as Malaysia’s competition regime matures.

title: 'CIMB Completes Malaysia’s First Tokenised Sukuk Settlement Using Tokenised Deposits
body: 'CIMB Group Holdings Bhd has completed a pilot to test the settlement of tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits in a controlled environment, paving the way for broader applications enabled by blockchain technology. These potential applications include instant, or atomic, settlement for cross-border transactions, as well as the democratisation of investment assets — such as enabling bonds to be sold in smaller amounts that retail investors can more easily afford. The pilot was carried out through CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd in connection with a RM1.68 billion issuance under CIMB Islamic’s existing RM10 billion senior sukuk wakalah programme, with tenors of five, seven, 10 and 15 years. Of the total issuance, RM1.38 billion was issued in tokenised form and subscribed to by 12 institutional investors, while the remaining RM300 million was issued as a traditional sukuk. The order book was covered 1.73 times, with the pricing date set at Aug 19 and settlement completed on Aug 27, according to Sylvia Wong, regional head of tokenisation at CIMB Group Wholesale Banking. The key distinction between CIMB’s pilot and an earlier pilot conducted by Khazanah Nasional Bhd lies in how settlement occurred. CIMB’s pilot involved settling both the tokenised sukuk and tokenised deposits, meaning the financial asset and the cash were both settled on-chain — though the tokens mirror legal records that continue to exist within the traditional system. A tokenised deposit refers to a bank deposit recorded as a digital token on a blockchain, effectively representing commercial bank money in digital form. In contrast, Khazanah’s tokenised sukuk, which settled in mid-May, was paid for using fiat currency, or the ringgit, through traditional payment rails rather than blockchain. In that case, only the financial asset was settled on-chain, while the cash portion moved through conventional channels. “For our pilot, we created tokenised deposits to settle the tokenised sukuk, so both of these settlements are on the blockchain,” Wong said, adding that the blockchain used for the settlement is called CIMB Blockchain Connect. The digital asset custodian (DAC) involved in the pilot — the entity responsible for safeguarding clients’ tokenised assets — is not among the two DACs currently registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC). “For this pilot, we cleared with the SC that a DAC licence is not required. We just need the ability to custodise these assets and the deposits,” Wong said during a press conference. What It Means for Ordinary People Wong explained that the central feature of the pilot is atomic settlement, where a buyer’s money and a seller’s asset change hands at exactly the same instant. She noted, however, that this concept holds limited relevance for individual consumers, who can already transfer and settle smaller sums instantly through existing payment infrastructure such as DuitNow. Settlement remains far from instantaneous in the institutional market, though. When large sums of money are sent overseas — for purposes such as funding a child’s education — the process can take several days as funds move through traditional channels involving multiple banks. “Now, with blockchain technology, if everyone is on the same blockchain, it happens literally instantaneously,” she said. The pilot nonetheless follows a “digital twin” approach, meaning the on-chain token mirrors traditional legal records rather than replacing them entirely; the process is therefore not conducted wholly on-chain. “The technological capability [for atomic settlement] is there, but are we ready to go [completely] instantaneous? We may not be ready just yet. Imagine, it is fine if it is RM100, but it is a different story if the amount is RM100 million, for a bank. Banks are looking for less friction, but not frictionless for now,” she said. Adopting a digital twin model means banks such as CIMB are investing in testing tokenised solutions through blockchain technology, even as traditional legal records and processes continue to run in parallel — meaning cost savings have yet to materialise. However, as more processes shift on-chain in the years ahead, banking operations could become faster and more efficient, while tokenisation could also help democratise asset classes by making them more accessible to retail investors. Making Financial Markets More Efficient According to a press release, the pilot was carried out as part of CIMB’s participation in Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, which offers a controlled environment for financial institutions to test new digital asset applications. CIMB has also been engaging with the SC on the broader development of tokenised capital market products. The completion of the pilot was announced at Menara CIMB in Kuala Lumpur, at an event attended by Finance Minister II Senator Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said the pilot demonstrates how Malaysia can build on its established strengths in Islamic finance and capital markets as financial infrastructure becomes increasingly digital. “Malaysia has developed deep capabilities in both Islamic finance and the capital markets. The next step is to ensure that these strengths continue to evolve alongside changes in technology and the way financial transactions are conducted. This pilot is important because it moves tokenisation beyond theory and tests how digital financial assets and commercial bank money can work together in a controlled environment. The objective is not digitalisation for its own sake, but to explore whether technology can make financial markets more efficient, transparent and connected while preserving strong standards of governance, investor protection and shariah compliance,” he said. Novan Amirudin, group chief executive officer of CIMB Group, said the pilot provided the bank and regulators with practical insights into the operational, legal and regulatory requirements involved in tokenised financial transactions. “This pilot allows us to test how tokenised financial assets can operate alongside existing market infrastructure and, importantly, how tokenised deposits can be used for settlement. The potential benefits are practical. Greater automation and faster settlement could reduce friction in financial transactions, improve liquidity management and increase capital efficiency. The experience gained from this pilot will help us assess how these capabilities can be developed further in Malaysia and, potentially, across regional and cross-border applications,” he said. Beyond Technology: Partnership and Integration During the press conference, Ahmad Shahriman Mohamad Shariff, CEO of Group Islamic Banking, CIMB, said an equally significant achievement of the pilot was persuading major fund management firms and government agencies to build the infrastructure required to settle CIMB’s tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits. “If they were to choose, it is easier for them to settle [with cash] in fiat [currency], as that’s business as usual for them. But in order to join the pilot, they have to set up their own infrastructure. While we are trying to encourage people to explore [tokenisation] and onboard them, there’s a fair amount of work on their side [to be completed] as well. And we are very glad and happy to see the responses. It was well-received,” he said.

Adopting a digital twin model means banks such as CIMB are investing in testing tokenised solutions through blockchain technology, even as traditional legal records and processes continue to run in parallel — meaning cost savings have yet to materialise. However, as more processes shift on-chain in the years ahead, banking operations could become faster and more efficient, while tokenisation could also help democratise asset classes by making them more accessible to retail investors. Making Financial Markets More Efficient According to a press release, the pilot was carried out as part of CIMB’s participation in Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, which offers a controlled environment for financial institutions to test new digital asset applications. CIMB has also been engaging with the SC on the broader development of tokenised capital market products. The completion of the pilot was announced at Menara CIMB in Kuala Lumpur, at an event attended by Finance Minister II Senator Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said the pilot demonstrates how Malaysia can build on its established strengths in Islamic finance and capital markets as financial infrastructure becomes increasingly digital. “Malaysia has developed deep capabilities in both Islamic finance and the capital markets. The next step is to ensure that these strengths continue to evolve alongside changes in technology and the way financial transactions are conducted. This pilot is important because it moves tokenisation beyond theory and tests how digital financial assets and commercial bank money can work together in a controlled environment. The objective is not digitalisation for its own sake, but to explore whether technology can make financial markets more efficient, transparent and connected while preserving strong standards of governance, investor protection and shariah compliance,” he said. Novan Amirudin, group chief executive officer of CIMB Group, said the pilot provided the bank and regulators with practical insights into the operational, legal and regulatory requirements involved in tokenised financial transactions. “This pilot allows us to test how tokenised financial assets can operate alongside existing market infrastructure and, importantly, how tokenised deposits can be used for settlement. The potential benefits are practical. Greater automation and faster settlement could reduce friction in financial transactions, improve liquidity management and increase capital efficiency. The experience gained from this pilot will help us assess how these capabilities can be developed further in Malaysia and, potentially, across regional and cross-border applications,” he said. Beyond Technology: Partnership and Integration During the press conference, Ahmad Shahriman Mohamad Shariff, CEO of Group Islamic Banking, CIMB, said an equally significant achievement of the pilot was persuading major fund management firms and government agencies to build the infrastructure required to settle CIMB’s tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits. “If they were to choose, it is easier for them to settle [with cash] in fiat [currency], as that’s business as usual for them. But in order to join the pilot, they have to set up their own infrastructure. While we are trying to encourage people to explore [tokenisation] and onboard them, there’s a fair amount of work on their side [to be completed] as well. And we are very glad and happy to see the responses. It was well-received,” he said.

title: 'Bomba’s Fire Safety Manager Mandate for 9,451 Buildings Puts Compliance Demand in Focus for Unique Fire
body: 'Malaysia’s move to make building owners directly accountable for fire safety is set to widen the compliance market for fire protection suppliers, placing Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) among the companies positioned to benefit. From 1 April 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM) and a Fire Safety Officer (FSO), and to establish a Fire Safety Organisation at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement is in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025. Nor Hisham said any building inspected over the next one to two years that is required to hold a Fire Certificate will have to put the new structure in place. He was speaking after launching the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur on 6 October 2026, where the first cohort of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs received their certificates. A key change lies in how Fire Certificates will be renewed. Going forward, JBPM will assess annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs for certificate renewal, instead of physically inspecting every building each year. JBPM currently has 13 registered training providers and has issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. Compliance shifts to building owners The framework transfers day-to-day fire safety responsibility from the authorities to building owners and their certified in-house personnel. Under the programme, FSMs undergo a five-day course covering building inspections, evacuation planning, reporting and maintenance, while FSOs complete a three-day technical course. With a certified FSM accountable for an annual report that underpins Fire Certificate renewal, building owners are expected to place greater emphasis on keeping fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, sprinkler systems, detection and alarm devices and suppression systems in working order. This points to steadier demand for equipment replacement, servicing and refilling across the 9,451 designated premises, which include high-occupancy and high-risk buildings. Unique Fire, established in 1997 and headquartered in Shah Alam, Selangor, assembles, manufactures and distributes active fire protection systems, equipment and accessories for the built environment. Its range spans hand portable fire extinguishers, fire hose reels, hydrant and sprinkler systems, wet and dry riser systems, fire detection and alarm devices, and fire suppression systems including wet chemical and carbon dioxide systems. The Group markets products under its own Unique, Unique227, Yama and Commander brands alongside third-party brands such as Kidde, and also provides fire protection equipment servicing and dry chemical fire extinguisher refilling machines. The Group has already identified the amended Act as a demand driver. For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Unique Fire’s revenue rose 6.2% to RM114.7 million, supported by stronger assembly and distribution sales, particularly of fire suppression systems. Executive Director Marcus Liew said the core fire protection business continued to grow amid a supportive regulatory environment, backed by enforcement of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 and project rollouts under the 13th Malaysia Plan, and that the Group expects sustained demand driven by regulatory compliance requirements and ongoing contract awards. The Group is also extending its reach beyond Malaysia through Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, a 60:40 joint venture with Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd to manufacture and supply fire sprinklers, with Shanghai Mosafe providing technical support towards Underwriters Laboratories (UL) certification. With the FSM and FSO requirement taking effect in less than six months, the new compliance regime is set to move fire safety from a once-a-year inspection exercise to a continuous obligation for building owners, a shift that plays directly into Unique Fire’s product and service offering.

title: 'VIB hoàn tất khoản vay quốc tế 285 triệu USD trong kế hoạch 1 tỉ USD
body: 'Ngân hàng Quốc Tế Việt Nam (VIB) đã hoàn tất khoản vay hợp vốn trị giá 285 triệu USD từ chín định chế tài chính tại châu Á.  Chi phí vốn cạnh tranh, mở rộng đối tác quốc tế  Giao dịch trên được đồng thu xếp bởi United Overseas Bank Limited (UOB), Maybank Securities Pte. Ltd. và Cathay United Bank Co., Ltd. Ba ngân hàng này cùng China Construction Bank Corporation giữ vai trò ngân hàng thu xếp chính và dựng sổ. Năm định chế tài chính quốc tế khác cũng tham gia cấp vốn. Khoản vay được giải ngân thành ba đợt trong năm 2026.  Với kỳ hạn 3 năm, chi phí vốn của khoản vay thấp hơn khoảng 30 điểm cơ bản so với khoản vay hợp vốn trước đó. Nguồn vốn này bổ sung kỳ hạn trung hạn, đồng thời giúp ngân hàng đa dạng hóa cơ cấu huy động.  Giao dịch có sự tham gia của bảy đối tác từng thực hiện các khoản vay hợp vốn trước đây và hai đối tác mới. Việc có thêm đối tác mới cho thấy ngân hàng tiếp tục mở rộng quan hệ với các định chế tài chính quốc tế trong bối cảnh thị trường tài chính toàn cầu còn nhiều biến động.  Bà Lee Chin Hwoi, Giám đốc Bộ phận Tài trợ Vốn vay, Khối Ngân hàng Đầu tư Tập đoàn UOB, cho biết giao dịch thể hiện sự hợp tác giữa hai bên và kỳ vọng vào triển vọng phát triển dài hạn của ngân hàng. Trong bối cảnh các định chế tài chính trong khu vực đang tìm cách đa dạng hóa nguồn vốn và tăng cường khả năng chống chịu của bảng cân đối, UOB tiếp tục kết nối khách hàng với nguồn vốn toàn cầu và các cơ hội tăng trưởng bền vững.  Chủ động nguồn vốn quốc tế cho chiến lược tăng trưởng  Khoản vay 285 triệu USD nằm trong kế hoạch huy động 1 tỉ USD nguồn vốn trung và dài hạn từ thị trường quốc tế của VIB trong năm 2026. Ngân hàng đang tiếp tục làm việc với các đối tác để triển khai những giao dịch tiếp theo.  Tổng số dư vốn huy động nước ngoài, gồm cả ngắn hạn và trung, dài hạn, hiện đạt 1,6 tỉ USD và dự kiến tăng lên 2 tỉ USD vào năm 2027.  Ông Hàn Ngọc Vũ, Tổng giám đốc VIB, cho biết ngân hàng tập trung vào chi phí vốn, kỳ hạn và sự đa dạng của các đối tác trong kế hoạch mở rộng nguồn vốn quốc tế trong năm nay. Việc bổ sung các nguồn vốn mới nhằm tăng tính chủ động trong quản trị thanh khoản và cân đối kỳ hạn giữa nguồn vốn với nhu cầu sử dụng vốn.  Nguồn vốn trung và dài hạn từ thị trường quốc tế cũng giúp đa dạng hóa các kênh huy động bên cạnh tiền gửi khách hàng và nguồn vốn trong nước.  Chi phí vốn cạnh tranh giúp ngân hàng chủ động hơn trong quản lý chi phí và cơ cấu nguồn vốn, từ đó hỗ trợ hiệu quả hoạt động và phát triển các giải pháp tín dụng phù hợp với nhu cầu khách hàng.  Nguồn vốn từ khoản vay hợp vốn vừa hoàn tất góp phần đáp ứng nhu cầu tín dụng của khách hàng cá nhân, doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa cùng các khách hàng doanh nghiệp khác, phù hợp với định hướng kinh doanh và quản trị rủi ro của ngân hàng.  Trong quý II-2026, ngân hàng triển khai chương trình tín dụng ưu đãi quy mô 15.000 tỉ đồng, với lãi suất từ 8%/năm, dành cho doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa, doanh nghiệp sản xuất, xuất nhập khẩu và các đơn vị tham gia chuỗi cung ứng.  Với khách hàng cá nhân, ngân hàng cung cấp các khoản vay mua nhà với lựa chọn cố định lãi suất đến 5 năm, giúp người vay chủ động tính toán chi phí tài chính.  Bên cạnh việc mở rộng nguồn vốn quốc tế, ngân hàng tiếp tục củng cố vốn tự có. Vốn điều lệ đạt 37.354 tỉ đồng sau khi hoàn tất phát hành hơn 323 triệu cổ phiếu để trả cổ tức với tỉ lệ 9,5%. Đến cuối quý II-2026, dư nợ tín dụng đạt gần 400.000 tỉ đồng, trong khi lợi nhuận trước thuế 6 tháng đầu năm đạt hơn 5.180 tỉ đồng.  Việc tăng vốn tự có và bổ sung nguồn vốn trung, dài hạn giúp ngân hàng có thêm nguồn lực đáp ứng nhu cầu tín dụng, đồng thời tăng khả năng chủ động trong quản trị thanh khoản và kiểm soát rủi ro.  Đọc bài gốc tại đây.

title: 'Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Twentytwo13
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Coaches of Premier League hockey teams scheduled to play on Deepavali day are happy they will now battle it out on different dates, as the Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) repeats its 2018 scheduling boo-boo. Two matches – Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces Hockey Team and TNB Thunderbolts versus Maybank – were originally scheduled for Nov 8, the day Deepavali is celebrated in Malaysia. However, the matches will now be rescheduled, much to the delight of TNB Thunderbolts and Terengganu Hockey Team. Mohd Harfizi Baharom of Terengganu said he had been informed that the match against the soldiers would now be played on Nov 9. “It is good that we will not be playing on such an auspicious day. It gives those celebrating the festival time to spend with their families,” Mohd Harfizi told Twentytwo13. “Several of our players have only just returned from the Asian Games. Unfortunately, there is a packed international calendar and the national team will be off to the Asian Champions Trophy from Oct 27 to Nov 5. “As such, having an extra day to prepare for the match against the Armed Forces is welcome. We are third in the standings, but have not given up hope of winning the title. One day can make a difference.” However, the new dates are not reflected on MHC’s website as of publication time. TNB Thunderbolts coach Nor Saiful Zaini, who is also the national junior coach, said he has yet to receive official notice of the new date. “I know it is not easy for MHC to juggle the calendar, but we shouldn’t play on Deepavali or any other religious festival. I am waiting for confirmation regarding the change of date,” said Nor Saiful. In 2018, the Razak Cup was initially scheduled from Nov 3-11, with Deepavali falling on Nov 6 that year. After protests from teams, especially Negeri Sembilan, which threatened to pull out of the tournament, MHC eventually brought forward the tournament to Oct 26-Nov 3. The repeat of the episode raised eyebrows, as those in charge of scheduling the league should have been fully aware of the festive seasons in the country. Meanwhile, Nor Saiful said he would have his hands full as the national juniors will compete in the Sultan of Johor Cup (Oct 17-24), followed by the Murugappa Gold Cup (Oct 25-Nov 4) in India. Nor Saiful was instrumental in recently guiding the national team to next year’s Junior World Cup. “I will need to juggle my team selection carefully, as we have to consider the league matches as well as the two major tournaments. “Some of the teams may be reluctant to release their junior players, but on the bright side, I have the chance to test more players in Johor and India,” he added.

title: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst
body: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. Still, 10 out of 12 research houses tracked by Bloomberg recommend investors to “buy” Axis REIT and two are on “hold” calls. The average target price is RM2.22, a potential gain of up to 21% in the next 12 months from current price of RM1.84. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Phoenix Distributing Expands Custom Home Builder Outreach with Addition of Dawn Lohr
body: 'Oct 6, 2026 Charleston-based residential fire protection company welcomes Dawn Lohr as Builder Partnerships Manager to strengthen relationships with custom home builders throughout the Lowcountry. Charleston, United States, October 6, 2026 -- Phoenix Distributing, LLC, a residential fire protection company specializing in residential fire sprinkler solutions, today announced that Dawn Lohr has joined the company as Builder Partnerships Manager. In her new role, Lohr will focus on developing and supporting relationships with custom home builders, developers and other residential construction professionals throughout the Charleston area and surrounding Lowcountry. As Phoenix Distributing continues expanding its residential fire sprinkler capabilities and builder-focused services, Lohr will serve as an important connection between the company and the residential construction community. Her responsibilities will include builder outreach, relationship development, educational initiatives and helping construction professionals better understand the planning and coordination involved in incorporating residential fire sprinkler systems into new homes. Dawn Lohr, Builder Partnerships Manager at Phoenix Distributing, works with a custom home builder on residential fire protection planning in the South Carolina Lowcountry. "Residential fire protection works best when it is considered early in the construction process and coordinated closely with the builder," said Phoenix Distributing CEO Charlie Stewart. "Dawn's ability to build relationships and communicate effectively makes her an excellent fit for what we're building at Phoenix. We want builders to view us as a long-term residential fire protection partner rather than simply another subcontractor." Lohr is based in Charleston and holds a degree in Marketing from Loyola University Maryland. She brings an entrepreneurial background and extensive experience building relationships, communicating with diverse audiences and developing community connections. In addition to her business career, Lohr is a published author and speaker. "I am excited to join Phoenix Distributing and have the opportunity to work directly with builders throughout the Lowcountry," said Lohr. "Residential fire sprinklers are an important part of protecting families and homes, and I look forward to helping builders better understand the solutions, resources and support Phoenix can provide." Phoenix Distributing works with custom home builders, developers, contractors, plumbing professionals and other industry partners to provide residential fire sprinkler expertise from project planning and design through supply, installation and inspection support. The company's approach is designed to make residential fire protection easier to coordinate within the home-building process while supporting applicable project and code requirements. The addition of Lohr comes as Phoenix increases its outreach to custom home builders throughout coastal South Carolina, including the greater Charleston area and communities extending along the Lowcountry coast. About Phoenix Distributing, LLC Phoenix Distributing, LLC specializes in residential fire protection solutions with decades of industry experience in residential fire sprinkler design, supply, installation and support. Through its specialized brands and operating companies, Phoenix provides builders and industry professionals with an integrated resource for residential fire sprinkler systems, technical expertise, education and field support. Phoenix is committed to advancing residential fire protection through professional expertise, education, innovation and strong partnerships with the building community. For more information, visit PhoenixHomeFireSprinklers.com. title: '默迪卡118发展完成 PNB放眼经常收入达6亿 | e南洋
body: '（吉隆坡5日讯）国民投资机构（PNB）子公司PNB Merdeka Ventures私人有限公司（PNBMV）预计，随着默迪卡118（Merdeka 118）发展项目完成，中期每年可取得约5亿至6亿令吉的经常性收入。 根据大马评级机构MARC点出，默迪卡118办公楼约70%的空间已转租。PNBMV已将办公楼整体以“三重净租赁”方式出租予母公司PNB，因此可降低办公楼空置率及大部分房地产相关成本风险。 默迪卡118办公楼拥有约160万平方尺净可出租面积，其中约40%，即33层，已转租予马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主板金融股），约20%出租予PNB，另约10%出租予其他租户。 MARC预计，办公楼出租率未来5年可提高至约90%，每年净房地产收入料达1亿3700万令吉。 与此同时，MARC已确认PNBMV总值60亿令吉的默迪卡伊斯兰债券获AAAIS评级，展望稳定。 该评级与PNB的AAA／稳定企业信用评级一致，主要受到PNB提供无条件及不可撤销滚动担保的支持，以弥补伊斯兰债券本金及利润支付的任何短缺。 至于预计下月开业的7层楼零售商场，目前已有或正在洽谈的租赁协议覆盖约81%的75万324平方尺净可出租面积，指示性平均租金为每平方尺11.92令吉。 值得注意的是，马银行已正式进驻默迪卡118，而这座吉隆坡地标也已易名为“马银行默迪卡大楼”（Menara Merdeka Maybank）。

title: 'PNB unit eyes up to RM600mil recurring annual income from Merdeka 118
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd expects recurring income from the completed Merdeka 118 development to reach RM500 million-RM600 million a year over the medium term. About 70 per cent of the project's office space is already sub-leased, according to MARC Ratings. The firm said the office component is fully leased to parent Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) under a triple-net master lease. This shields PNB Merdeka from occupancy and most property-related cost risks. MARC said about 70 per cent of the tower's 1.6 million sq ft net lettable area (NLA) has been sub-leased. This comprises 40 per cent, or 33 floors, sub-leased to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), 20 per cent to PNB and about 10 per cent to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90 per cent over the next five years, with the office tower projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137 million. MARC has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka's RM6 billion Merdeka sukuk Wakalah with a stable outlook. The rating aligns with PNB's AAA/Stable corporate credit rating, supported by PNB's unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee covering any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk. MARC said for the seven-storey retail mall, which is expected to open next month, lease agreements covering 81 per cent of its 750,324 sq ft NLA have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental of RM11.92 per sq ft. The Merdeka 118 development, near Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, has incurred RM10.6 billion in development costs to date. The cost was largely funded by two earlier sukuk programmes that have since been restructured into the current rated issuance. The planned residential components are expected to add another RM1.4 billion in development costs, to be funded through a mix of borrowings and equity injections. Two residential towers, with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2 billion, are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027, while a serviced apartment project has an estimated GDV of RM745 million. MARC said these residential and serviced apartment components remain exposed to demand risk amid competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. PNB Merdeka is wholly owned by PNB and was established to undertake the Merdeka 118 project. This includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a 17-floor luxury hotel, a three-floor observation deck and the upcoming retail mall. PNB Merdeka is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both designated National Heritage sites.

title: '马股闭市微升0.88点 银行股撑大局 - 财经 - 即时财经
body: '马股闭市微升0.88点 银行股撑大局 （吉隆坡5日讯）部分银行股和消费股趁低吸纳，抵销杨忠礼双雄走软的冲击，富时综指周一开高走高，最终全日微升0.88点。  富时综指周一上半天曾升至1640.46点，上扬9.59点，随后回吐涨幅，午休上升1.84点，至1632.71点。 午盘之后虽然守住升势，但尾盘几乎回吐涨幅，最终微升0.88点，以1631.75点挂收。不过，全场下跌股超过上升股，有598只下跌股、564只上升股，另有524只平盘。 30只综指成分股中，有14只上升、13只下跌和3只没有起落。上涨的综指股包括国际船务(MISC,3816,主板交通物流组)起17仙，至7令吉70仙；99迷你超市(99SMART,5326,主板消费产品服务组)起6仙，至3令吉12仙。 部分银行股走稳，收盘时，丰隆银行(HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组)涨24仙，收报22令吉88仙；大马银行(AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组)起11仙，收于6令吉50仙；联昌集团(CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组)涨8仙，收报7令吉73仙；大众银行(PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)起5仙，至4令吉71仙。不过，马来亚银行(MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)则下挫2仙，至10令吉。 另一边厢，杨忠礼电力(YTLPOWR,6742,主板公用事业组)下跌14仙，收于5令吉54仙；杨忠礼机构(YTL,4677,主板公用事业组)降8仙，至2令吉16仙。 反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上升19.78点，至12190.35点，创业板指数也涨77.15点，收报5606.61点。 其他马股指数普遍上涨，科技指数上涨1.74%，为全场最出色，另外，建筑指数则下跌1.46%，是全场最差。 全场成交量达到47亿8168万1200股，总值28亿8516万8841令吉。 全球股市方面，美国非农就业数据低于预期，降低联储局加息的概率，亚洲股市全面上涨，收盘时，台湾加权指数急升2.55%：日本日经指数大涨2.40%，菲律宾马尼拉综指上扬2.03%；印尼雅加达综指起1.36%，新加坡、泰国和香港股市也上涨少于1%。 韩国和中国股市今天休市。 美元指数回升，马币兑美元和新元周一双双走低。 根据《彭博社》行情，马币兑美元全日游走于4.0778至4.0885，截至下午5时报4.0875，低于上周五的4.0820；马币兑新元全日在3.1865至3.1950之间徘徊，截至下午5时挂3.1941，上周五收于3.1922。 大豆油价格上涨，带动大马衍生产品交易所12月指标期货上涨28令吉，至每公吨4563令吉。  热门新闻 百格视频

'马股闭市微升0.88点 银行股撑大局 （吉隆坡5日讯）部分银行股和消费股趁低吸纳，抵销杨忠礼双雄走软的冲击，富时综指周一开高走高，最终全日微升0.88点。  富时综指周一上半天曾升至1640.46点，上扬9.59点，随后回吐涨幅，午休上升1.84点，至1632.71点。 午盘之后虽然守住升势，但尾盘几乎回吐涨幅，最终微升0.88点，以1631.75点挂收。不过，全场下跌股超过上升股，有598只下跌股、564只上升股，另有524只平盘。 30只综指成分股中，有14只上升、13只下跌和3只没有起落。上涨的综指股包括国际船务(MISC,3816,主板交通物流组)起17仙，至7令吉70仙；99迷你超市(99SMART,5326,主板消费产品服务组)起6仙，至3令吉12仙。 部分银行股走稳，收盘时，丰隆银行(HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组)涨24仙，收报22令吉88仙；大马银行(AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组)起11仙，收于6令吉50仙；联昌集团(CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组)涨8仙，收报7令吉73仙；大众银行(PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)起5仙，至4令吉71仙。不过，马来亚银行(MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)则下挫2仙，至10令吉。 另一边厢，杨忠礼电力(YTLPOWR,6742,主板公用事业组)下跌14仙，收于5令吉54仙；杨忠礼机构(YTL,4677,主板公用事业组)降8仙，至2令吉16仙。 反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上升19.78点，至12190.35点，创业板指数也涨77.15点，收报5606.61点。 其他马股指数普遍上涨，科技指数上涨1.74%，为全场最出色，另外，建筑指数则下跌1.46%，是全场最差。 全场成交量达到47亿8168万1200股，总值28亿8516万8841令吉。 全球股市方面，美国非农就业数据低于预期，降低联储局加息的概率，亚洲股市全面上涨，收盘时，台湾加权指数急升2.55%：日本日经指数大涨2.40%，菲律宾马尼拉综指上扬2.03%；印尼雅加达综指起1.36%，新加坡、泰国和香港股市也上涨少于1%。 韩国和中国股市今天休市。 美元指数回升，马币兑美元和新元周一双双走低。 根据《彭博社》行情，马币兑美元全日游走于4.0778至4.0885，截至下午5时报4.0875，低于上周五的4.0820；马币兑新元全日在3.1865至3.1950之间徘徊，截至下午5时挂3.1941，上周五收于3.1922。 大豆油价格上涨，带动大马衍生产品交易所12月指标期货上涨28令吉，至每公吨4563令吉。  热门新闻 百格视频

title: '市场人气低迷拖累，马股综指周一表现滞后，收盘微幅走高
body: '受地缘政治风险和通胀风险持续引发的担忧，以及股市人气低迷的拖累，马股综合指数周一表现滞后，未能跟上区域市场的乐观情绪，收盘仅微幅走高。 截至下午闭市，综合指数涨0.88点或0.05%，至1,631.75点。 市场整体表现平衡，全场上涨股564只，下跌股58只，524只平盘，另1063只股无交易。全天成交量47.81亿股，总成交额28.85亿令吉。 综指成分股涨跌互见，雀巢（NESTLE，4707，主板消费股）涨48仙至90.00令吉，马国际船务（MISC，3816，主板交通与物流股）涨17仙至7.70令吉，国油气体（PETGAS，6033，主板公用事业股）涨10仙至17.30令吉。 下跌股，吉隆坡甲洞（KLK，2445，主板种植股）跌14仙至20.86令吉，杨忠礼电力（YTLPOWR，6742，主板公用事业股）跌14仙至5.54令吉，金务大（GAMUDA，5398，主板建筑股）跌11仙至4.99令吉。 银行股，马银行（MAYBANK，1155）跌2仙至10.00令吉，大众银行（PBBANK，1295）涨5仙4.71令吉，联昌国际（CIMB，1023）涨8仙至7.73令吉，兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066）涨3仙至7.46令吉，丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819）涨24仙至22.88令吉，大马银行（AMBANK，1015）涨11仙至6.50令吉。 热门股方面，Zetrix AI（ZETRIX，0138，主板科技股）跌5仙至6.5仙，威铖（VS，6963，主板工业股）涨3仙至32仙，捷硕科技（JAKS，4723, 主板建筑股）跌1仙至17仙，力扬科技（EFORCE，0065，主板科技股）跌4仙至17仙，顶级手套（TOPGLOV，7113，主板保健股）涨2.5仙至78.5仙。 其他重要股项，马太平洋（MPI，3867，主板科技股）涨1.00令吉至43.40令吉，科艺集团（KGB，0151，主板工业股）涨49仙至9.12令吉；峇都加湾（BKAWAN，1899，主板种植股）跌1.48令吉至18.98令吉，联合种植（UTDPLT，2089，主板种植股）跌32仙至31.06令吉。 亚太主要股指，新加坡海峡时报指数起 0.52% 至 5,664.34 点，香港恒生指数起 0.28% 至 24,040.34 点，日本日经指255数起 2.40% 至 69,946.86 点。韩国开天节补假休市，中国股市则国庆长假期休市。 The post 市场人气低迷拖累，马股综指周一表现滞后，收盘微幅走高 appeared first on 股票消息.

title: 'Malaysia steps up healthcare push in Cambodia
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is stepping up efforts to attract Cambodian healthcare travellers, with Maybank (Cambodia) Plc and the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC) showcasing 14 Malaysian hospitals in Phnom Penh. In a statement, Maybank Cambodia chief executive officer and country head Rath Sophoan said the event aimed to make it easier for Cambodian families to make informed healthcare decisions while incorporating financial planning into the process. "MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 was designed around a simple question: how can we make it easier for Cambodian families to take a confident next step when health matters? "The event connected families with the people, expertise and options behind Malaysia's healthcare institutions, while bringing financial readiness into the same conversation," he said. MH WellFest Cambodia 2026, held at Borey Peng Huoth Eco Park, drew about 2,000 visitors and almost 800 runners, providing Cambodian families with direct access to Malaysian healthcare providers and specialists. The two-day event, endorsed by the Malaysian Embassy in Phnom Penh, highlighted Malaysia's healthcare capabilities, including health screening, preventive care, specialist services and treatment options. MHTC chief executive officer Datuk Suriaghandi Suppiah said healthcare travel depended on trust and confidence in the quality of care available. title: 'Bursa once said no to crypto. LIDAC26 showed how far Malaysia has come since
body: 'Back in 2024, I wrote a column lamenting Bursa Malaysia’s decision to keep bitcoin and other crypto assets off its new multi-asset exchange, asking whether it might go down as Bursa’s biggest blunder.  Two Thursday’s ago, I spent the better part of a day at M Resort & Hotel in Kuala Lumpur listening to regulators, bankers and fund managers talk about digital assets not as a fringe curiosity, but as the plumbing for the next generation of our capital market. What a difference two years makes.  The event was LIDAC26, the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference, now in its second edition. Luno, one of the digital asset exchanges registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), pitched it squarely at institutions rather than retail punters, and the room reflected that.  The main hall kept the headline sessions flowing from 9.30am, four breakout sessions ran in smaller rooms alongside it through the day, and the session screens I saw all carried a QR code for live audience questions.  Attendees could even earn seven continuing professional development (CPD) points, the credits licensed finance professionals collect to keep their qualifications current, which tells you exactly who the organisers were courting.  So what were the big takeaways? Three stood out.  1. Stablecoins are the real story  Luno chief executive James Lanigan opened proceedings with a slide that cut through a lot of the noise. By Luno’s count, about RM1.43 trillion worth of assets had been tokenised, or recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain, by the first quarter of 2026, and roughly RM1.26 trillion of that was stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the US dollar.  That’s right. Around 90% of all tokenised assets are, in effect, digital cash, the overwhelming majority of which is tokenised USD, cementing it as not only the world’s reserve currency but the currency of choice in the budding crypto economy.  Lanigan’s framing was that the industry had moved from speculation, through building infrastructure, and was now firmly in its institutional era, with one of his final slides declaring that Malaysia was not a late market, but an early one.  2. The regulator wants substance, not buzzwords  The most anticipated session was that by Wong Huei Ching, the SC’s executive director of digital strategy and innovation, who laid out where Malaysia’s rules are heading.  Her message, stripped to its core, was that putting an asset on a blockchain is not innovation in itself, and that pilots need to prove their worth before the rules are rewritten.  The SC is practising what it preaches. In April, it teamed up with Khazanah Nasional, our sovereign wealth fund, to price Malaysia’s first tokenised sukuk (an Islamic bond recorded on a blockchain), a RM100 million pilot that SC chairman Mohammad Faiz Azmi said would test tokenisation’s potential “in a controlled and credible manner”.  The market she regulates is growing fast, too. Trading value on Malaysia’s licensed digital asset exchanges hit RM17.14 billion in 2025, a 23% jump from RM13.93 billion the year before, according to the SC.  3. The ringgit is going on-chain  John Ho, head of legal and financial markets at Standard Chartered, walked participants in the main hall through Bank Negara Malaysia’s growing list of experiments. These include Project Mawar, which explores a wholesale digital ringgit for banks, and the central bank’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, where Standard Chartered and Capital A are testing a ringgit stablecoin, while Maybank trials tokenised deposits.  The prize is not small. One industry estimate cited on stage, and widely reported, puts Malaysia’s tokenisation opportunity at around RM175 billion by 2030.  The tidbits  Many other speakers added flair and colour to the proceedings. Former deputy international trade and industry minister Ong Kian Ming spoke on navigating digital assets in a fragmenting global order, while Harjit Singh of HSS Advisory and Anil Puri of EY tackled a question plenty of Malaysian crypto investors have been asking for years: how exactly will all this be taxed?  My favourite, though, was a breakout billed as Malaysian builders shaping the global digital asset landscape. On one stage sat TM Lee, co-founder of CoinGecko, Matthew Tan, founder of Etherscan, and Siong Ong, co-founder of Jupiter, products used by crypto traders the world over.  CoinGecko and Etherscan were both born right here in Kuala Lumpur, and I can’t help but feel proud that some of the most widely used tools in the industry were built by Malaysians.  Siong Ong’s speaker photo on the big screen? A Pudgy Penguin, an uber popular non-fungible token (NFT) collection. In a day full of suits, it was a welcome reminder of where this industry came from.  The one glaring miss  I was, however, surprised that bitcoin, the 800-pound gorilla in the room, barely got a look-in. Bitcoin alone is worth around RM6.9 trillion today, according to CoinGecko, and together with ether, the Ethereum network’s native token, the pair make up about two-thirds of the entire crypto market.  Stablecoins, for all the stage time they got, account for a mere 10%. Despite more than a decade of relentless innovation in the industry, bitcoin still commands over half of all crypto value, and not telling that story was a missed opportunity.  So where does that leave us? The SC revised its guidelines on Mar 2 to permit digital currency exchange-traded funds (ETFs), and Bursa, the very exchange that shut crypto out of its multi-asset platform in 2024, said in March that it welcomed the listing of digital currency ETFs, and told reporters in July that it planned to add them to its line-up.  The regulator has built the framework, Khazanah has shown the plumbing can work and Bank Negara is already testing the ringgit on-chain. All that’s left is for the first digital currency ETF to actually start trading on Bursa. After all, it’s about time the exchange that once said no had something to show for its yes.

title: 'Player fatigue threatens TNB campaign as MHL resumes
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The second round of the Malaysian Hockey League (MHL) begins on Monday, and it has caused havoc for league leaders Tenaga Nasional (TNB) and their season campaign.   TNB will face the Armed Forces on Wednesday at the National Hockey Stadium in Bukit Jalil but 11 of their players will only be arriving on Monday from the Asian Games.    Malaysia were defeated 5-1 by defending champions India in the Asiad final in Nagoya on Saturday.    The first round of MHL ended on May 17 with TNB leading the standings on 19 points from six wins and a draw, followed by Maybank and Terengganu Hockey Team with 17 and 14 points respectively.

title: 'IOI Marina View secures financing
body: 'SINGAPORE: IOI Marina View, a real estate developer, has secured an Islamic term financing facility worth SG$1.73 billion (US$1.35 billion) from DBS Bank, Maybank Singapore, OCBC and UOB, according to Allen & Gledhill, which acted as the transaction counsel to the banks. The facility will be used to finance IOI Marina View’s acquisition of investment holding company MVKimi.

title: 'Doktor diperdaya bapa bekas penyanyi, polis siasat penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa
body: 'Ampang Jaya: Polis sudah membuka kertas siasatan membabitkan penipuan pelaburan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat milik seorang lelaki yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi. Ketua Polis Daerah Ampang Jaya, Asisten Komisioner Khairul Anuar Khalid berkata, mangsa, doktor swasta berusia 38 tahun pada awal 2023 bersama suaminya berurusan dengan suspek berkaitan projek Kad Prihatin Siswa yang dikaitkan dengan sebuah syarikat secara bersemuka dan melalui WhatsApp. Menurutnya, suspek memperkenalkan projek terbabit sebagai pelaburan yang membabitkan 20 buah universiti dan kira-kira 620,000 pelajar serta menjanjikan pulangan keuntungan kepada pelabur. "Mangsa membuat lima kali transaksi pembayaran dengan jumlah keseluruhan sebanyak RM300,000 ke atas nombor akaun Maybank milik suspek sepanjang 2023. "Selepas daripada itu, satu perjanjian pelaburan ditandatangani yang menyatakan pelaburan sebanyak RM300,000 dengan keuntungan sebanyak 10 peratus sebulan selama 12 bulan dan modal akan dipulangkan pada tamat tempoh perjanjian," katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini. Beliau berkata, mangsa kemudiannya didaftarkan sebagai pemegang 10 peratus saham syarikat terbabit. "Bagaimanapun, keuntungan dan dividen yang dijanjikan tidak pernah diterima. Mangsa dan suami beberapa kali meminta penjelasan, pembayaran dividen serta salinan perjanjian yang dimatikan setem, namun suspek memberikan pelbagai alasan dan gagal memberikan penyelesaian. "Siasatan dijalankan mengikut Seksyen 420 Kanun Keseksaan dan tiada tangkapan setakat ini," katanya. Harian Metro hari ini melaporkan lelaki itu meyakinkan pelabur bahawa projek Kad Prihatin Siswa membabitkan 20 universiti mampu menjana pulangan lumayan dan kononnya ingin membantu lebih ramai orang Melayu kaya sepertinya. Itu taktik seorang lelaki bergelar Datuk yang juga bapa kepada bekas penyanyi memperdayakan pasangan doktor sehingga menyebabkan kerugian RM300,000 selepas melabur sejak 2023. Malah, dia turut mendakwa berkawan dengan pegawai tertinggi kerajaan dan kononnya minit mesyuarat projek ini juga sudah dihantar ke kerajaan dengan 620,000 pelajar akan menikmati kad terbabit hasil kerjasama dengan syarikat telekomunikasi terkenal.

title: 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers
body: 'Two lawsuits filed within days of each other in late July and early August have renewed a question that matters to every investor. When financial statements rest on estimates that could go either way, what does a “clean” audit opinion actually guarantee? The liquidators of Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd are seeking at least RM1.56 billion from KPMG, alleging that unqualified opinions between FY2016 and FY2019 failed to detect revenue overstatements of up to 87%. The suit claims the misstatements would have been uncovered earlier, before the group paid RM1.795 billion in dividends, which the claim links to the alleged audit failures. Around the same time, the Sabah government, together with other plaintiffs, sued Ernst & Young for RM2.4 billion over its audits of Sabah Development Bank, alleging that EY issued unqualified opinions for years even though, according to the claim, 85.94% of the bank’s loan portfolio had been recorded as non-performing loans by FY2018. Both claims remain before the courts, and the allegations have not been tested at trial. The cases will turn on negligence and evidence. But they expose a deeper structural tension that the courts cannot resolve. There is a gap between what an audit opinion actually asserts and what investors assume it guarantees. The lawsuits concern alleged audit failures. The broader issue, however, exists even where there is no allegation of failure. To see that tension clearly, it helps to separate alleged audit failure from the routine judgements in every set of audited accounts. Serba Dinamik and Sabah Development Bank are outlier cases. The structural issue is visible in ordinary audits of Malaysia’s largest companies, whose auditors have not been accused of anything. Maybank’s FY2025 audited accounts provide one illustration. The auditors identified expected credit losses on loans, advances and financing as a Key Audit Matter (KAM). These assets represent 64.3% of the group’s total assets. The auditors stated that measuring expected credit losses (ECL) “requires the application of significant judgement and increased complexity”, involving forward looking factors, probability weighted scenarios and management overlays. They tested models, challenged assumptions and engaged credit modelling specialists. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s FY2025 statements offer another. Post employment benefit liabilities of RM13.3 billion at group level were valued using actuarial assumptions on salary increases, medical cost inflation and discount rates. The auditors “focused on this area because of the significant estimates made by management”, checked assumptions against historical data and compared discount rates to market yields with valuation experts. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. These are not presented as cases of audit failure. The system is working as designed. Yet TNB reports that a one percentage point movement in the discount rate can change its defined benefit obligation by more than RM1 billion. Maybank’s KAM similarly describes extensive audit procedures without showing investors the range of possible outcomes. The KAM explains the judgement, but not how sensitive the number may be. International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 701 requires auditors to communicate KAMs and allow them to highlight matters requiring significant auditor attention, while the opinion remains on the financial statements as a whole. But the framework is binary while uncertainty is not. Two competent valuers may reach different estimates, and a figure can be reasonable without being the only supportable answer. KAMs can therefore become lists of procedures rather than explanations of risk. Estimation uncertainty exists on a continuum while audit reporting remains categorical. The question is not whether KAMs should exist, but whether they tell investors enough about how uncertain the most consequential numbers really are. Malaysia’s Audit Oversight Board has identified “failure to sufficiently review significant risk areas and significant judgements” as a recurring enforcement concern. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) highlighted in its November 2025 statement the importance of high-quality valuation practices, appropriate use of valuation experts and rigorous audit assessment. The International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) has likewise identified accounting estimates, including fair value measurement, as an area where audit regulators have consistently found deficiencies. When auditors use KAMs to flag a valuation without qualifying the opinion, they are telling investors that the matter involved significant judgement but that the financial statements nevertheless met the requirements for an unmodified opinion. That may be technically correct for Maybank and TNB. But the Serba Dinamik case illustrates how insufficient that signal can be for investors. The concern is not simply whether auditors get the judgement wrong. Even a sound audit can leave investors unable to see how fragile a reasonable estimate may be. That is the gap the current reporting model should address. Four reforms would help. First, require sensitivity disclosure in the KAM. Auditors should disclose the reasonable range of outcomes and its impact on the financial statements. TNB’s statements already include sensitivity analysis on discount rate assumptions. This information should be connected directly to the KAM, rather than leaving investors to piece the implications together from different sections of the annual report. Second, consider graduated reporting for significant estimation uncertainty. Such reporting could signal that an estimate falls within an acceptable range but remains highly sensitive, without implying that there is a material misstatement. The existing Emphasis of Matter framework under ISA 706 could provide a starting point. Third, require independent valuation review for specified material Level 3 assets. A second valuation would provide an additional check on management bias. The auditor could assess the divergence as evidence and consider the additional data point when applying professional scepticism. Fourth, strengthen audit committee disclosure. Audit committees should disclose how they challenged management’s fair value assumptions. If the committee accepted management’s numbers without meaningful scrutiny, that should be visible to shareholders. None of these solutions are radical. Each builds on existing frameworks, including Malaysian Financial Reporting Standard 13 (MFRS 13), ISA 701, ISA 540 and Malaysia’s corporate governance code. They require recognition that the current approach to fair value auditing, while technically sound, is insufficiently transparent for the risks involved. Judgement is unavoidable. Opacity is not. 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers

'Two lawsuits filed within days of each other in late July and early August have renewed a question that matters to every investor. When financial statements rest on estimates that could go either way, what does a “clean” audit opinion actually guarantee? The liquidators of Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd are seeking at least RM1.56 billion from KPMG, alleging that unqualified opinions between FY2016 and FY2019 failed to detect revenue overstatements of up to 87%. The suit claims the misstatements would have been uncovered earlier, before the group paid RM1.795 billion in dividends, which the claim links to the alleged audit failures. Around the same time, the Sabah government, together with other plaintiffs, sued Ernst & Young for RM2.4 billion over its audits of Sabah Development Bank, alleging that EY issued unqualified opinions for years even though, according to the claim, 85.94% of the bank’s loan portfolio had been recorded as non-performing loans by FY2018. Both claims remain before the courts, and the allegations have not been tested at trial. The cases will turn on negligence and evidence. But they expose a deeper structural tension that the courts cannot resolve. There is a gap between what an audit opinion actually asserts and what investors assume it guarantees. The lawsuits concern alleged audit failures. The broader issue, however, exists even where there is no allegation of failure. To see that tension clearly, it helps to separate alleged audit failure from the routine judgements in every set of audited accounts. Serba Dinamik and Sabah Development Bank are outlier cases. The structural issue is visible in ordinary audits of Malaysia’s largest companies, whose auditors have not been accused of anything. Maybank’s FY2025 audited accounts provide one illustration. The auditors identified expected credit losses on loans, advances and financing as a Key Audit Matter (KAM). These assets represent 64.3% of the group’s total assets. The auditors stated that measuring expected credit losses (ECL) “requires the application of significant judgement and increased complexity”, involving forward looking factors, probability weighted scenarios and management overlays. They tested models, challenged assumptions and engaged credit modelling specialists. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s FY2025 statements offer another. Post employment benefit liabilities of RM13.3 billion at group level were valued using actuarial assumptions on salary increases, medical cost inflation and discount rates. The auditors “focused on this area because of the significant estimates made by management”, checked assumptions against historical data and compared discount rates to market yields with valuation experts. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. These are not presented as cases of audit failure. The system is working as designed. Yet TNB reports that a one percentage point movement in the discount rate can change its defined benefit obligation by more than RM1 billion. Maybank’s KAM similarly describes extensive audit procedures without showing investors the range of possible outcomes. The KAM explains the judgement, but not how sensitive the number may be. International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 701 requires auditors to communicate KAMs and allow them to highlight matters requiring significant auditor attention, while the opinion remains on the financial statements as a whole. But the framework is binary while uncertainty is not. Two competent valuers may reach different estimates, and a figure can be reasonable without being the only supportable answer. KAMs can therefore become lists of procedures rather than explanations of risk. Estimation uncertainty exists on a continuum while audit reporting remains categorical. The question is not whether KAMs should exist, but whether they tell investors enough about how uncertain the most consequential numbers really are. Malaysia’s Audit Oversight Board has identified “failure to sufficiently review significant risk areas and significant judgements” as a recurring enforcement concern. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) highlighted in its November 2025 statement the importance of high-quality valuation practices, appropriate use of valuation experts and rigorous audit assessment. The International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) has likewise identified accounting estimates, including fair value measurement, as an area where audit regulators have consistently found deficiencies. When auditors use KAMs to flag a valuation without qualifying the opinion, they are telling investors that the matter involved significant judgement but that the financial statements nevertheless met the requirements for an unmodified opinion. That may be technically correct for Maybank and TNB. But the Serba Dinamik case illustrates how insufficient that signal can be for investors. The concern is not simply whether auditors get the judgement wrong. Even a sound audit can leave investors unable to see how fragile a reasonable estimate may be. That is the gap the current reporting model should address. Four reforms would help. First, require sensitivity disclosure in the KAM. Auditors should disclose the reasonable range of outcomes and its impact on the financial statements. TNB’s statements already include sensitivity analysis on discount rate assumptions. This information should be connected directly to the KAM, rather than leaving investors to piece the implications together from different sections of the annual report. Second, consider graduated reporting for significant estimation uncertainty. Such reporting could signal that an estimate falls within an acceptable range but remains highly sensitive, without implying that there is a material misstatement. The existing Emphasis of Matter framework under ISA 706 could provide a starting point. Third, require independent valuation review for specified material Level 3 assets. A second valuation would provide an additional check on management bias. The auditor could assess the divergence as evidence and consider the additional data point when applying professional scepticism. Fourth, strengthen audit committee disclosure. Audit committees should disclose how they challenged management’s fair value assumptions. If the committee accepted management’s numbers without meaningful scrutiny, that should be visible to shareholders. None of these solutions are radical. Each builds on existing frameworks, including Malaysian Financial Reporting Standard 13 (MFRS 13), ISA 701, ISA 540 and Malaysia’s corporate governance code. They require recognition that the current approach to fair value auditing, while technically sound, is insufficiently transparent for the risks involved. Judgement is unavoidable. Opacity is not. body: '（巴生1日讯）班达马兰华小B校将于10月17日（星期六）晚上7时正，在该校冷气大礼堂举办“文艺·相聚·闪耀班B”文艺晚宴，吁请各界慷慨解囊共募学校发展经费。 大会主席兼董事会总务范忠星在新闻发布会指出，该校家教协会举办此项文艺晚宴是为了发扬中华文化、丰富校园人文气息，并为学生打造一个展现才华的广阔舞台。 他说，此项盛会不仅是孩子们展现艺术潜能的重要时刻，更是凝聚家长及各界热心华教力量、共谋学校未来发展的重要契机。 “本次晚宴的核心目的旨在筹募发展经费，其重点用途包括支持家教协会的日常运作、全力推动校内才艺与文艺发展、提升与翻修陈旧的校园设施，以及全面增设智慧黑板。” 他期望通过这一系列的软硬件升级，为莘莘学子营造一个更优质、更具科技感与人文气息的学习与成长环境。 筹委会主席兼家教协会主席林珮雯则呼吁社会贤达、家长及热心华教人士踊跃支持，共襄盛举。 她强调，班B华小一直以来获得各界热心华教人士与家长的鼎力支持。面对庞大的校园建设与活动发展开支，单凭学校现有资源难以尽善尽美，因此恳切期盼广大热心家长及社会贤达能慷慨解囊。 她说，筹委会特设多项赞助方案： 鸣锣贵宾：捐献1万2000令吉或以上（受邀为大会鸣锣贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席1桌）。 击鼓贵宾：捐献6000令吉 或以上（受邀为大会击鼓贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券5张）。 亮灯贵宾：捐献3000令吉 或以上（受邀为大会亮灯贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券2张）。 赞助贵宾：捐献 RM1,000 或以上（受邀为大会赞助贵宾，芳名刊登于征信录，并获赠宴席名誉券2张）；捐献500令吉或以上（获赠宴席名誉券1张）。 她说，大众也可选择捐购宴席每桌1500令吉，或随缘捐献。 有意赞助或购票的善长仁翁，款项可通过现金、支票或银行转账交至各班班主任或筹委会负责人处。 银行转账详情：银行名称：MAYBANK；户头名称：PIBG SJK(C）PANDAMARAN B PEL KLANG；户头号码：5124 5512 5645；备注（Reference）：SUMBANGAN 1017（银行转账资料请附上交予班主任或筹委会负责人）；支票抬头请写明：PIBG SJK(C）PANDAMARAN B PEL KLANG 任何垂询，欢迎联络家协主席林珮雯（电话号码：012-351 5115）、校长郑长杰（电话号码：012-2878738）、票务主任张绣琴（电话号码：016-227 2232）或家协财政纪惠霞（电话号码：016-712 2816）。

title: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances
body: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances (as at July 31, 2026) that Lee had injected into Shenton 101, the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. The final repayment sum will be determined on completion. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who turned down an earlier offer from Lee in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments following several asset acquisitions at the time. To manage potential conflicts of interest, IOI Properties had entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 acquired Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — via tender for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The vehicle secured S$376.23 million in bank borrowings to finance the acquisition, with the remainder of the purchase price, buyer's stamp duty (S$26.87 million), planning consultation fees and ongoing holding costs funded via interest-free advances from Lee. These existing bank borrowings will be consolidated into IOI Properties' accounts upon completion of the deal. No shareholder approval needed The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as its highest percentage ratio is 3.79% — below the 5% threshold under Bursa's listing rules. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on the request of Lee, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. Plans for a 35-storey mixed-use landmark The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Lee and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The deal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion.
