body: '债息升冲击本地金融业 马银行9个月首跌破10令吉 （吉隆坡1日讯）美国国债收益率持续走高，银行持有债券面对更大的账面亏损压力，加上融资成本可能上升，本地银行股今日普遍走低，马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主板金融股）更跌破10令吉大关，为近9个月来首次。 马银行连续三个交易日下跌，今日收市跌4仙或0.4%，报9令吉95仙；联昌国际（CIMB，1023，主板金融股）及丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819，主板金融股）则双双下跌逾1%。 涵盖保险公司及证券行等非银行金融企业的富时大马金融指数，也跌至10个月来最低水平。 艾芬黄氏投行指出，债券收益率走高通常会对银行造成压力，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，将导致较大的账面亏损，侵蚀资本；若银行出售有关债券，则必须确认相关亏损。 与此同时，银行也可能需要提高存款利率以吸引存户，进而推高融资成本。 该行今日发布的研究报告指出，这将对银行短期非利息收入及资本充足率造成压力。 美联储上个月上调利率，为3年来首次加息，带动10年期马来西亚政府证券（MGS）收益率一度升至4.18%，随后略为回落。 随着越来越多经济学家预期，国家银行可能在11月举行今年最后一次预定货币政策会议时上调隔夜政策利率（OPR），市场对利率走势的关注进一步升温。 艾芬黄氏投行表示，债券收益率走高通常也会推高企业债券收益率，并影响银行及其他企业的融资决策，进而影响银行所赚取的费用收入。 根据该投行分析，马银行及安联银行（ABMB，2488，主板金融股）的债券组合久期最长。债券久期除了代表债券通过现金流收回成本所需的时间，也反映债券对利率变化的敏感度。 相比之下，大众银行（PBBANK，1295，主板金融股）及丰隆银行的债券组合久期最短。 在资本适足率方面，艾芬投行认为，马银行、兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066，主板金融股）及联昌国际可能面对较大的资本比率跌幅；大众银行及丰隆银行由于债券组合久期较短，所受影响则相对较小。 The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Cover Story: How the AI tidal wave is reshaping the jobs market
body: 'This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 21, 2026 - September 27, 2026 FOR engineering outfit owner John, using artificial intelligence (AI) in his work has been a game changer. He “trains” the AI to write codes in the company’s style and now merely checks to ensure that the codes are written correctly. “I use AI to write more routine codes and it has helped me cut down coding time significantly, where a few days of work can be accomplished in 20 minutes. But I still need a few employees because engineers need to be at the physical location to make sure hardware is properly installed and conduct test runs,” he says. These days, the use of AI is prevalent in all aspects of life, in various sectors of the economy and professions, and more so among white-collar workers. Early research has shown that AI has, by some measure, improved the productivity of workers, but it still depends on the complexity of tasks and the user’s ability in AI prompting. Even so, AI is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. As a result, companies will soon be able to achieve the same outcomes with fewer workers — or, in some roles, none at all. The concern among white-collar workers about AI displacing jobs is real. Jobstreet’s Workplace Happiness Index found that while only around one-third of Malaysian workers feel “very” or “extremely” concerned about AI affecting their job security, the score is even higher among professional services workers, coming in at 47%. While there is no evidence of massive job loss as a result of AI at this juncture, recruitment agencies observe that job postings for certain roles have been declining. Jobstreet by SEEK in Malaysia managing director Nicholas Lam says AI is certainly putting pressure on some forms of white-collar work, particularly roles involving repetitive, standardised or administrative tasks, many of which are being automated. Current data points, however, more towards roles being redesigned than entire professions being replaced. “The clearest early signs of pressure are in selected content and administrative roles. Job ads for positions such as content writer, copywriter, secretary and graphic designer declined between 2024 and 1H2026. We see these trends as directional indicators that automation may be changing how these roles are structured, rather than proof of one-for-one job replacement,” Lam says. This observation is consistent with a May report by the International Labour Organization (ILO), which found that studies using job postings and online labour-platform data show a significant decline in demand for skills associated with routine writing and translation, following the diffusion of generative AI (GenAI) tools, alongside increased demand for AI-related skills such as machine learning and natural language processing. PwC Malaysia managing partner Soo Hoo Khoon Yean argues that the gradual redesign of work does not necessarily imply that workers will be displaced. Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. Read also: Cover Story: AI may boost productivity, but what about workers’ share? Instead, he says, it points to a gradual shift in the mix of capabilities and skills required in those roles. “There may be a growing divide between workers who are able to integrate AI into their workflows and adapt to evolving skill requirements, and those who are unable to,” Soo Hoo says. “As AI becomes more capable, competitive advantage will increasingly come from areas where human strengths like context, judgement and accountability matter most. This includes making high-stakes decisions, solving nuanced problems, managing stakeholder relationships, and bringing together insights from different disciplines to create solutions that AI alone cannot deliver.” Such expectations are starting to show up in the hiring landscape in Malaysia, with AI or digital tools becoming more common in the workplace. Randstad Malaysia associate director, emerging technology recruitment Dylan Long sees a clear shift in Malaysia’s hiring landscape, where employers are increasingly prioritising talent who are adept in AI and digital tools. “This trend is no longer confined to specialised tech departments; instead, having basic knowledge and practical experience with AI has rapidly evolved into a fundamental, baseline requirement for almost any professional role. There is an immense demand for individuals who demonstrate high digital agility,” Long says. He adds that a proactive willingness to embrace self-directed learning and integrate AI into one’s routine work has become a powerful, highly attractive differentiator in the current market. Statistics from Jobstreet confirm this change in the hiring landscape. According to Lam, the recruitment agency’s data shows that 70% of employers factor AI knowledge into hiring decisions, while one in three treat AI capability as a core hiring requirement. At the same time, demand for dedicated AI hiring is also increasing rapidly, notes Lam. AI-labelled job ads grew by 131% year on year in 2025. In 1H2026, the number of AI-labelled job ads was already 24% higher than the total for the whole of 2025, he says. One question that has often been raised is whether junior hiring will be reduced as a result of AI proliferation. A Gartner Inc survey carried out late last year found that 22% of chief human resources officers in the US reported that at least one business leader in their organisation has stopped hiring for entry-level roles as a result of AI automation. Some argue that removing the routine or repetitive tasks traditionally assigned to junior staff — often a training ground for developing judgement and gaining crucial experience — could ultimately hurt organisations by weakening their future talent pipeline. According to Soo Hoo, however, PwC’s global research shows that the bar is now higher for junior talent, with emotional quotient, judgement and leadership skills — qualities normally expected of senior hires — being prioritised. “Organisations will need to rethink how early-career talent is developed, including creating new pathways through which early-career employees can learn through application and experience,” he says. “Traditional apprenticeship models built largely around repetitive tasks may need to evolve into more structured experiences that accelerate the development of these broader capabilities.” Sufficient AI talent in Malaysia? While employers today want workers who can use AI in ways that help create value, there is also a need for AI developer roles in the country, notes Soo Hoo. “Malaysia needs to strengthen both the depth and breadth of its AI talent base. Findings from our 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer indicate that AI-related roles in Malaysia are currently concentrated in roles that apply AI in business functions (AI user roles) rather than roles focused on developing core AI technologies (AI developer roles),” he says. Soo Hoo cautions that the pipeline of specialised AI talent in Malaysia may not be sustainable for the country’s long-term ambitions, given the pace at which AI is evolving. “Malaysia needs both AI user and AI developer roles in our journey towards realising our AI Nation 2030 aspirations. We need to expand the pool of highly specialised engineers, data scientists and technical experts who can develop and commercialise homegrown digital innovation. At the same time, we must equip workers across sectors with AI literacy, applied skills and judgement to use these technologies productively and responsibly,” he explains. Having said that, every paradigm change will have its drawbacks. Human resources practitioners are reporting that, because of the speed at which the AI world is moving, employees are starting to experience AI fatigue, or “AI brain fry”, as they try to keep pace with the changes. “Companies need to think about the pace at which and direction in which they are adopting AI in their systems and processes. AI fatigue is a real issue and it’s not because employees are not eager to learn. This could result in a decrease, instead of an increase, in efficiency and productivity,” says an HR practitioner. A human resources director with a local company says some employees might not want to go down the AI rabbit hole. “We have reskilling programmes where we reassign certain affected roles to other areas in the company. But some of our employees, typically those who are closer to retirement, say they would rather opt for an early retirement plan, instead of reskilling,” notes the director. State of the labour market Minister of Economic Affairs Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said last Friday that a total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs from January to Sept 16, representing an increase of 15,196 over the same period last year. A recent report on the Social Security Organisation’s Employment Insurance Scheme (EIS) shows that professionals, managers, executives and technicians was the occupation category that saw the highest retrenchment rate, at 51% of the total loss of employment (LOE) benefit applications. It is not a new phenomenon, however, and has been in line with the data from 2021 to 2025. While some have attributed the higher retrenchment numbers partly to the increased adoption of AI or automation in companies, Maybank Investment Bank group chief economist Suhaimi Illias says it is still too early to determine the extent to which AI is driving retrenchments. He points out that Malaysia’s level of AI adoption, compared to other countries around the world, is still moderate. Citing the Microsoft AI Economy Institute’s Global AI Diffusion Scoring, he highlights that Malaysia ranked 51 out of 147 countries, with AI users accounting for 21.8% of the working-age population as at 1Q2026. Countries ranked among the top 20 have AI adoption rates ranging from more than 30% to 70%. “There are also other factors behind the higher share of skilled-worker retrenchments. Voluntary/Mutual Separation Schemes or Early Retirement Planning (VSS/MSS/ERP) have consistently ranked among the top three reasons for retrenchments and were the leading reason between 2023 and 2025. Higher-skilled employees may be more inclined to participate in such schemes, given attractive payouts,” Suhaimi says. He adds that the spike in total retrenchments may also reflect companies managing rising cost pressures through headcount reductions. This year, while the Consumer Price Index has remained moderate at 1.9% y-o-y in June, from 1.4% in February, the Producer Price Index has seen a spike to 9.2% y-o-y, from -3.4%, implying that companies have not passed down much of their higher cost to consumers so far. Interestingly, the country’s unemployment rate has held steady around 3% despite rising retrenchments. Suhaimi explains that because job placements continue to outpace layoffs, the economy is still net-positive for job creation. In 1H2026, placements reached 74,874, significantly higher than the 47,030 retrenchments. The way forward for employees With 620,000 jobs in Malaysia expected to be reshaped by AI, digitalisation and the green economy over the next three to five years, Jobstreet’s Lam warns that early-career professionals must learn to use these technologies both practically and responsibly. “AI literacy should increasingly be treated as a baseline capability,” he adds. Still, being literate in digital tools alone is not enough. Randstad’s Long points out the younger generation are naturally adept at using and eager to adopt new technology, but global employers still prefer “job-ready” candidates who have practical experience. “New graduates can prepare by actively seeking out structured internships, graduate trainee programmes, and on-the-job training opportunities that offer direct exposure to complex, real-world projects,” he says. “In fact, according to the Randstad 2026 Job Market Outlook and Salary Guide report, continuous learning has become such a non-negotiable for long-term career security that 56% of Gen Z talent in Malaysia would outright reject a job offer if it did not provide clear learning and development pathways to future-proof their skills.” Meanwhile, Long notes that mid- to late-career professionals must future-proof themselves by blending their vast experience with modern technological efficiency. Ultimately, Lam concludes, today’s workforce — regardless of seniority — should strive to work with AI while sharpening the human and commercial skills that technology cannot easily replicate. title: 'Trading Of MKH Shares To Be Suspended
body: 'Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd will proceed with the compulsory acquisition of the remaining shares in MKH Bhd after securing valid acceptances representing at least 90% of the offer shares under its unconditional mandatory takeover offer.  MKH said Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in its shares upon the expiry of five market days from the extended closing date of the offer.  MKH said it had received a press notice from Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, on behalf of Whitmore and its ultimate offeror Batu Kawan Bhd, confirming that the 90% threshold had been met as at 5pm on Sept 30, 2026.  Whitmore is offering RM2.00 cash per MKH share for all remaining voting shares not already owned by Whitmore and Batu Kawan.  Following the acceptance level, Whitmore and Batu Kawan will invoke subsection 222(1) of the Capital Markets and Services Act 2007 to compulsorily acquire the remaining shares from dissenting shareholders.  A compulsory acquisition notice will be issued to those shareholders within two months from Sept 30.  Following the suspension, Whitmore and Batu Kawan intend to procure MKH to take the necessary steps to withdraw its listing status from Bursa Malaysia’s Official List.  If the delisting is completed, MKH shares will no longer be traded on the Main Market.  The takeover offer will remain open for acceptance until 5pm on Oct 8, 2026.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia to suspend trading in MKH shares after takeover offer
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia will suspend the trading of MKH Bhd on the Main Market after five market days from the extended closing date of Batu Kawan Bhd’s unconditional mandatory takeover offer for the property developer. According to Maybank Investment Bank Bhd in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on behalf of Batu Kawan and MKH, the suspension follows the receipt of valid acceptances of not less than nine-tenths in the nominal value of the offer shares as at 5pm yesterday. title: 'Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card: Everything you need to know before applying
body: 'Maybank has officially introduced its limited edition Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card in Malaysia. With initial physical branch allocations selling out rapidly across the country, fans looking to secure the card should now stand by for the official Maybank2u online rollout on 28 September 2026. What is the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? The card is an exclusive limited edition Visa debit card released in collaboration with Visa for the BTS World Tour Arirang. It links directly to any existing or new Maybank current or savings account, including popular options like a standard Savings Account i. Maybank has capped total nationwide issuance to 200,000 cards. Following the instant sell out of physical branch quotas, remaining card stock will be made available strictly through online applications. Additional features compared to a standard Maybank debit card While core banking functions mirror standard Maybank debit cards, the BTS edition includes several exclusive perks and modern payment integrations. Cardholders can add the Maybank Visa BTS World Tour Arirang Debit Card to Apple Pay and Samsung Wallet. This allows users to make contactless mobile payments directly from an iPhone, Apple Watch, or compatible Samsung Galaxy device without needing the physical card on hand. Beyond mobile wallet support and limited edition artwork, getting the card grants an immediate advantage in Maybank and Visa’s official concert ticket giveaway. While standard debit cardholders must accumulate spending to qualify, obtaining this limited edition card automatically awards an entry into the prize draw. In terms of banking capabilities, the card operates on the Visa network with smart chip security, contactless highway toll support, and standard fee structures, including the standard RM12 replacement fee. How to win BTS World Tour Arirang concert tickets in Kuala Lumpur Maybank and Visa are running a contest from 23 September 2026 until 1 November 2026, offering cardholders a chance to win pairs of tickets to the BTS World Tour Arirang concert at National Stadium Bukit Jalil on 12 December 2026. To participate, cardholders must first register by sending an SMS with the word BTS to the number 66628, or register through the dedicated Maybank2u promotion page. Once registered, users can earn entries through multiple qualifying actions: - Automatic entry: Successfully applying for or replacing an existing card with the limited edition BTS debit card awards one automatic entry. - Cumulative spending: Every cumulative RM400 spent on eligible retail transactions using any Maybank Visa debit card during the campaign period earns one entry. - Additional spending: Every subsequent RM400 spent yields additional entries to boost winning chances. Transactions involving eWallet top ups, government payments, and charity donations are excluded from eligible spend. Winners will be selected through Maybank’s randomiser system, with each cardmember eligible to win a maximum of one pair of tickets. How to apply for the Maybank BTS World Tour Arirang debit card? With physical branch allocations fully exhausted, all remaining card requests must be submitted online when portal access opens on 28 September 2026. Existing Maybank customers Existing Maybank debit cardholders do not need to visit a branch or collect cards in person. You can request a card replacement online via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. To place an order, log in to Maybank2u on the web, navigate to Settings, select Cards, go to Manage Debit Cards, and click Replace or Renew Card. Select the BTS card, enter your mailing address, and confirm the request using Secure2u or SMS TAC. The card will be delivered directly to your home address for a standard RM12 replacement fee. Delivery times may exceed thirty days during periods of high demand. If card allocations run out completely before your request processes, Maybank will issue a full refund of the replacement fee. Non-Maybank customers If you do not currently hold a Maybank account, you cannot directly order a card replacement online as a first time applicant. New customers must first open an account with Maybank. You can set up an account online through the MAE app or visit any Maybank branch with your MyKad or passport and a standard RM250 deposit, or RM50 with an employment letter. Once your account is active and registered on Maybank2u, you can stand by to request the BTS debit card replacement via Maybank2u starting 28 September 2026. Transaction limits and security settings The card comes with a default daily purchase limit of RM3,000, which can be increased up to RM10,000 via Maybank2u or adjusted at any Maybank ATM. Each card carries a validity period of seven years from issuance. Cardholders planning to use the card for online shopping or overseas ATM cash withdrawals must manually activate ecommerce and overseas transaction features inside Maybank2u prior to making transactions.

title: 'Maybank Tamatkan Khidmat Buka Akaun SSPN Prime Di Kaunter – Mulai 1 Oktober Ini
body:
'

Maybank hari ini mengeluarkan notis rasmi memaklumkan bahawa perkhidmatan pembukaan akaun deposit Simpan SSPN Prime di kaunter cawangannya bakal ditamatkan secara rasmi berkuat kuasa pada 1 Oktober 2026.

Penamatan ini dilaksanakan berikutan keputusan Perbadanan Tabung Pendidikan Tinggi Nasional (PTPTN) dalam usaha menyusun semula saluran perkhidmatan mereka. Oleh itu, semua cawangan Maybank tidak lagi akan menerima sebarang permohonan fizikal bagi pembukaan akaun baharu SSPN Prime bermula dari tarikh berkenaan.

Bagi pelanggan yang berhasrat untuk membuka akaun baharu atau menguruskan simpanan SSPN Prime, Maybank menasihatkan awam agar beralih kepada saluran dan platform rasmi yang telah disediakan oleh pihak PTPTN. Pembukaan akaun kini boleh dilakukan dengan lebih pantas dan mudah secara dalam talian menerusi aplikasi myPTPTN atau portal rasmi PTPTN, tanpa perlu hadir secara fizikal ke mana-mana kaunter bank ejen. Untuk sebarang pertanyaan atau maklumat lanjut mengenai produk, syarat-syarat simpanan, serta perkhidmatan berkaitan SSPN Prime, pelanggan boleh menghubungi talian khidmat pelanggan PTPTN atau melayari terus saluran maklumat rasmi mereka.

title: 'Maybank Championship makes stellar return, returns with prize bonanza
body: 'THE Maybank Championship is set for another star-studded chapter when Asia’s premier ladies’ golf event returns to Kuala Lumpur Golf & Country Club (KLGCC) from Oct 29 to Nov 1. With a $3 million (RM12.3m) prize purse, the fourth edition brings together Major champions, LPGA Tour winners and Southeast Asia’s emerging talents for four days of world-class competition at KLGCC. The competition for the coveted Tiger Trophy has never been more intense. Defending champion and Major winner Miyu Yamashita of Japan is one of the most in-form players this season, highlighted by a dominant nine-stroke victory at the CPKC Women’s Open in Canada in August, and a playoff win at the Sony JLPGA Championship in Japan in September. Having claimed a dramatic three-way playoff victory at last year’s Maybank Championship, she will have every intention of becoming the tournament’s first repeat champion. Crowd favourite and World No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand is also on a rich vein of form, having already claimed three LPGA Tour victories in 2026 to take her total title tally to ten. She returns for a fourth consecutive year in pursuit of the elusive Tiger Trophy, having narrowly missed out in each of her last appearances. Thitikul’s close friend Ruoning Yin of China, the 2024 Maybank Championship winner and a Major champion, will also return to Malaysia in winning mode having triumphed at the FM Championship in August. The spotlight will also firmly be turned on Korean ace Haeran Ryu, who is currently second on the LPGA Tour’s Race to CME Globe ranking on the back of successive Major victories in 2026 at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and the Amundi Evian Championship. Adding her considerable star power to the field is the perennially popular New Zealander Lydia Ko, a three-time Major winner and reigning Olympic champion who was inducted into the LPGA Hall of Fame in 2024 at age 27. Australian stalwart Hannah Green and Hye-Jin Choi of South Korea, who were the two other protagonists in last year’s playoff, will return with unfinished business on their agendas. The 2023 Maybank Championship winner Céline Boutier of France, who edged Thitikul in a nail-biting nine-hole playoff at KLGCC three years ago, is also in the field. Other fan favourites who have signed up include emerging English sensation Lottie Woad and her experienced compatriot Charley Hull, and Japanese twins Aki and Chizzy Iwai. The Maybank Championship is more than Asia’s premier golf event. It provides a distinctive regional pathway for Southeast Asian talent to earn their place alongside the world’s best. This year, five players who earned their places through the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier bring that story to life. Standout Thai amateur Marisa Tojai, who had already claimed four amateur titles in 2026 before arriving at the qualifier, secured the fourth spot at two-under 142, while Malaysia’s Liyana Durisic rounded out the top five at one-under 143. Through this performance-based pathway, each of these five players earned the right to play alongside the world’s best in a full-fledged LPGA Tour event, which is the primary objective of the Maybank Championship Asean Qualifier. For Malaysian fans, there will be plenty to roar about. Liyana Durisic is currently in great form, having already claimed four PGM Tour titles in 2026, and the Women’s World Sand Greens Championship held in Australia in March. She will be joined by a talented and recognizable group of Malaysian players entering as Sponsor’s Invitations, namely Mirabel Ting, Jeneath Wong, Natasha Oon and Kelly Tan, to make up a five-strong Malaysian challenge. 2025 Annika Award winner Mirabel Ting made headlines in 2024 by becoming the highest-finishing Malaysian in Maybank Championship history, with a T12 finish as an amateur. Her fine performances continued into her debut season on this year’s Epson Tour, helping her clinch two victories in 2026. The wins propelled Ting to the top of the Epson Tour’s Race for the Card standings and secured her place on the LPGA Tour for the 2027 season. Joining Ting is Malaysia’s highest-ranked amateur (currently ranked 59th), Jeneath Wong. After a stellar season in 2023 that saw her earn her a major championship start at the US Women’s Open, Wong made history as the first Malaysian to win the Women’s Amateur Asia-Pacific Championship in 2025. The victory earned her further major championship starts, bringing an increasingly impressive international resume to KLGCC. One-time Epson Tour winner and 2023 Epson Tour Rookie of the Year Natasha Oon makes her first appearance at the Maybank Championship since 2023, seeking to capitalize on her encouraging performance at the recent CPKC Women’s Open. The LPGA Tour rookie is rebuilding her momentum following a lengthy injury that saw her miss most of the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Completing the Malaysian line-up is two-time Olympian Kelly Tan, Malaysia’s most successful LPGA Tour player. Tan recorded her career-best results on the LPGA Tour with runner-up finishes at the Dow Great Lakes Bay Invitational in 2022 and 2023, and returns to KLGCC for the third time, bringing over a decade of elite professional experience and an intimate knowledge of the West Course. The Maybank Championship reflects Maybank’s belief in Harnessing Collective Power, bringing together world-class players, emerging ASEAN talent, partners and fans to elevate the game and create opportunity across the region.

title: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser
body: 'Sabah Energy Corp raises RM350 mil in maiden sukuk, Maybank IB appointed as adviser KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 17): Sabah Energy Corporation Sdn Bhd (SEC) has raised RM350 million through its maiden sukuk issuance under a RM3 billion sukuk wakalah programme. The issuance was announced in a joint statement with Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK). The sukuk was rated AAA with a stable outlook by RAM Rating Services Bhd and was priced through book-building, with demand reaching 2.2 times the amount offered. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd was appointed as the sole principal adviser, lead arranger, lead manager and sustainability structure adviser, as well as shariah adviser and facility agent. “This landmark issuance broadens and diversifies SEC's access to long-term ringgit funding while raising the profile of both SEC and Sabah among domestic and international institutional investors. The strong over-subscription reflects investors' confidence in SEC's credit strength and growth trajectory," said Maybank IB chief executive officer Michael Oh-Lau. Maybank said the issuance gives the Sabah state-owned energy company a longer-term funding source as it plans investments across its energy businesses, including natural gas infrastructure, power generation and renewable energy. SEC said the funding platform will support its strategic roadmap called PETA (Pelan Strategik dan Hala Tuju) 2030, which covers the expansion of its gas and infrastructure operations, power generation and renewable energy activities, as well as investments across Sabah's energy value chain. “In turn, this supports the broader outcomes envisaged under SERAMP 2040: stronger energy security, a faster energy transition and more reliable supply for Sabah," said SEC group chief executive officer Datuk Adzmir Abd Rahman. SEC has been Sabah's sole natural gas aggregator, transporter and distributor since its corporatisation in 1997. It has since expanded into power generation, renewable energy and offshore oil and gas support services. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. title: 'Maybank, Asian Banking School Explore Certification Programme For Wealth Advisory
body: 'Maybank and the Asian Banking School (ABS) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to explore the development of a professional certification framework for wealth advisory in Malaysia, aimed at introducing an industry-recognised benchmark for advisory capability.  The proposed certification framework, to be known as the ABS Wealth Advisory & Management Certification Programme, is intended to establish competency standards specifically for wealth advisory professionals in banking. Upon its launch, it will be Malaysia’s first industry-wide professional certification framework dedicated to wealth advisory.  The parties noted that as wealth management needs grow more complex, clients increasingly require advice that connects different aspects of their financial lives. This initiative they added aims to establish a consistent benchmark for the advisory capabilities required to serve clients holistically.  Maybank will serve as the Founding Industry Partner, contributing insights and its experience in developing wealth talent, while ABS will bring its expertise in professional banking development and certification. ABS will retain independence over the standards and how they are assessed and certified.  “This collaboration with the Asian Banking School allows us to contribute that experience beyond our organisation, to raise professional standards for wealth advisory in Malaysia, with the opportunity to extend elements of the programme across the region over time,” said Syed Ahmad Taufik Albar, Group CEO, Community Financial Services, Maybank.  The programme’s first intake is expected in the second half of 2027, and Maybank intends to incorporate the programme into Maybank Wealth Academy, connecting it with structured learning and career development through practical workplace application. The parties will also explore opportunities to extend relevant certification pathways to wealth professionals across the region.

title: '2026 Mazda CX-5 – third-gen secures over 600 bookings before launch; Maybank reports circa RM160k price tag
body: 'According to a market insight report by Maybank Investment Bank, Bermaz Auto has secured over 600 bookings for the third-generation Mazda CX-5 ahead of the SUV’s launch on October 8 this year. Bermaz Motor, the official distributor of Mazda vehicles here, previously said the latest CX-5 will initially arrive as a fully-imported (CBU) model before local assembly (CKD) starts “about 12-16 months” later. Estimated pricing for the SUV is said to be from RM170k. In its report, the investment back states that CKD production of the CX-5 will start in mid-2027, with pricing below said estimate at circa RM160k. The report also revealed a new B-segment SUV arriving in either 2027 or 2028, likely priced at around RM120k. This likely points towards the second-generation CX-3, which was confirmed by Mazda last month. As per the Japanese carmaker’s mid-year financial report, the next generation of the CX-3 will be introduced in phases in ASEAN, Japan and other markets from 2027, with Thailand being the production base for the model. Both the current CX-3 and Mazda 2 – the latter sharing the same underlying vehicle platform – have already been dropped from Bermaz Motor’s line-up.

title: 'HE Group berpeluang tambah lagi kontrak baharu capai sasaran RM350 juta pada FY26 – Maybank IB | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 14 Sept — HE Group Berhad berpeluang menambah lagi kontrak baharu bagi mencapai sasaran pengisian semula buku tempahan sebanyak RM350 juta pada tahun kewangan 2026. Menurut Maybank Investment Bank (Maybank IB), setakat ini ia meraih kontrak bernilai RM293 juta, atau 84% daripada sasaran ditetapkan bagi FY26, dan mencerminkan momentum kerja yang sihat. Perkembangan terbaharu ialah kontrak bernilai RM25 juta daripada pengeluar berkaitan semikonduktor bagi melaksanakan kerja pengagihan tenaga, dan memberikan keterlihatan hasil hingga tempoh 1HFY27. "Kami menganggarkan kontrak ini mampu menjana RM2 juta kepada keuntungan bersih HE Group sepanjang tempoh pelaksanaan, berdasarkan andaian margin 8% bagi projek berkaitan," jelas firma tersebut. Dengan buku tempahan sekitar RM317 juta, atau 2.6 kali ganda hasil bagi FY25, Maybank IB melihat kedudukan kontrak kumpulan itu memberikan sokongan terhadap keterlihatan pendapatan yang stabil. Namun, momentum pengisian semula perlu diteruskan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan kekal mampan, dengan kumpulan itu ada buku tender bernilai RM1.3 bilion sebagai sumber potensi kontrak baharu. Kira-kira 80% terdiri projek pusat data (DC), yang dijangka menjadi pemacu penting pertumbuhan HE Group, terutamanya dalam segmen pembinaan serta kejuruteraan mekanikal dan elektrikal (M&E). "Kami menjangka momentum perolehan kerja baharu terus kukuh pada suku keempat 2026, disokong buku tender yang besar, dengan projek DC berpotensi memberi sumbangan kepada operasi," kata Maybank IB. Firma penyelidikan itu turut mengekalkan sasaran pengisian semula kontrak kumpulan pada RM350 juta bagi FY26 dan RM250 juta masing-masing bagi FY27 dan FY28, selain mengekalkan semua unjuran hasil. Sehubungan itu, bersandarkan potensi positif tersebut, ia tidak mengubah saranan 'pegang' terhadap saham kumpulan berkenaan dengan harga sasaran (TP) juga masih kagi kekal kepada 96 sen sesaham. Penilaian ini berdasarkan gandaan harga kepada pendapatan (P/E) 18 kali terhadap unjuran hasil sesaham (EPS) FY27, iaitu dua sisihan piawai melebihi purata syarikat setara sektor M&E.

title: 'Maybank to acquire rest of Maybank Ageas for RM4.83 billion
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has entered into an unconditional share purchase agreement (SPA) with Belgium-based Ageas Insurance International NV to acquire the remaining 30.95% equity interest in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd (MAHB) for RM4.83 billion. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Maybank said the agreement involves acquiring 78 million MAHB shares from Ageas. The banking group said it signed the SPA today after receiving approval from Bank Negara Malaysia on Sept 1 and that the purchase consideration will be funded entirely through internally generated funds. Maybank said the proposed acquisition is intended to enable it to wholly own MAHB and provide the group with greater strategic flexibility. “The acquisition is also aimed at strengthening MAHB’s position as a national insurance and takaful player, supporting expansion across Southeast Asia, enhancing sustainable and resilient long-term value for the Maybank group, and improving capital management efficiency across its insurance and takaful franchises. “Full ownership of MAHB is expected to provide both Maybank and MAHB with greater strategic agility to accelerate product innovation, deepen bancassurance penetration, expand takaful propositions, and enhance capital and operational efficiency across the insurance and takaful franchises,” it said. Barring unforeseen circumstances, Maybank said that the proposed acquisition is expected to be completed on Sept 11. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd has been appointed as the principal adviser, while Morgan Stanley Asia (Singapore) Pte has been appointed as its international financial adviser.

title: 'Maybank Matches Up To RM250 In ASNB Units
body: '7th September 2026 - 3 min read Maybank and Amanah Saham Nasional Berhad (ASNB) are running the ASNB Invest & Win Campaign 2026, letting eligible customers who invest in ASNB funds stand a chance to win ASNB units worth up to RM250. The campaign runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, split into five monthly phases. To earn an entry, you’ll need to make at least two ASNB investments, in any fund, within the same phase. There’s no cap on the number of entries you can earn. To stand a chance at the full RM250, your total investment within that phase needs to reach at least RM250. If your total is lower, the prize you could win matches that lower amount instead. Each phase draws 148 winners, adding up to 740 across the whole campaign. Each customer can only win once during the entire campaign period, even if they qualify for multiple entries. Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) units, or ASB 2 or ASB 3 Didik units if their ASB limit has been reached. Non-Bumiputera winners receive Amanah Saham Nasional Equity 5 or Amanah Saham Nasional Sukuk units, depending on fund availability. If a winner has reached the investment limit across all applicable funds, they’ll receive cashback of the same value instead.
